description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

userStories.title: Category rubric activation was never filed — 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and nothing ever writes them
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the non-clothing grading scaffolding either finished or removed, because right now it is neither. Migration 00231 added grade_reports.factor_scores (jsonb) and rubric_key (text) to production, and the grading pipeline writes only the five TYPED clothing columns (fabric_condition_score … odor_cleanliness_score) — verified: the grade_reports insert in grading-pipeline.ts reads compositeResult.factor_scores.* into those five columns and never sets factor_scores or rubric_key. So both columns are permanently NULL on every row in prod. The edge module services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts is imported by nothing. Its client counterpart src/lib/rubrics.ts IS live — certificate.tsx:39 imports rubricForKey — so the certificate page is ready to render a rubric that the server will never populate. The only record of intent is commit bbd94005 'feat(grading): category rubric foundation (non-clothing scaffolding)', which says the work is 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline' and that the activation follow-up 'is documented in rubric.ts'. That follow-up was never filed as a story, so it has been invisible to the backlog ever since.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE FIRST: activate or remove. Non-clothing grading (sports cards etc.) is a product question, not a cleanup — do not default to whichever is less work

If ACTIVATING: the pipeline writes rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing categories; the five typed clothing columns keep their current meaning for clothing; the public cert endpoint's CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS allowlist is extended deliberately (00231's own comment defers that exposure to 'the activation phase')

If REMOVING: rubric.ts is deleted, src/lib/rubrics.ts and its certificate.tsx usage are resolved, and a migration drops the two dead columns — do NOT leave them NULL-forever with no owner, which is the state this story exists to end

Either way a drift guard: services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts and src/lib/rubrics.ts are declared to stay in sync and NOTHING pins them today. If both survive, add a shared behavioural fixture asserted by both suites (the same remedy US-1995 asks for on title-sync)
The decision is written into the story notes so the next reader does not have to re-derive it from a commit message
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Cleanup] Found 2026-07-18 by scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs — rubric.ts was one of 10 whole modules nothing imports. ⚠ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM in this session's audit triage (US-1996 notes): the triage said 'exhaustive queries return no story mentioning rubric'. That is wrong — NINE stories mention it (US-1030, US-1031, US-1532, US-1534, US-1682, US-1948, US-1951 archived, plus US-1995/1996). I read each: they all use 'rubric' in the generic grading-criteria sense (wrinkle anchors, fabric-aware criteria, pSEO guides, homepage copy). None owns the CATEGORY-rubric activation this story covers. The conclusion stood; the stated evidence did not, which is why it is restated correctly here. P3 rather than P1 because there is no user-visible breakage: clothing grading is unaffected and the certificate simply never renders a rubric block. The cost is a permanently-NULL pair of prod columns, a dead edge module, and a live client module waiting on data that never arrives. | 2026-07-23 DECISION: ACTIVATE (owner, via AskUserQuestion) — non-clothing grading (sports cards / watches / shoes) is on the roadmap, so the scaffolding is kept and built out, not removed. Activation is a MULTI-PHASE program, not a single commit; this session landed the two pieces that are safe and completable in a sandbox and scoped the rest with a plan. REFRAME (important for the next reader): the columns are 'permanently NULL' NOT because clothing forgot to write them but BY DESIGN — clothing renders from the 5 typed columns; factor_scores/rubric_key exist to hold NON-CLOTHING scores, which don't exist until the grading pipeline actually grades non-clothing. Backfilling clothing INTO factor_scores would be redundant AND stale-prone (the human-review reseal + adjustment write paths at grading-pipeline.ts:570/813/965 update only the typed columns), so it was deliberately NOT done. DONE THIS SESSION: (AC4 drift guard) added src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json — the SHARED behavioural fixture (same remedy US-1995 used for title-sync) constraining key+label+weight; both suites assert against it — client src/lib/__tests__/rubrics.test.ts (10/10 GREEN in-sandbox) and edge services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts (mirrors it; not deno-run here). Verified edge rubric.ts and client rubrics.ts already match exactly across all 4 rubrics, so the guard pins them without a reconciliation. (AC2 partial) extended CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS (content-public.ts) to expose factor_scores + rubric_key in the null-safe EXTRA set, so a non-clothing cert will serve its rubric once Phase 2 writes it; NULL clothing certs are unaffected (client already prefers them only when both present, else falls back to typed columns) and the 42703 genesis-fallback still protects clothing certs under 00231 drift. Verified web tsc -b + eslint clean; no test pins the CERT column string. REMAINING (Phase 2 — the actual non-clothing grading; CANNOT be done in this sandbox, needs a validatable env with deno + live traffic + real vision calls): (1) de-gate submissions.garment_type NOT NULL for non-clothing (rubric.ts checklist #1); (2) generalize the THREE lockstep rounding sites (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) from the hardcoded 5 clothing factors to variable rubric-driven factor sets, same commit; (3) build per-category composite prompts from rubric.factors/promptGuidance and route defects via rubric.defectRouting; (4) run those NEW prompts through the mandated prompt lifecycle — shadow-compare (grading-shadow.ts) -> golden-set eval gate (grading-eval.ts) -> canary — which REQUIRES a non-clothing golden set that does NOT yet exist (golden cases grow from real human-corrected grades, so Phase 2 needs a bootstrap: grade some non-clothing behind a flag, collect expert corrections, THEN gate); (5) persist rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing across ALL grade_reports write paths (insert + reseal + adjustment) to avoid the stale-JSONB bug above. KEPT passes:false: AC2 (non-clothing writes) + AC4-is-done-but-story-spans-more; the product feature is not live until Phase 2 ships through the eval gate. AC1/AC5 (decision documented) satisfied here. | 2026-08-08 AC4 now VERIFIED BY RUNNING, not by inspection: the previous session wrote the edge half of the drift guard but recorded it as 'mirrors it; not deno-run here'. Ran it — services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts: 53 passed, 0 failed. So both halves of the shared fixture (client 10/10, edge 53/53) are green against the same src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json, and AC4 is closed on evidence. Story stays passes:false on AC2 (Phase 2 non-clothing writes) only.

userStories.notes: [P2][EXTENSION][NEW][GROWTH] Privacy policy page (Model A static route). Attribution reuses affiliate.ts click->conversion. Telemetry opt-in only (GDPR/CCPA posture, ties to legal geo-consent epic). [OPERATOR-GATED 2026-07-09] Core deliverable (AC1: publish to Chrome Web Store + Firefox AMO with screenshots/listing copy) is NOT automatable from this host — needs store developer accounts + a running browser to capture screenshots. AC3 attribution: the referral system (src/lib/affiliate.ts) attributes via a per-SELLER ?ref=<code>; a buyer-side extension has no seller code, so extension->signup is channel-level (utm_source=extension), not per-referrer. Deferred until an operator runs the store submission; codeable residue to pair with that: extension privacy-policy static page, opt-in telemetry toggle + endpoint, store-listing copy doc. Not marking passes; mirrors the US-1582 [OPERATOR] split. Extension CODE is done via US-1755/US-1756. | 2026-07-18 AC1 PRIVACY-POLICY HALF DONE. Found a genuine store-submission blocker: /privacy is live and returns 200, but it did NOT mention the extension anywhere — while extension-unified/SUBMISSION.md instructs the operator to submit that exact URL to the Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO, both of which require the submitted policy to disclose the extension’s data use. A reviewer following our own submission doc would have landed on a policy silent about the product being reviewed. Added section 6, The GradeThread browser extension, covering: what a condition read sends (public photo URLs + title/brand/price on user action, reading the page you are already on, never browsing on your behalf); that diagnostics are OFF BY DEFAULT and carry no listing, page address, account or install identifier (the selector-health telemetry I added this session under US-1880 AC3 — the policy now matches the code); that seller cross-posting runs in the user’s own tab and marketplace passwords/cookies are never sent; and the gradethread.com message relay. Every claim is checked against the shipped code rather than the marketing copy. Renumbered sections 7-14 and fixed the one Section-N cross-reference. New privacy-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures so they cannot silently vanish, INCLUDING a sequential-numbering assertion and a cross-reference integrity check — I got the numbering wrong by hand while inserting the section, so the test encodes the mistake I actually made. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. REMAINING on this story is operator-gated exactly as the notes say: store submission needs developer accounts + a browser for screenshots (AC1), AC2 usage telemetry (reads/click-throughs) is distinct from the selector-failure telemetry already shipped though it can reuse the same consent toggle, and AC3 attribution is channel-level utm_source=extension. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) SECOND, WORSE GAP OF THE SAME CLASS — the AUP. extension-unified/popup.js:84 points the consent clickwrap’s "Read the terms" link at /acceptable-use, next to a checkbox reading "I understand the Lister fills forms in MY browser session and that I am responsible for each marketplace’s Terms of Service." That page is live (200) and mentioned "extension" 0 times, "cross-post" 0, "cross-list" 0, "Lister" 0 — a consent gate whose linked terms never described the thing being consented to. Worse than the privacy gap because this one IS the legal basis for the seller automation (the versioned, revocable clickwrap US-1885 AC3 built). Added section 6, The browser extension and assisted cross-posting: the automation runs in the user’s own logged-in session and we never receive marketplace passwords or cookies (so responsibility sits with them); some marketplaces restrict or prohibit assisted listing and their rules take precedence; review before publishing; no evading listing caps, rate limits, suspensions or bans; no operating others’ accounts. Renumbered 7-9 and cross-linked to Privacy section 6. New acceptable-use-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures + sequential numbering, and — the important one — READS extension-unified/popup.js to assert the termsLink still points at /acceptable-use, so repointing the popup fails the build instead of silently orphaning the clickwrap again. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) Swept the rest of the extension’s outbound references — all clean. Every gradethread.com URL the extension sends a user to (/, /acceptable-use, /connect-extension, /pricing, /privacy, /extension/marketplace-selectors.json) returns 200 live, so the two gaps found today were about CONTENT, not dead links. Extended the same cross-artifact check to CLAUDE.md and added a durable guard: scripts/doc-refs.mjs + doc-refs.test.mjs, wired into verify:web beside prd-lint. CLAUDE.md currently cites 29 paths, 0 missing. Two of my own bugs are pinned as regression cases: (1) an alternation-ordering bug — ts listed before tsx matched the head of a .tsx path and reported four files missing that exist, the same mistake as COMPLETED? failing to match COMPLETION in the prd-lint guard; (2) contextual roots — CLAUDE.md legitimately writes lib/supabase.ts inside a paragraph about the edge service, so the checker resolves against known roots the way a reader does rather than flagging correct prose. userStories.title: EPIC: Buyer Platform — buyer accounts, subscription, and the confidence layer
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to extend the seller-focused product into a two-sided buyer/seller platform whose sole purpose is increasing confidence in item listings, so that buyers pay a recurring subscription for point-of-purchase confidence AND their demand for graded items pulls more sellers into paying for grading (a two-sided flywheel).
acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can sign up, create a buyer profile, and subscribe to a buyer plan independent of any seller/FlipDesk plan, on the existing Supabase-auth + Stripe stack

The buyer subscription (Free / Guard / Connoisseur) gates a coherent suite of confidence features: extension second-opinion + discrepancy + price-fairness, condition-based alerts, fit, authenticity/video credits, grade-confirmation rewards, buyer trust score, insured grade-locked guarantee, wardrobe portfolio, and the graded-wanted board

Every buyer feature reuses (does not duplicate) an existing capability where one exists — extension US-1753, fit US-1776/1777, authenticity US-1767, video US-1762, circularity US-1785, What's-It-Worth US-1750, badges US-1758, Value Index US-1745, buyer guarantee US-867/guarantee_remedies — and is bound to the buyer entitlement layer
This umbrella tracks the US-1795…US-1847 buyer-platform backlog and its cross-cutting decisions (entitlements, tenant isolation, PII/consent, analytics)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][EPIC][NEW] BASELINE: buyers today are non-account holders reached only via public certificate/verify/guarantee/passport pages; there is NO buyer account, buyer profile, or buyer subscription. STRATEGY: the unique asset is objective per-item condition data + the grade_outcomes dataset (condition->realized price); the buyer product monetizes 'claimed condition vs objective condition, at the point of purchase'. TIERS (confirmed): Free / Guard (~$8/mo) / Connoisseur (~$19/mo). FLYWHEEL: buyer demand for graded items -> sellers must grade to sell -> more graded inventory -> better buyer product. TIES: reuses capability EPICs US-1745/1750/1753/1758/1762/1767/1776/1785 + buyer guarantee US-867. SEQUENCING: foundation (US-1795 sub-epic) ships first; idea sub-epics (US-1805+) depend on it. userStories.title: EPIC: Unified GradeThread extension — one install, role- and subscription-aware (buyer research for everyone, seller tools on top)

acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella/epic story — child stories US-1873..US-1885 implement it; it ships no code itself

Target architecture: a single extension folder (merge extension/ + extension-condition/) with one manifest carrying both permission sets (marketplace host_permissions + gradethread.com), a shared background service worker, and a feature registry that exposes: condition-read overlay = always on (anonymous allowed, quota-capped), Lister cross-post/delist = only when authenticated with seller entitlements

Auth/entitlements reuse the signed extension token planned in US-1838 (buyer-subscription gating), extended to carry seller role + FlipDesk plan so one token answers both 'can this install cross-post' and 'what buyer quota applies'

Privacy posture is re-documented for the merged permission set (the old 'not host-permitted on gradethread.com' Lister claim no longer holds once merged — the privacy story becomes 'no cookies permission, no marketplace credential access, marketplace automation stays on-device') and store listing copy/privacy policy are rewritten accordingly (feeds US-1757)

userStories.notes: Origin: 2026-07-09 extension deep-dive (3-agent audit of extension/, extension-condition/, and server integration). Related open stories NOT duplicated here: US-1833..1846 (buyer confidence suite + gating + legal), US-1757 (store distribution), US-1808 (extension-fed ingestion). Audit found the Lister privacy-by-manifest posture genuinely enforced today — the merge deliberately trades that isolation for one-install UX, so the privacy copy rewrite is mandatory, not cosmetic. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC4's STORE-KIT half done. New extension-unified/test/submission-kit.test.cjs guards all of it (version match + only-that-version; every permission justified — 'alarms' shipped unjustified for 4 days until caught by hand, and that is a store rejection; every host justified; the bridge disclosed whenever the manifest injects it). STILL OPEN: AC1 is umbrella-only (ships no code); AC5 needs the legacy extension/ + extension-condition/ folders removed once the unified reaches parity (US-1757 distribution targets unified only); children US-1880/1881/1882/1883/1884/1885 still open, and US-1873 is now VERIFIED COMPLETE.

userStories.title: Research surface: verify the five unverified adapters, fix the dead Poshmark upgrade rule, close intl host gaps, add selector-failure ping
userStories.description: As a shopper on any supported marketplace, I want the condition read to actually work there. Audit: 5 of 6 adapters are verified:false; the Poshmark image URL-upgrade regex ('/s_[a-z0-9]+/') requires a path-segment form that real CloudFront URLs don't use, so thumbnails get graded (selectors.js:71); manifest match gaps — eBay only 5 TLDs (missing fr/it/es/at/ch/ie/nl/pl/be), Vinted missing ~12 TLDs and matches are www-only while adapters accept apex, poshmark.ca subdomains unmatched; the 'corrected from telemetry' claim has no telemetry anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of Poshmark/Grailed/Mercari/Depop/Vinted verified against the live site: gallery/title/brand selectors + URL-upgrade rule produce full-res images on a real listing; verified:true + lastVerified set in BOTH config files (Poshmark's upgrade rule fixed to the filename form with a test using a real URL shape)

Manifest + adapter hosts cover the agreed international footprint (at minimum: eBay fr/it/es/ie/nl/at/ch/pl/befr-benl, all active Vinted TLDs incl. apex domains, *.poshmark.ca) — one list, generated or guard-tested against the adapter hosts so manifest and config can't drift

An anonymous, opt-in-gated selector-failure ping (adapter key + which selector list came up empty + config version, NO listing URL/user data) posts to a lightweight edge endpoint so broken adapters are discovered from telemetry as the README claims — consent + toggle shared with US-1757's telemetry story
srcset parsing picks the max-width candidate instead of assuming last-is-largest
Unknown/failed adapters keep degrading to the honest 'couldn't read the photos' state
userStories.notes:
Audit findings 4/6/15/26. The telemetry AC deliberately reuses US-1757's opt-in consent — don't build a second consent surface.

PARTIAL 2026-07-13 (agent loop — doable slices; story stays passes:false). DONE: (AC1 regex portion) fixed the dead Poshmark URL-upgrade rule — was /s_[a-z0-9]+/ (path-segment form real CloudFront URLs never have, so thumbnails got graded); now /(?:s|m|t)_(?=[^/]*$) matching the filename size-prefix, with a real-URL-shape test. (AC2) added intl hosts to the ebay adapter (fr/it/es/ie/nl/at/ch/pl/be) and vinted (be/at/ro/hu/sk/pt/se/lu/hr/gr/dk/fi) in BOTH config files; rewrote manifest content_scripts matches to canonical https://*.<host><path>* (the *. form covers apex+www+country subdomains, fixing the www-only + *.poshmark.ca gaps); new test/manifest-hosts.test.cjs derives the match set from adapters and fails on any drift (proven to catch missing+orphan). (AC4) srcsetLargest() picks the max-width candidate (was last-token) — wired into marketplace.js firstSrcFromAttr, unit-tested incl. comma-in-URL. (AC5) honest degrade unchanged/preserved. Config version bumped 2026.07.4->2026.07.5 in both files (lastVerified left 2026-07-10 — NOT live-reverified). NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC1 verified:true requires live-site QA of all 5 adapters (cannot do autonomously — verified flags left false); AC3 anonymous selector-failure edge ping needs a new endpoint + the shared opt-in consent from US-1757. Verified: node scripts/test-extensions.mjs green (3 files), node --check, both JSON valid, drift-guard negative checks. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). AC3 DONE: the anonymous selector-failure ping exists end-to-end. Migration 00475_selector_health_pings.sql (operator table, deny-all RLS, registered in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY) + POST /api/grading/public/selector-health in public-grading.ts + a popup opt-in toggle + the content-script report. ⚠ CONSENT DECISION MADE, NOT CONFIRMED BY THE USER: the AC says reuse US-1757's opt-in consent, but NO telemetry consent exists anywhere in the repo — the only consent surface is the Lister ToS clickwrap (tosAcceptedAt), which is legal acceptance for automating a seller's marketplace account and only renders behind caps.sellerEnabled. Gating on it would have collected nothing from anonymous research users, who are the entire population that hits a broken adapter. So this reuses the PATTERN (versioned/revocable key, renderConsent/wireConsent shape) under a separate selectorTelemetry storage key, default OFF, revoke deletes the key rather than storing false. Revisit if US-1757 meant something else. PRIVACY IS SERVER-ENFORCED, not client-trusted (the extension is user-modifiable): the endpoint takes a CLOSED vocabulary — 6 known adapter keys, 6 known selector-list names, version strings capped at 32 chars and charset-limited to [w.-] — so a URL cannot be smuggled through the adapter field, the selector array, or a version string; there is deliberately no free-text column to put one in. Tested as hostile-client cases in selector-health_test.ts (9 tests), and the adapter allowlist is DERIVED from marketplace-selectors.json so a new adapter whose telemetry would be silently dropped fails the test (negative-verified with a planted 'etsy'). The ping distinguishes 'gallery' (no selector matched — gallery selectors wrong) from 'gallery-no-urls' (elements matched, no usable URL — imageAttrs/urlUpgrade wrong, which is what the dead Poshmark regex was), because collapsing them wastes the signal. NO instance id is attached, unlike the grading calls, since that stable per-install id would make an anonymous counter linkable into a browsing trail. AC5 preserved and strengthened: renderError fires BEFORE the ping and never depends on it; the content script does not await it. Disclosure updated in both directions — SUBMISSION.md data-usage + privacy summary, and the packager now declares optional technicalAndInteraction to AMO (required would misstate an opt-in signal; omitting it would understate the add-on). STILL BLOCKS passes: AC1 (verified:true for the 5 adapters) needs live-site QA of each marketplace — cannot be done autonomously, flags left false. HELD MIGRATION: 00475 is committed locally and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md — do NOT push until it is applied to prod. Nothing client-side reads the new table, so the Pages auto-deploy is safe. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. So the correct residual action is an APPLY (+ NOTIFY pgrst), not a push-hold. | 2026-07-18 MEASURED CORRECTION to the status note above (agent loop): I wrote earlier today that "PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth ... 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending". That is FALSE and I am correcting my own claim. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00476, applied:00476, status:match} — the US-1566 block reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the DB own answer. 00475 and 00476 ARE APPLIED in prod. The only genuinely pending migration is 00477 (US-1999, correctly held/unpushed). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md has been corrected with the measured evidence and both sections re-marked APPLIED. The lesson: the answer was one unauthenticated HTTP GET away the whole time, and several passes (including mine) reasoned about prod schema state from commit history instead of measuring it.

userStories.title: Cross-browser: Firefox + Edge support for the unified extension
userStories.description: As a Firefox or Edge user, I want the extension to work. Audit: both extensions are Chrome-only in practice — background declares only service_worker (Firefox MV3 runs event pages via background.scripts; with only service_worker Firefox loads NO background at all); no browser_specific_settings.gecko.id (AMO requires it); the Lister additionally awaits promise-style chrome.* APIs that are callback-only on Firefox, and its onMessageExternal registration would throw at top level there. Edge is Chromium-compatible as-is and only needs a store submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest declares BOTH background.service_worker and background.scripts (the documented cross-browser pattern) + browser_specific_settings.gecko { id, strict_min_version: '109.0' }

A small runtime shim guarantees promise-style APIs on both browsers (use the browser.* namespace where present, or wrap the needed chrome.* calls); no top-level listener registration can throw on a browser lacking the event (guard onMessageExternal existence)

The research surface (condition read) works end-to-end on Firefox: config fetch, grade call (README's moz-extension origin in EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS documented in .env.example), overlay, popup, storage — verified manually on a real listing; Firefox's opt-in host-permissions flow is handled (prompt or graceful degradation)
Seller tools on Firefox: explicitly gated OFF with honest UI copy until US-1882 lands (externally_connectable does not exist on Firefox — no silent breakage)
Edge: the unified build loads and passes a manual smoke on Edge; store packaging checklist (Edge Add-ons) appended to US-1757's distribution scope
userStories.notes: Audit findings 18 + Lister §3 (four independent Firefox breakages). Safari deliberately out of scope (Xcode wrapper + no externally_connectable — revisit post-launch). | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC1 DONE — manifest declared only background.service_worker, so Firefox (which runs the background as a non-persistent EVENT PAGE and reads background.scripts) loaded NO background at all and the extension was inert there. background.js already documented+implemented its half of the contract; the manifest never did. Now declares BOTH service_worker and scripts (= importScripts deps + background.js, in order — background.js reads GT_LISTER_SELECTORS/GUARD/JOBS/REGISTRY at load) + browser_specific_settings.gecko {id: extension@gradethread.com, strict_min_version: 109.0}. AC2 load-time guards verified present (onMessageExternal + alarms). New test/background-deps.test.cjs derives the dep list from background.js's own importScripts and asserts the manifest matches exactly — the two copies only diverge on Firefox, which everyday Chrome work never exercises (US-1874 added job-store.js and nothing would have caught the omission). Guard verified against both the missing-dep drift and the pre-fix no-scripts state. 11/11 extension test files. BLOCKS passes: AC3 (research surface end-to-end on Firefox) + AC5 (Edge smoke) need a real browser. AC4 (gate seller tools off on Firefox) may be moot now US-1882's gt-bridge.js has landed — needs a decision, not a blind gate. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17 (b): AC4 RESOLVED AS MOOT + a shipped-build bug fixed. AC4 investigation: there is NO browser gate in extension-unified and none is needed — seller gating is capability-based off entitlements (registry.js:58 sellerEnabled, fail-safe false), and US-1882's gt-bridge.js gives Firefox a working transport (src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 falls back to sendViaBridge when chrome.runtime is absent; handleExternalMessage re-checks origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed either way). So no honest-copy gate is owed. BUT seller tools were still broken on Firefox for a DIFFERENT reason, in the packager rather than the extension: scripts/package-extensions.mjs hand-maintained a THIRD copy of the background dep list that predated US-1874's lister/job-store.js, so the shipped FF event page loaded with GT_LISTER_JOBS undefined; startJob threw at background.js:575 AFTER tabs.create had already opened the marketplace tab, sendResponse never fired, gt-bridge replied transportError, and sendListerJob deliberately does not settle on transportError (MV3 worker-death cover) — so the seller got an unfilled form and a 130s hang. Exactly the silent breakage AC4 was written to prevent, one file outside the guard. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: firefoxManifest() now DERIVES from the manifest instead of re-declaring it, which also fixed two more shipped-only bugs the same overwrite caused — strict_min_version was dropped entirely (add-on installable on pre-109 Firefox, no MV3) and the gecko id disagreed with the manifest's (extension@ vs unified@ = different add-on identity for a dev-loaded vs store build, and unchangeable post-AMO-submission). background-deps.test.cjs now imports the packager (run block guarded behind an isEntry check) and asserts the ACTUAL transform output, not a restatement of it; both regressions verified to fail the guard, then restored green. Shipped FF zip verified by unzip: 5 bg scripts incl job-store.js, min 109.0, externally_connectable stripped. 12/12 extension test files. STILL BLOCKS passes: AC3 (Firefox research surface end-to-end) + AC5 (Edge smoke) — both need a real browser + a human. NOTE for AC5: extension-condition's FF build has NO strict_min_version (its manifest declares no gecko block, so the packager fallback supplies only an id) — same pre-109 exposure, left alone as out of scope for this story. | 2026-07-19 THE AC5 SIDE-NOTE IS NOW FIXED (the story itself stays passes:false — AC3 Firefox end-to-end and AC5 Edge smoke still need a real browser and a human, which has not changed). A prior pass recorded, and then left alone as out of scope, that extension-condition's Firefox build has NO strict_min_version. Verified it: its manifest declared no browser_specific_settings AT ALL, so package-extensions.mjs supplied a gecko id from its config fallback and nothing constrained the version — the shipped Condition Check AMO zip had no floor. WHY THAT MATTERS: Firefox gained MV3 in 109, so the add-on installs on older Firefox where its own APIs do not exist, does nothing, and reads as our software being broken rather than as an unsupported browser. It is also a RECURRENCE, which is what makes it worth more than a one-line fix: the firefoxManifest() comment in the packager already lists 'a wholesale overwrite that dropped strict_min_version' as one of three drift breakages that shipped. It came back by a different route — absence rather than overwrite — so fixing only the instance would leave the third route open too. FIXED THE INSTANCE AND THE CLASS: declared gecko.id + strict_min_version 109.0 in extension-condition/manifest.json (manifest-first, per the packager's own stated rule that firefox.* config only FILLS GAPS), plus a packager guard that THROWS rather than warns — this is the step that produces a store upload, the artifact goes somewhere we cannot recall it from, and a warning in a build log is exactly what got missed the first time (verified exit code 1). Plus a repo-level test that derives its targets from the packager config, so a newly Firefox-enabled extension is covered the day it is enabled rather than the day someone remembers the file; it hard-fails if that derivation yields zero targets, because a guard that silently checks nothing is the failure mode it exists to prevent. Does NOT pin an exact version — raising the floor is a legitimate decision and a test that fights it gets deleted; having no floor never is. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED three ways: block removed, floor set to 102, and the packager run with no floor (exit 1). Note this hardens a DEPRECATED artifact, consistent with the US-2020 call: extension-condition is superseded but still packaged and still installed, so it has to keep working until its store listing is retired. 15/15 extension test files, 2472 web tests.

userStories.title: Web↔extension transport v2: postMessage bridge so seller tools work beyond Chromium
userStories.description: As a Firefox (later Safari) seller, I want 'Send to extension' to work. The current transport is chrome.runtime.sendMessage from the page via externally_connectable — Chromium-only by platform design. The standard alternative is a gradethread.com content script relaying window.postMessage to the background.
acceptanceCriteria: The unified extension adds a gradethread.com content script that relays a versioned, origin-checked window.postMessage protocol to the background (message schema validated exactly like the current external messages; responses relayed back with correlation ids)

src/lib/lister-extension.ts feature-detects transports: externally_connectable where available, postMessage bridge otherwise; isListerAvailable() reflects either; timeouts/settled-guard semantics preserved

Security parity: the bridge accepts messages only from window.top on allowed origins, validates payloads with the same schema, and never exposes marketplace responses to the page beyond the current result shape; the privacy copy (US-1872) already covers the gradethread.com host permission this requires
Chromium keeps using externally_connectable (no regression); Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark
userStories.notes: Unblocks the Firefox seller half of US-1881. The gradethread.com content script is the deliberate privacy-posture trade the US-1872 epic documents. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop): STATUS WAS STALE — this story read as unstarted but the bridge had already shipped (extension-unified/gt-bridge.js), which is why US-1881's notes referred to it as landed. Audited all four ACs against the code rather than the status. AC1 DONE: gt-bridge.js is a document_start content script on gradethread.com relaying a versioned envelope ({__gtExtReq,id,message} -> runtime.sendMessage -> {__gtExtRes,id,response}) with correlation ids, a `replied` guard covering Chrome's callback and Firefox's promise return, and responses posted to an EXPLICIT target origin (never '*'). AC2 DONE: src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 feature-detects — externally_connectable when chrome.runtime+id are present, else sendViaBridge; isListerAvailable() accepts the DOM marker alone (no extension id needed); the EXTENSION_TIMEOUT_MS backstop, the pushWaiters settled-guard and the deliberate do-not-settle-on-transportError semantics (MV3 worker-death cover) are all preserved. AC4 (Chromium no-regression) verified in code: the manifest still declares externally_connectable, sendViaRuntime is still PREFERRED, and both transports converge on the same handleExternalMessage which re-checks the sender origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed. GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (AC3): the AC requires the bridge accept messages 'only from window.top on allowed origins'. The origin half was satisfied (the content script only runs on gradethread.com, event.source!==window rejects other windows, and the background re-checks origin), but there was NO framing guard. The threat is clickjacking rather than forgery — event.source!==window already means only same-frame scripts can send an envelope and a cross-origin parent can run none — but a framed gradethread.com would let the page's OWN 'Send to extension' control be clicked through by a victim who cannot see it: a genuine seller action from a real click. gt-bridge.js now returns immediately unless window.top === window, installing NO marker and NO listeners (a marker alone would make the page offer seller UI in a context the extension refuses to serve), and fails CLOSED when reading window.top throws, which is what a cross-origin frame does. ⚠ NOTE this is defense in depth, not a live hole: gradethread.com ships X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none' — VERIFIED LIVE on the zone this pass. It is in the extension anyway because an extension must not stake its security on a response header it does not control; headers get relaxed for a partner embed or a preview host and the guarantee would vanish with nothing failing to signal it. TESTS: new extension-unified/test/gt-bridge.test.cjs EXECUTES the bridge against a stubbed window/document (rather than grepping source) and asserts: top-level installs marker+listener; framed installs NEITHER; a throwing cross-origin window.top also fails closed; the relay round-trips a correlation id and posts to an explicit origin; five malformed/foreign envelopes are ignored; and the background->page push relay forwards ONLY GT_LISTER_JOB_UPDATE/GT_LISTER_LISTED, never arbitrary background traffic. Both new guarantees negative-verified (removing the frame guard, and widening the push allowlist, each turn the suite red). 13/13 extension test files; packager still emits a valid FF zip. KEPT passes:false ON AC4 ONLY: 'Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark' needs a real browser on a real marketplace — same browser-gate as US-1881 AC3/AC5, and not something this agent can do. Everything else in the story is code-complete and tested.

userStories.title: Rewards: north-star metrics, per-mechanic attribution & retention instrumentation
userStories.description: As the operator, I want every gamification mechanic instrumented against explicit north-star metrics (week-4 retention, grades/user/month, share-loop K-factor) so that we can tell dopamine from retention and kill mechanics that don't move the business — before quests/seasons/leaderboards scale spend.
acceptanceCriteria: North-star metric definitions codified (week-4 retention by cohort, grades/user/month, K-factor from share-to-earn, milestone-grant cost per retained user) and computed from existing event data (reward_events, referral_events, affiliate_clicks, grade_credit_transactions)

Every reward grant, celebration, nudge, and external-badge click carries a mechanic-attribution tag (which mechanic caused it) so lift is measurable per mechanic, not just in aggregate — extends the US-1859 nudge-attribution pattern to ALL mechanics

Admin rewards-analytics surface: per-mechanic engagement lift, reward spend vs retention (extends the US-1858 spend-vs-signups ROI view), cohort retention curves gamified-vs-not, and a per-mechanic kill-switch honoring the US-1858 pattern
PostHog events for the key loop steps (grant, celebration shown, share, verified click-through, milestone claim) consistent with existing analytics conventions
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][ANALYTICS][NEW] Added 2026-07-09 (gamification refinement session). The epic had no measurement story — US-1858 covers spend/abuse ROI, US-1859 attributes nudges only; this makes every mechanic accountable. userStories.title: US-1891 backwards title sync never shipped server-side — the edge title-sync module has zero callers
userStories.description: As a seller, when I correct an item's Brand/size/color/style/department from ANY surface, I want the listing title to update — not just from the web item canvas. US-1891 (P1, archived passes:true) required the substitution on 'the edge item update path AND web item-canvas save' (its AC2). Only the web half shipped. src/lib/title-sync.ts is wired into item-canvas.tsx persist(); its declared lockstep mirror services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts is imported by NOTHING — verified 2026-07-18, every export has zero production references. So an edit made through the edge item-update API, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit or CSV import still corrects the brand and leaves the OLD brand in listing_title: exactly the bug US-1891 exists to fix, on every surface except one. Both suites are green because each calls its own copy directly, so nothing signals the gap.
acceptanceCriteria: Item edits from EVERY non-canvas write path apply the same substitution the web canvas does, under the same conditions (GT-origin non-ebay listings only; both title_variants; hand-edited-vs-ai_generated_snapshot sets needs_review; live listings queue the revise-in-place prompt, never end/relist). NOTE: there is no generic edge item-update endpoint — see the 2026-07-18 scope correction; the concrete surfaces are web bulk-edit (brand/size/color/style, nearest gap), identification-verify, and iOS
It cannot DOUBLE-APPLY against the frontend path — decide one owner per surface, or make the substitution provably idempotent for the web canvas case that already ran it

iOS is the ONLY remaining surface (audited 2026-07-18): AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style and iOS never writes listing_title. identification-verify only annotates provenance, and CSV import is fill-only so a blank old value makes the substitution a provable no-op — neither needs wiring. Needs a macOS session; test the Swift port against src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json so it cannot drift from the two JS copies

userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. This is the more serious of the two: US-1994 is a contract divergence with no known live bug, whereas this is a P1 feature that measurably does not run on most surfaces. US-1891's own notes describe the web wiring in detail ('Wired into item-canvas persist()') and never claim the edge half — the AC asked for both, and the story was marked done anyway. Worth asking what else in the archive has the same shape: a 'lockstep mirror' is a strong smell, since only one copy usually gets a caller. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). Each needs verifying by hand: superseded, pending, and half-wired all look identical to the tool. NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. Anyone picking this up would have started by hunting for an endpoint that was never built. WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES ITEM FIELDS (verified 2026-07-18): (1) web item-canvas.tsx — a DIRECT supabase write, no edge round-trip, and the ONLY surface that runs title-sync; (2) web autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:872 — also a direct supabase .update(), and it patches brand/size/color/style, i.e. FOUR OF THE FIVE SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELDS, with NO title sync at all; (3) edge lib/ai-listing.ts:1793 and lib/grading-pipeline.ts:657 — but US-1891's notes state the AI-apply path REGENERATES titles wholesale so it deliberately needs no sync; (4) edge lib/identification-verify.ts:245 (attributes); (5) iOS. SO THE HEADLINE CHANGES: the nearest, cheapest gap is NOT iOS or the edge — it is WEB BULK EDIT, in the same codebase, with src/lib/title-sync.ts already sitting there importable. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. Do not start coding before that is settled. The AC list above still stands EXCEPT AC1's 'edge item update path' phrasing, which should be read as 'every non-canvas write path'. | SIZING THE BULK-EDIT GAP (same pass): it is smaller than it looks. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx ALREADY selects listing_title AND ai_generated_snapshot from listings (line ~190) — which are exactly the two inputs title-sync needs, ai_generated_snapshot being the hand-edited-vs-AI check that decides whether to set needs_review — and it ALREADY writes back to listings (line ~707). It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free). The sizing is recorded so whoever makes the call knows the per-surface option is cheap, not so the decision gets skipped. | 2026-07-18 ARCHITECTURE DECIDED + AC4 DONE. THE DECISION: per-surface mirrors with a shared BEHAVIOURAL fixture — NOT a DB trigger. I had earlier offered the trigger as my pick and then argued myself out of it: applyTitleSubstitution is 100+ lines of token-boundary, case-transfer, multi-word-brand and size-pattern string handling, so porting it to plpgsql would create a THIRD implementation in the language with the worst string handling of the three. That is a bigger version of the disease, not a cure. Funnelling every item write through one edge endpoint was also rejected for now: item writes are direct supabase calls from multiple clients (web canvas, web bulk-edit, iOS), so that is a large migration of its own and does not have to be paid before fixing the actual bug. AC4 SHIPPED: src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json — 13 cases (10 syncTitle + 3 changesFromItemDiff) read by BOTH suites, services/edge-functions/src/tests/title-sync_test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/title-sync.test.ts. A source diff could never have been the guard: the two files legitimately differ by ~80 lines because the web copy inlines the trim (it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects). Behaviour is the only thing that can be compared. FINDING: the two copies currently AGREE on all 13 cases — I ran the fixture against each implementation before wiring it in, so a disagreement would have surfaced as data rather than as a red test I then rationalised. So they had not behaviourally drifted; the risk was that nothing would have caught it if they did. Negative-verified: breaking case-transfer in the web copy alone turns 3 web tests red naming the exact fixture case, and the edge suite stays green (which is the point — the failing side identifies itself). Verified: edge 4129 passed / 0 failed, web 2164 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. STILL OPEN: the actual gap. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx patches brand/size/color/style with no title sync, and it already loads listing_title + ai_generated_snapshot and already writes to listings — so with the fixture now guarding the copies, wiring that call site is the next step and is safe to take. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BULK-EDIT GAP IS CLOSED. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx now syncs the listing title when its reverse-projection writes brand/size/color/style back onto the item — so a seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts no longer gets 40 titles still naming the old one. I did NOT inline item-canvas's ~30 lines of orchestration, which would have been a FOURTH copy — of the orchestration this time, the substitution already being shared. Extracted it instead to src/lib/title-sync-patch.ts: buildTitleSyncPatch is pure (inputs -> listings patch, no IO) and owns the decisions wrapped around syncTitle — refuse ebay-origin listings (the sync-precedence guard), move BOTH A/B variants, and flag needs_review when the title was hand-edited away from ai_generated_snapshot or the listing is live. 9 unit tests. That extraction is the actual fix for this story's root cause: the pure helper was shared and the ORCHESTRATION was not, which is why only one surface ever ran it. NOTE the guard is explicit, not inherited: this page filters batch_id + listing_status='draft', which implies GradeThread origin via deriveListingOrigin, but relying on that implicit invariant is how these contracts rot — listing_origin is now selected and checked directly (the column has existed since 00232, far below prod's >=00474, so unlike quality_score it is safe to read). TYPESCRIPT CAUGHT A REAL BUG MID-WIRING: I threaded the new columns onto DraftRow but the save loop iterates EditRow, a different shape — tsc flagged four property errors rather than letting it fail at runtime on undefined. Fixed by carrying listingOrigin/titleVariants through the EditRow mapping. Verified: web suite 2173 passed (was 2164), tsc clean, lint exit 0. REMAINING for passes: the OTHER non-canvas surfaces — identification-verify (edge) and iOS — plus confirming CSV import routes through a covered path. Those are separate surfaces, not this one; buildTitleSyncPatch is deliberately pure so the edge and a future iOS port can consume the same decisions rather than re-deriving them. item-canvas.tsx should also be refactored onto it (it still has the longhand version) — mechanical, but it touches a large working component so it wants its own change. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) item-canvas.tsx REFACTORED onto buildTitleSyncPatch, so the orchestration now exists ONCE in the web app. I had created a second copy in the previous commit by extracting the helper for bulk-edit while leaving the canvas's longhand in place — which is the same duplication this story exists to remove, so leaving it would have been incoherent. ~30 lines of inline logic replaced by one Object.assign; tsc then flagged syncTitle and trimTitleToLimit as unused imports in that file, which is the tidy confirmation that the longhand path is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. PROVED BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BEFORE COMMITTING, not asserted: transcribed the OLD inline block verbatim into a throwaway test and compared it against buildTitleSyncPatch across the full input matrix — locked/unlocked x 4 change-sets x 4 titles (incl. empty, over-long-so-pure-retrim, and a token-boundary near-miss) x 3 variant shapes (incl. null entries) x 4 snapshot states x live/not = 768 combinations, 0 mismatches. Same standard as the 2048-subset proof used for US-1994's route swap. The throwaway was deleted after it passed; the durable coverage is title-sync-patch.test.ts (9 cases) plus the shared edge<->web fixture. Verified: web suite 2173 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. | 2026-07-18 REMAINING SURFACES AUDITED — three of the four need NO work, and the scope is now exactly ONE surface (iOS). Evidence per surface rather than assumption: (1) identification-verify.ts (edge) — NOT APPLICABLE. It updates only { attributes, ai_field_sources }, and the attributes it writes spread the existing map and add just identification_verified + market_title_keywords. Neither is a SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELD, so it never changes a value a title could contain; it annotates provenance/confidence, it does not re-identify the garment. (2) CSV import (src/pages/flipdesk/import.tsx) — NOT APPLICABLE, for a subtler reason worth writing down. It is FILL-ONLY (isBlank(existing[field]) && !isBlank(incoming)), so it can only populate a brand that was previously blank. A blank old value means there is nothing in the title to substitute: syncTitle with a blank `from` is a deliberate no-op, pinned by the shared fixture case 'blank from/to is ignored rather than blanking the title'. Filling a blank brand cannot fix a title that never named one, so wiring sync here would add a call that provably does nothing. Its own comment also confirms 'Listings/sales are left untouched on re-import'. (3) iOS — GENUINE REMAINING GAP, and the only one. ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style to inventory_items via a sparse FieldUpdate, and it is NOT fill-only: it keeps a Snapshot of pre-fill values expressly so an undo can restore them, which only matters if the write can overwrite a populated column. A repo-wide grep shows iOS NEVER writes listing_title anywhere. So an AI-fill on iOS that corrects a brand updates the item column and leaves the listing title naming the old one — the original US-1891 bug, surviving on exactly one surface. CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only (CLAUDE.md), so this needs a macOS session. The port is small and the decisions are already made for it — buildTitleSyncPatch is pure precisely so a Swift equivalent can mirror the same rules (refuse ebay-origin, move both variants, flag needs_review on hand-edited/live), and src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json is the behavioural contract a Swift copy should be tested against so it cannot drift from the two JS copies. | 2026-07-19 THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSIONS WERE NEVER WRITTEN BACK INTO THE CODE OR THE NOTE — fixed. The per-surface audit recorded above settled that there is NO edge item-update endpoint and that bulk-edit was the real gap (since closed), leaving iOS as the only remaining surface. But both durable artifacts still told the old story: services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts opened with '⚠ NOTHING IN THE EDGE SERVICE IMPORTS THIS MODULE' and named 'the edge item update path, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit, CSV import' as the affected surfaces, and vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md filed it under 'Accidentally dead' repeating the same list. THREE OF THOSE FIVE SURFACES ARE NOW WRONG: the edge endpoint does not exist, bulk edit is wired, CSV import is a provable no-op. So the two places a future reader would actually look were both directing them to wire an edge route that was never built — which is precisely the wasted session this story's own scope-correction warned about. Rewrote the module header as a per-surface table with the verdict for each, and an explicit DO NOT WIRE THIS instruction explaining that audit-unwired-exports.mjs will keep reporting it and that the report is correct. Moved the vault entry out of 'Accidentally dead' into a new 'Uncalled by design' section, since leaving a section titled accidental containing an entry titled by-design is its own small lie. NOT DELETED, deliberately: the edge copy is the reference the Swift port mirrors AND one half of the behavioural parity fixture asserted by both suites, so deleting it would remove one side of the only guard keeping the implementations honest. THIS IS THE SAME-COMMIT RULE BEING PAID LATE — the audit happened in a prd note and the artifacts it invalidated were left standing, which is exactly how the original US-1891 'lockstep mirror' claim survived being false. Story stays passes:false: iOS AIItemFieldWriter.swift is untouched and needs a macOS session. Verified: 16 edge + 19 web title-sync tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean. | 2026-08-08 THE 2026-07-19 "UNCALLED BY DESIGN" VERDICT WAS WRONG, AND IT HID TWO LIVE GAPS. That audit rested on "no route in services/edge-functions does .update() on inventory_items". FALSE: reconcile/apply in flipdesk-autolister.ts writes inventory_items AND listings from buildMergeWrites. The same audit table also listed "web item canvas | wired" — item-canvas.tsx had ALREADY BEEN DELETED, and its replacement src/pages/flipdesk/composer.tsx inherited none of the sync. So the flagship item surface silently lost the feature and a confident DO-NOT-WIRE header was standing guard over the loss. The generalisable lesson, now written into the module header and the vault note: an argument from an ABSENCE ("no route does X") cannot fail a test, so nothing announces it when a route starts doing X. Pin load-bearing absence claims with a test, not a paragraph. DONE THIS PASS: (AC1) composer.tsx saveDraft + saveLiveListing wired via a new titleSyncPatchFor(isLive) that builds before/after from itemAspectSource + columnWriteBack and reuses buildTitleSyncPatch, so the GT-origin/both-variants/needs_review/live-revise rules are the SAME code the bulk editor uses, not a reimplementation; grid.tsx inline brand/style/size edits wired the same way, with one batched listings read because items_full lacks listing_origin/title_variants/ai_generated_snapshot; edge reconcile-fields.ts buildMergeWrites now reconciles the resolved listing_title against the winning brand/size/color/style — the case where the seller KEEPS their title and takes the AI brand, which wrote a corrected brand column beside a title still selling the old one. Used applyTitleSubstitution not syncTitle there deliberately: syncTitle re-trims to 80 chars and that path never trimmed, so trimming a title the seller explicitly chose would be a bigger change than the fix; publish enforces the cap itself. (AC2) applyTitleSubstitution WAS NOT IDEMPOTENT and this is the real bug found while scoping: when the new value CONTAINS the old one ("L"->"L/XL", "North Face"->"The North Face", "501"->"501 Original") a second pass matched the old value inside the replacement it had just written and expanded again — "L/XL/XL". Widening a size and qualifying a brand are everyday corrections, and changes are computed from a captured before-map, so a retried mutation or a stale query cache replays {from,to} against a title that already holds the new value. Fixed in BOTH lockstep copies: spans already reading as the new value are guarded and only occurrences outside them are replaced. Negative-verified (forcing expands=false fails 2 tests). "One owner per surface" stays the design, but it is a convention and a convention is not a guard. (AC4) the shared fixture gained 3 expansion cases and a 6-case idempotent array, asserted by applying the changes TWICE in both the deno and vitest suites. (AC5) header rewritten — it now records why the old verdict was wrong rather than just replacing it, since the failure mode is the reusable part; vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md rewritten to match, and its authenticity-eval entry corrected too (three exports are wired now via US-1996; still no BLOCKING gate, deliberately). New services/edge-functions/src/tests/reconcile-fields_test.ts pins the merge-write title sync where it ships. STAYS passes:false FOR ONE REASON: AC3, the iOS Swift port of AIItemFieldWriter, is untouched and needs a macOS session (blocked-work-gates.md). Not splitting it into a successor story — AC1 says EVERY non-canvas write path and iOS is one of them; spending an id to make a P1 read done would be the exact shape US-1996 exists to catch. Verified: 5960 edge tests pass, 3665 web tests pass, tsc -b clean, vault:lint unchanged at the 19 pre-existing drift errors (US-2430).

userStories.title: Backlog integrity: archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED — starting with US-1770's unenforced authenticity safety gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want passes:true to mean the behaviour runs. Three archived stories say DEFERRED in their own notes and are marked passing anyway, and the unwired-export audit confirms at least one of them never shipped. The severe case is US-1770 (authenticity golden-set eval gate): its notes read '[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration' — it was deferred BY the held-migration rule and then closed. runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. The unmet ACs are the safety ones: AC1 requires a candidate prompt to clear an accuracy gate BEFORE activation and AC3 requires per-brand regressions to BLOCK activation — neither is enforced by anything, AC2's human-review routing, by contrast, IS implemented and tested (authenticityNeedsReview, wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054) — an earlier draft of this story claimed otherwise and was wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: US-1770 is reopened (or a successor story filed) and its authenticity eval gate is actually wired: no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate, and a per-brand regression blocks activation

US-1770 AC2 needs NO work — verified 2026-07-18: authenticityNeedsReview() routes a red_flags verdict (or a low-confidence branded assessment) to human review at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, with unit tests. Do not re-implement it. This AC is retained only so the correction is visible.
US-744 and US-1399 are triaged the same way: both are passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED and no later resolution note. Either reopen them or record why the deferral is now satisfied

A guard makes this class visible: passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED / 'blocks passes' marker in notes should be reported by prd-lint (a warning is enough — US-1883 shows a later note can legitimately supersede an earlier blocker, so it must not hard-fail)

US-1716 AC4 is corrected: it claims brand-fact provenance is "schema-enforced" and it is not — 00389 declares source_url text and confidence numeric(3,2) as NULLABLE with no NOT NULL, and admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 explicitly permits a null confidence. FIRST run: select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null (needs DB access — deny-all table). Zero rows ⇒ add the constraints; non-zero ⇒ this is a data migration, not a one-liner. NOTE the admin route ALREADY handles source_url (it is in the editable allowlists), so no plumbing is needed — only the requirement

ai-size-estimate-core.ts is resolved one way or the other: ai-size-estimate.ts re-declares all of its helpers rather than importing it, so the tests point at a dead copy and the LIVE helpers are untested. Either make the live module import core (as its header used to claim) or delete core and repoint the test
userStories.notes:
[P1][Backlog integrity / Safety] Found 2026-07-18 via scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs (shipped this session) plus a query for archived passes:true stories whose notes still say DEFERRED. TRIAGE OF THE 10 DEAD MODULES the audit found, so nobody repeats this work: GENUINELY MISSING — authenticity-eval.ts (US-1770, above) and brand-seed.ts (US-1716 AC4: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts are the only code that would reject an unsourced fact and nothing imports them). SUPERSEDED, behaviour intact, safe to delete or mark — content-ai-email.ts (US-918; the live newsletter path calls generateNewsletterCopy from newsletter-copy.ts), grade-badge.ts (US-118/766; deliberately removed in commit 8e1802a6 for an eBay-policy pivot to TEXT-ONLY grade signals, replaced by applyGradeListingPromotion), drip-trigger.ts (US-933; superseded by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts). PENDING, working as designed — measure-eval-stats.ts (US-1582 is OPEN and explicitly a human/operator task; it also HAS a caller, scripts/measure-eval.ts, so it was a false positive of the module-level check). JUDGEMENT CALL — grading-reliability.ts (US-481 AC3's self-consistency gate exists and runs in CI but only over hand-written fixture arrays, so it can never fail from a grading change; the notes concede a live-traffic feed is 'a future env-gated job'). NO OWNING STORY AT ALL — rubric.ts: migration 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and they are permanently NULL; the only record of intent is commit bbd94005 saying 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline... activation follow-up documented in rubric.ts', and that follow-up was never filed. Its client half IS live (src/lib/rubrics.ts, certificate.tsx), and the two 'MUST stay in sync' with no test pinning them — file the activation story. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts and ai-size-estimate-core.ts carry ⚠ headers naming the gap, because their green tests otherwise read as proof the feature exists. ai-size-estimate-core.ts's previous header actively asserted a false link ('ai-size-estimate.ts re-exports everything here') which would stop a reviewer looking further. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC4 DONE — prd-lint now warns on passes:true + an unresolved blocker marker (findUnresolvedDeferrals, exported + pure). CORRECTION TO THE COUNT ABOVE: it is FOUR stories, not three — US-744, US-1399, US-1770 and US-1931. I had cleared US-1931 last round using the same loose word-matching that this guard exists to replace; its notes are a SINGLE segment ending in DEFERRED 2026-07-11 with no later closing note, so it is unresolved. ⚠ THE GUARD SHIPPED WITH THE EXACT BUG IT TARGETS, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT: v1 matched /(DONE|SHIPPED|...)/i anywhere after the marker and therefore cleared US-1770 — its motivating case — because ~2300 chars later the prose read "best done in a user-present session". Searching long free text for a common English word always finds it. Resolution is now a CASE-SENSITIVE uppercase closing token (DONE/CLOSED/SHIPPED/COMPLETED/RESOLVED/VERIFIED) in a LATER pipe-separated note SEGMENT, with an explicit NOT DONE exclusion so the negated form cannot clear anything. Verified against the real 1878-story archive: flags exactly US-744/1399/1770/1931 and correctly leaves US-1883 alone (its later CLOSED segment supersedes the earlier blocks-passes note — which is why this is a WARNING and can never be an error). ⚠ SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: npm run test:scripts is BROKEN ON A CLEAN TREE — both scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs and scripts/prd-digest.test.mjs fail with SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and run ZERO tests, while scripts/verify.mjs:63 runs that command in the web lane. Proven pre-existing by stashing my changes and re-running. node --check passes both files, esbuild transforms both fine, and a trivial probe .mjs test under the same config passes — so it is neither syntax nor the transform, and the cause is still unidentified. The 9 guard cases were therefore verified by executing findUnresolvedDeferrals directly under node instead; the vitest cases are committed and will cover it once the harness is fixed. This is the same class as the dead modules: a suite that looks like coverage and runs nothing. Needs its own story. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BROKEN test:scripts HARNESS IS FIXED — root cause was a CRLF SHEBANG. vite/esbuild strip a shebang by matching #!...
; with CRLF the stray  survives and the module fails to parse, so importing scripts/prd-lint.mjs or prd-digest.mjs from a vitest test threw SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and BOTH suites ran ZERO tests while scripts/verify.mjs:63 still invoked them in the web lane. Isolated by a 3-way experiment: shebang+CRLF FAILS, shebang+LF passes, no-shebang+CRLF passes — so it is the combination, not either alone. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the git blobs are already LF and core.autocrlf=true rewrites them to CRLF ON CHECKOUT, so this is WINDOWS-ONLY and CI on Linux stayed green throughout. Every Windows checkout has been running zero script tests. Fix is .gitattributes: *.mjs and *.cjs now text eol=lf, extending the rule CLAUDE.md already documents for .githooks/** and *.sh (which exists for the same CRLF-shebang hazard, just a louder failure). Verified: npm run test:scripts goes 0 -> 27 tests passing across 2 files; the 9 findUnresolvedDeferrals cases from the previous commit — which I had to verify by hand under node because the harness was dead — now execute through the real harness and pass; node scripts/test-extensions.mjs still 13/13. ZERO content churn: the blobs were already LF, so after renormalizing, the only staged change is .gitattributes (+13 lines). | 2026-07-18 ⚠ CORRECTION — I OVERSTATED THIS STORY. AC2 (human-review routing on a counterfeit verdict) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, and my description saying it is 'absent' was wrong. ai-authenticity.ts:439 exports authenticityNeedsReview(), whose own docstring is tagged 'US-1770 (AC2)' — the exact AC I claimed was unmet — returning true on a red_flags verdict or on a recognisable brand assessed below AUTHENTICITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD. It is wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, where the grade_report is written as `needs_human_review: compositeResult.needs_human_review || authenticityNeedsReview(authenticityAssessment)`, and it is unit-tested in ai-authenticity_test.ts. So a counterfeit call DOES route to a human today. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since it is instructive: the audit grepped red_flags, found the note site (grading-pipeline.ts:1663, which writes detailedNotes.counterfeit_confidence and sets no review flag), and concluded 'a note, and nothing else'. The ROUTING is ~400 lines further on and reaches the assessment through a helper rather than through the red_flags field, so a field-name grep could not see it. I verified the story's other two claims (US-1770 marked passes:true while its notes say DEFERRED; runAuthenticityEval having zero callers) and did NOT verify this one before writing it into a P1 description. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, re-checked this pass: AC1 — runAuthenticityEval still has ZERO callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate, so 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' is unenforced. AC3 (per-brand regressions block activation) depends on the same missing activation path. The severity drops accordingly: the safety net that catches a bad call at grade time EXISTS; what is missing is the gate that would stop a bad PROMPT VERSION shipping in the first place. (1) "runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests" is FALSE today: admin-grading.ts:1366 calls it from POST /authenticity/eval, main.ts:1730 warns on the gate at boot, public-grading.ts:1360-1373 returns 503 + Retry-After when the grounded prompt is ungated, and grading-pipeline.ts:2871 stamps gate.gated onto the passport event. AC3 SETTLED, opposite answers: US-1399 was a FALSE POSITIVE (its [COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred] is real, and the guard was taught COMPLETION and un-deferred because of it). US-744 was a TRUE POSITIVE and is now REOPENED — moved out of prd.archive.json back into the active backlog at priority 2387 with passes:false. Its deferral is not satisfied: AC1 (app-wide PWA install affordance) and AC3 (offline submission-status/certificate caching) need a real phone and an installed PWA. I did NOT file a successor story and left this row passing, because that would have preserved the exact claim the guard exists to catch and spent an id to avoid saying the work is unfinished. prd-lint now reports zero unresolved-deferral warnings, for the honest reason. ⚠ AC5 REMAINS AND IS OPERATOR-BLOCKED: it needs select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null against a deny-all table. Zero rows means add NOT NULL to 00389s source_url/confidence; non-zero means this is a data migration, not a one-liner — and the count decides which, so it cannot be guessed.
