userStories.title: FlipDesk is described but never shown publicly; contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA signals vaporware
userStories.description: As a high-volume reseller evaluating FlipDesk, we want to see the actual tool before signing up. The public site describes FlipDesk with icon+text cards but shows ZERO product screenshots, GIFs, or demo; the genuinely strong AutoLister (batch upload, HEIC/Live Photo, auto-group, bulk generate, auto-publish) is only visible AFTER signup. The power-reseller persona had to commit on faith and nearly bounced. Compounding the vaporware read: the homepage closing section pairs 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' even though the product is clearly live — a mixed launch signal at the exact conversion moment.
acceptanceCriteria: Homepage and /for-resellers show real FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery (screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF) of the bulk pipeline
The contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA is removed or reconciled now that the product is live
userStories.notes: [P3][Web/Conversion] 5-persona QA sweep 2026-07-13. Power-reseller persona: the tool is strong but hidden behind a signup wall; 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' reads as vaporware. | 2026-07-14 (branch claude/prd-stories-review-lsem0z): AC2 SATISFIED + AC1 SUBSTANTIALLY ADDRESSED. AC2: audited the whole app — there is NO public "Join waitlist" CTA rendered anywhere (WaitlistForm component is unused; the homepage/for-resellers closing CTAs are "Try FlipDesk Free"/"Start Grading Free" + a legit newsletter signup), so the vaporware CTA contradiction is already gone. AC1: the landing page already showed the FlipDesk pipeline via honest per-stage stylized mocks (labeled "not a real screenshot"); /for-resellers only DESCRIBED it in text. Extracted the stage data to src/components/marketing/flipdesk-stages.ts and a reusable presentational src/components/marketing/flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx (no landing-only data-flipdesk-* scroll-scene hooks, so flipdesk-scene.ts does not bind it), then added a "The full reseller workflow, built in" section to /for-resellers rendering the full source→grade→list→reprice→reconcile pipeline + a "Try FlipDesk Free" CTA. landing.tsx now imports the shared FLIPDESK_STAGES (dropped its inline copy + now-unused Boxes/Tag icons). Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; npm run build prerenders 213 routes and dist/for-resellers.html (36KB) contains the pipeline stages + honesty caption + CTA. KEPT passes:false: AC1 literally asks for real screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF — the stylized mocks show the flow honestly but real product imagery is a design-asset follow-up (no FlipDesk/AutoLister screenshots exist in the repo to wire in). | 2026-08-02 AC2 RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not taken from the previous note): grepped every .tsx/.ts under src for waitlist CTAs. WaitlistForm has ZERO importers — the only hit outside its own file is a COMMENT in newsletter-signup.tsx saying it mirrors WaitlistForm's prerender-safe dynamic import. So the string "Join waitlist" exists only inside a component nothing renders, and the vaporware CTA contradiction is genuinely gone from every public surface. AC2 holds. AC1 IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM A CHECKOUT and I want that stated plainly rather than left as "substantially addressed". The AC asks for REAL FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery — screenshots or a short GIF of the bulk pipeline. What exists is honest stylized mocks, explicitly labelled "not a real screenshot", now shared between the landing page and /for-resellers via flipdesk-stages.ts + flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx. That was the right intermediate step and it removed the /for-resellers text-only gap, but a labelled mock is precisely what the story says is insufficient: the persona in the description "had to commit on faith", and a drawing that admits it is a drawing does not fix that. Producing the real thing needs the app running against a real account with real inventory, someone to capture it, and a judgement call about what seller data is safe to show publicly. That is a human with the product open, not a code change. RECOMMENDATION: treat AC1 as an asset-production task and either assign it or split it out, rather than leaving the story open against a checkout that cannot satisfy it. A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME GREP, worth its own attention: the waitlist BACKEND is still live while its only public entry point is orphaned. /api/waitlist exists, /admin/waitlist is in the admin nav, and edge-fetch.ts:160 still routes a waitlist-gated account to a dedicated pending page — but nothing on the public site can add anyone to that list. So the system is half-wired in the direction that is hard to notice: an operator opening the admin page sees a waitlist that can only ever shrink. Same shape as vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md catalogues, and the same decision it always needs — either the waitlist is a live feature whose public capture form should be rendered somewhere, or it is retired and the form, the admin page and the gating branch go together. Not decided here because removing gating touches the auth path, and rendering a waitlist form on a live product would reintroduce the exact vaporware signal AC2 exists to prevent. That tension is the reason it needs a decision rather than a default.

userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Trigger + per-listing results now live in the app. Placement is deliberate: the button sits IN the amber "this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its title/price/description/photos" banner on the item canvas — the exact place the seller hits the wall — rather than on a settings page they would have to know to look for. useMigrateEbayListings() reports eBay reasons PER LISTING rather than collapsing to one "done" (a multi-variation rejection is actionable, "failed" is not), capped at 3 toasts so a large batch cannot bury the screen. ⚠ FOUND AND FIXED A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE LOOK BROKEN: item-canvas computed lockedByEbay via deriveListingOrigin() but its listings query never SELECTED listing_origin — and that persisted column is exactly what migration writes, and what deriveListingOrigin lets WIN over the provenance signals. So post-migration the row still had a platform_listing_id, no batch_id and no synced_to_ebay_at, the canvas would have re-derived "ebay", and the seller would have seen the locked banner and the migrate button still sitting there after a SUCCESSFUL migration. Added listing_origin to the select + the two type literals, and invalidated the item_ebay_sync query in the mutation (it backs that banner; without it the UI would not refetch at all). Pinned with a NEW test file src/lib/__tests__/listing-origin.test.ts — deriveListingOrigin gates revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote and the locked-fields banner across the app and had ZERO test coverage before this; 5 tests now cover persisted-marker-wins (both directions), unrecognized-marker fallback, batch/sync signals, draft-with-no-listing-id, and non-eBay platforms. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. STILL passes:false — the only thing left is a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it), which cannot be done from the sandbox. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. Post-deploy smoke checks run the same day: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 (auth enforced) rather than a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which is the specific failure that would indicate 00477 had not landed; a real certificate off sitemap-certs.xml still returns 200, so the grading/cert path is unbroken; and gradethread.com now serves Permissions-Policy camera=(self) (a first check showed the old camera=() from a cached response — the cache-busted request confirmed the fix is live, worth noting because that cached read looked exactly like a failed deploy). | 2026-07-19 RE-VERIFIED LIVE. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' — auth enforced, route mounted, and specifically NOT a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which remains the exact signature that would mean 00477 (listings.inventory_sku) had not landed. So the feature is still healthy in prod. The ONLY remaining item is unchanged and unreachable from a sandbox: a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it) needs a live seller account with legacy listings. TWO INCIDENTAL SIGNALS FROM THE SAME PROBE, worth recording for whoever runs the next deploy: /health/ready still reports schema {expected:00478, applied:00479} — so the DEPLOYED edge predates the 00480-00485 stack, and the phantom 00479 is still there; and features{} has NO 'alerting' key while observability reads 'ok'. Both are artefacts of the deployed build predating today's work: US-2003 adds the alerting group and US-2001 makes observability report DEGRADED until GIT_SHA is a real SHA. Expect both to change on the next deploy — 'alerting' will appear as degraded (no channel configured) and 'observability' will flip from ok to degraded until the build arg is wired. Neither is a regression; they are the new checks becoming visible.

userStories.title: Handbags and small leather goods cannot be graded — 'bag' routes into the clothing rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of handbags, I want a bag graded on the things that determine a bag's price, because 'bag' is already a garment_category and item_category has 'bags' (00230), while the only rubric that will accept it grades fabric condition at 30% and odor at 10%. A handbag's condition is corner and edge-paint wear (the single most-inspected area and the most expensive to restore), handle and strap darkening and cracking, hardware plating loss and zipper pull function, interior lining staining and pen marks and odor, structural slouch and base sag, and glazing on the edges. The category also carries the most authenticity weight of anything we touch — the existing tells (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) are ALL bag brands — so grading and the authenticity add-on land on the same item here, and the certificate has to be careful not to let a condition grade read as an authenticity verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: A handbags/leather-goods rubric is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Photo slots cover the areas that decide a bag's grade: corners, base, interior, hardware, handles/straps, and the date-code/serial location.

A condition grade on a bag must NOT read as an authenticity statement anywhere on the certificate or in the buyer writeup — an explicit separation, test-asserted on the rendered copy, given these are the brands the authenticity add-on covers.
Measurement templates cover bag dimensions (width, height, depth, strap drop).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2. Highest-value of the three new-rubric stories: handbags carry the most price-per-item and are the exact brands the authenticity add-on covers (louisvuitton/coach/gucci are ALL bag brands), so the condition-vs-authenticity separation on the certificate is a liability requirement, not polish.

userStories.title: Neckwear and small accessories cannot be graded — ties, belts, scarves and gloves have no rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of accessories, I want ties, belts, scarves and gloves gradeable, because belt and scarf are already garment_category values with nowhere to route and neckwear is not even representable. These share a shape — small, single-construction, few failure modes, and a condition profile the clothing rubric's five factors describe badly. A tie's condition is the blade shape and roll, the tipping and keeper loop, the interlining (a tie that has lost its roll is damaged even with a perfect face), and stains that are effectively permanent on silk. A belt's is the strap creasing and cracking, the buckle and prong and the hole elongation. A scarf's is fringe integrity, pilling and pulls. Odor and cleanliness at 10% and structural integrity at 25% do not carry those.
acceptanceCriteria: An accessories rubric (or a small set of them where the categories genuinely diverge) is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Decide and record whether ties/belts/scarves/gloves share one rubric or split — the decision goes in the story notes, not a commit message.
garment_category is widened to represent neckwear and gloves; the migration follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats.
Measurement templates cover the fields the categories are actually sold on (tie blade width and length, belt length and hole positions, scarf dimensions).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a golden set bootstrapped for these categories.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2, same prerequisite as US-2223. belt and scarf are already garment_category values with nowhere to route; neckwear is not representable at all.

userStories.title: Headwear cannot be graded — hats have a garment_category, no rubric, no photo slots and no measurements
userStories.description: As a seller of hats, I want to grade a cap the way I grade a hoodie, because headwear is a high-volume resale category and today 'hat' is a garment_category value that routes into a clothing rubric which cannot express it. Verified: GARMENT_CATEGORIES includes 'hat'; rubric.ts has clothing, sports_cards, watches and shoes and nothing else; MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES has top/bottom/dress/outerwear/shoes/watch/generic and nothing else; the required image types are front/back/label. A fitted cap's condition lives in places none of those reach: brim shape and flatness, crown structure and collapse, the sweatband (the first thing to fail and the first thing a buyer inspects), the button and eyelets, embroidery integrity and pulls, and staining at the front panel and sweatband.
acceptanceCriteria: A headwear rubric is added to rubric.ts with its own factors and weights summing to 1.0, plus promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared rubric-factors fixture.
A headwear measurement template is added (fitted size / circumference, crown height, brim length) in the units the category actually uses.
Headwear-appropriate photo slots exist (crown, brim, sweatband/interior, label) — grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is.
The weighted-overall computation stays in lockstep across all three rounding sites in the same commit as any factor-set generalization this requires.

The new rubric's prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first — a rubric with no golden set cannot pass the gate and must not be activated around it.
Any enum widening (image_type, garment_category) follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats in the migrations skill.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2 — the factor-set generalization across the three lockstep rounding sites is a prerequisite for ANY new rubric, and US-1997's notes already scope it. Do not build a fourth rubric before that lands.

userStories.title: Edge builds ship with release="dev" — every prod edge error is unattributable to a commit (frontend is correct)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to know which build produced a production error. The frontend does: https://gradethread.com serves a bundle tagged release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814", a real commit SHA, so Cloudflare Pages is wiring VITE_RELEASE_SHA correctly. The EDGE does not: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"dev"}, measured 2026-07-18. Root cause is exact — services/edge-functions/Dockerfile:12 declares ARG GIT_SHA=dev and line 13 sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA}; its own comment (lines 9-11) says the builder must pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT, and the Coolify build is not doing so, so the literal default ships. lib/observability.ts:52 releaseSha() therefore returns "dev" and tags every Sentry event, structured log and trace with it. This is an ASYMMETRY between the two halves of the system, and the half that is blind is the one handling grading, payments, eBay writes and webhooks.
acceptanceCriteria: The Coolify build passes the commit into the image (GIT_SHA build arg = $SOURCE_COMMIT or the platform equivalent), so RELEASE_SHA is a real SHA in production.
GET /health on production returns a release that matches the deployed commit — verify by measuring the endpoint after a deploy, not by reading the config.
Sentry edge events carry that release, so an error can be attributed to a deploy and "did the fix ship?" is answerable. Confirm a real event is tagged.

A guard so this cannot silently regress: the edge should REFUSE to report healthy-and-production while release is the literal default "dev"/"unknown" — or at minimum surface it as a degraded feature in /health/ready features{} alongside the existing observability entry, which currently reports "ok" while the release is meaningless.
Document the build-arg requirement in COOLIFY.md next to the other deploy settings, since the Dockerfile comment alone did not survive contact with the actual deploy.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Observability][Measured] Found 2026-07-18 during the cross-platform production-readiness deep dive, by querying prod rather than reading config. EVIDENCE, all live: /health -> {"status":"ok","service":"gradethread-edge-functions","env":"production","release":"dev","errorTracking":"enabled"}; the frontend bundle /assets/index-CIbHzx5V.js contains release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814" (which is also proof Pages auto-deployed that commit). WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC TAG: with every edge event tagged "dev" you cannot (a) attribute a production error to a build, (b) tell whether a deployed fix actually shipped, (c) see a regression appear at a release boundary, or (d) make a rollback decision on evidence — and ROLLBACK.md assumes you can identify the bad build. Note errorTracking reports "enabled" and /health/ready features.observability reports "ok", so the health surface actively says observability is fine while the release dimension of it is inert; that is why AC4 asks for a guard rather than just a config fix. The fix itself is small (one build arg); the reason it survived this long is that nothing measured it. | 2026-07-19 AC1/AC4/AC5 DONE; AC2/AC3 need a deploy to confirm. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A MISSING BUILD ARG, and the fix is DECLARATIVE rather than another instruction: docker-compose.coolify.yml now carries build.args GIT_SHA: dev. That placement is the whole point — the Dockerfile has carried a comment telling the builder to pass GIT_SHA since it was written, and per this story's own evidence that comment did not survive contact with the actual deploy. A build arg in compose is APPLIED BY THE PLATFORM instead of remembered by a person, so documenting it harder would have reproduced the same failure. The :-dev fallback keeps a plain local docker compose build working. AC4 DONE and it is the anti-regression half: the observability feature group now requires SENTRY_DSN *and* a real RELEASE_SHA, so /health/ready reports observability DEGRADED while the release is a placeholder — previously it reported 'ok' in the exact prod state this story measured (errorTracking enabled, release 'dev'), which is the false confidence that let it sit unnoticed. isRealReleaseSha is deliberately permissive on FORM: it rejects the placeholder set (dev/unknown/local/none/latest/empty) but accepts short SHAs and tags, because the measured failure was the literal ARG default surviving the build, not a malformed SHA — requiring 40 hex chars would break tag-based deploys for no benefit. 4 tests, including the exact prod state as a case. AC5 DONE in COOLIFY.md with a MEASURE-DO-NOT-READ verification step (curl /health | jq .release), plus the warning that deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant needs the same args block. ⚠ REMAINING AND GENUINELY UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: AC2 (measure /health after a deploy) and AC3 (confirm a real Sentry event carries the release). Both require the deploy to actually happen. What HAS changed is that a regression now announces itself on /health/ready instead of waiting for someone to think to curl. [2026-07-19 AC4+AC5 DONE, AC1-AC3 NEED THE COOLIFY BUILD + A PROD MEASUREMENT] AC4: /health/ready now carries features.release, degraded whenever the release is unattributable (dev / unknown / empty / whitespace, case-insensitive). Deliberately a SEPARATE key from features.observability: that group reports ok whenever a Sentry DSN is present, which stays true and stays misleading while every event it ships is tagged dev. Also deliberately does NOT flip the service to not_ready — the AC allowed either, and refusing readiness on an untagged build would pull grading, payments and webhooks out of rotation to protect observability. health.ts already argues this exact principle for the schema probe (a probe that can fail a container over a diagnostic is a worse bug than the blind spot it fixes). A test asserts ready stays true. releaseReadiness() is pure; 5 new tests. AC5 FINDING: COOLIFY.md already had a US-2001 build-args section from an earlier pass, and it CLAIMED /health/ready reports features.observability as degraded on a placeholder release. That was FALSE — nothing implemented it. The documentation described a guard that did not exist, which is a plausible reason nobody built one; same defect class as US-2035 (comment asserting a property the code lacks) and US-2123 (copy advertising an ungranted entitlement). Doc now names the real key, shows the curl, and records the correction rather than quietly overwriting it. STILL OPEN (all need the deploy, not code): AC1 the Coolify build must actually pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT — docker-compose.coolify.yml declares it but prod measured release=dev on 2026-07-18, so either the deploy uses docker-compose.yml or the Build Args field is unset. AC2 verify by curling /health after a deploy. AC3 confirm a real Sentry event carries the SHA. The new features.release entry makes AC2 checkable without remembering the curl. | 2026-08-02 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and it FAILS. The AC insisted on measuring the endpoint rather than reading the config, and that instruction earned its keep: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns features.release = 'unattributable: release="dev" — the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg, so errors cannot be tied to a commit'. So AC1 is declared but NOT IN EFFECT. docker-compose.coolify.yml carries build.args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, and the running image was still built without it. Three candidate causes, in the order worth checking: (1) Coolify is deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant — the previous pass explicitly warned that the plain file needs the same args block, and that warning is now the leading hypothesis rather than a footnote; (2) the running image predates the compose change and no rebuild has happened since; (3) SOURCE_COMMIT is not populated in this Coolify version, so the :-dev fallback wins silently — which is exactly what the fallback is designed to do and exactly why it is indistinguishable from cause (2) without a rebuild. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until this is fixed: every event currently ships tagged 'dev', which is the state the story exists to end. WHAT THIS CONFIRMS ABOUT AC4, and it is the useful part: the guard works. /health/ready reported the problem in plain language, unprompted, to a caller who did nothing but curl a public endpoint. That is the difference between a config that is wrong and a config that ANNOUNCES it is wrong — before this, the only way to learn it was to notice that every Sentry release said dev. The AC4 decision not to flip the service to not_ready also holds up: the service is genuinely serving, and pulling grading and payments out of rotation to protect observability would have been the wrong trade. STILL OPEN: AC1 in practice (the build arg must actually reach the image), AC2 re-measured after that deploy, AC3 confirmed on a real event. All three need one Coolify rebuild, and the first thing to check is which compose file the service is deploying from. ALSO OBSERVED IN THE SAME RESPONSE, recorded here because it is the same curl: schema reports {expected:00512, applied:00512, status:match}. See the note on the held-migration gate. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-03: any "HELD"/"apply-BEFORE-push" wording earlier in this note describes the state AT THE TIME OF WRITING and is STALE. Prod was measured at applied=00514 on 2026-08-03 via /health/ready (the database's own answer, not a recollection), and every migration up to 00514 is on origin/main. The only migration currently held is 00515 (US-2168), which is unrelated to this story. Do not read this note as evidence that the branch is frozen. | 2026-08-08 CAUSE (1) CONFIRMED AND FIXED. The 2026-08-02 pass listed three candidate causes and said the first thing to check is which compose file the service deploys from. Checked it, and the answer is in this repo's own doc: COOLIFY.md line 11 says the one-time setup makes Coolify 'auto-pick docker-compose.yml'. That file's first line calls itself 'Production compose used by Coolify' — and it had NO build.args block. So the arg was declared only in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is not the file the documented setup deploys. docker-compose.staging.yml was missing it too.

FIX: both now declare args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, identical to the .coolify.yml one. Deliberately declared in ALL of them rather than picking the 'right' one — the question 'which compose file is it actually using?' is precisely what nobody could answer for three weeks, and making the answer irrelevant is cheaper than making it knowable.

NEW STATIC GUARD (AC4's missing half): services/edge-functions/src/tests/compose-release-arg_test.ts walks every docker-compose*.yml, and any file with a build: section that lacks GIT_SHA fails CI with the reason. It also asserts the Dockerfile still wires ARG GIT_SHA -> ENV RELEASE_SHA, so the guard cannot stay green over a dead mechanism. Override files with no build: section (docker-compose.dev.yml) are exempt — they inherit the base build. Sabotage-verified: deleted the arg line from docker-compose.yml, test failed naming the file; restored, 2 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

WHY A STATIC GUARD ON TOP OF THE RUNTIME ONE: the /health/ready guard worked exactly as designed and still cost three weeks, because it can only speak after a bad image is already serving. A per-file declaration that only one file carries is a per-file bug, and nothing was looking ACROSS the files. This test looks across the files.

COOLIFY.md rewritten: the old text carried a warning telling the operator to add the block by hand or fill in Coolify's Build Args field — asking a person to remember something, which is the failure mode this story is about, and the Dockerfile had been asking in a comment since it was written. It now states all three files declare it, records why, and keeps ONE residual manual step for the only cause the code cannot rule out (a Coolify version that does not populate SOURCE_COMMIT, where :-dev wins silently).

STILL passes:false, and only on the deploy: AC2 (curl /health/ready after a Coolify rebuild and see a real SHA) and AC3 (confirm a Sentry event carries it). Both need a rebuild, which ADE Hub is disarmed for. Nothing further is doable from a checkout — the code side of AC1 is now complete on all three files and guarded.

userStories.title: Category grading criteria cover 8 of 20 garment categories — 12 categories grade with no category guidance at all
userStories.description: As a seller of a shirt, a coat or a skirt, I want the grader to know what matters on my category, because the ones that do get it are measurably better guided. Verified: ai-grading.ts:320 GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA has exactly 8 keys (jeans, pants, shorts, jacket, sweater, hoodie, t-shirt, dress) while src/lib/constants.ts GARMENT_CATEGORIES has 20 values. The 12 with no entry — shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf, other — fall through to the generic prompt with only DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE. Each of the missing ones has real category-specific signal the model is currently not told to look for: collar and cuff fray and yellowing on shirts, seam slippage and pulls on blouses, lining and shell separation and pilling on wool coats, zipper and hem and lining on skirts, and for footwear the outsole and midsole entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Every value in GARMENT_CATEGORIES has a criteria entry, or the fallback is made explicit and deliberate for the ones that genuinely have none.
Each new entry follows the existing voice: what is INTENTIONAL design on this category vs what is genuine wear, since that distinction is the whole point of the block.
The prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, not a silent edit — this changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once.
Golden-set cases exist for the newly-covered categories before activation, tagged so the eval report can slice per category.
Categories already covered produce byte-identical prompts, test-guarded, so the eval measures only the new coverage.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 8 of 20 categories covered. Cheapest coverage win in the epic (prompt data, no schema), but it changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once so it needs a real eval cycle and per-category golden cases first. | 2026-08-08 AC1/AC2/AC5 DONE. AC3 IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN, and that is the finding. AC4 unchanged and still blocking.

AC1: all 11 remaining categories written (shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf). "other" is DELIBERATELY left uncovered and the absence is now pinned by a test: it is the value assigned when the category is UNKNOWN (garment-mapping.ts maps five of six garment types to it), so an "other" item may be any of the twenty and there is no honest guidance to give. Generic filler there would restate DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE and make coverage look complete while the real gap is upstream classification.

AC2: each entry draws the design-vs-defect line, and a test fails any entry that names only defects. The calls worth having are the ones a generic prompt gets backwards: midsole yellowing on sneakers is OXIDATION not soil (and some releases ship pre-yellowed), vachetta patina on a bag is supposed to darken, leather patina on boots is desirable aging, the molded footbed impression on sandals is permanent use that affects resale, and the fold crease at the worn hole is the defining signal on a belt.

AC3 CANNOT BE SATISFIED — verified, not assumed. The AC says ship through shadow -> golden-set eval -> canary. That lifecycle covers the SYSTEM prompt ONLY. GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA is interpolated into the per-image USER message by buildUserPrompt, and: an ai_prompt_versions row carries one prompt_text which becomes the system block, so no override can reach it; canary picks between two system texts; runEval overrides system text only, so the criteria are ambient on BOTH legs of its comparison; grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only AND reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path at all. Worse, PerImageAnalysis carries no version field, so PER_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION never reaches a grade record — bumping it would have looked like compliance and changed nothing.

So the change ships ENV-FLAG GATED (GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2, default OFF), which is the only gate the architecture offers and is the same pattern GRADING_BASELINES / GRADING_TAG_OCR already use. The eleven entries live in a SEPARATE map from the shipped eight, so byte-identity is a property of the file rather than a claim a reviewer has to diff. Composite grades attributed with a +cat2 suffix, appended last per the stated ordering rule.

AC5 DONE and strengthened: byte-identical for the eight with the gate ON, AND a no-op for all twenty with it OFF, so deploying this commit changes no grade. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED four ways — dropped a category entry (AC1 + coverage + disjoint reddened), flipped the gate to default-on (the no-op test reddened), duplicated a key into both maps (only the source-scan caught it, which is exactly why that test is a source scan and not behavioural), and moved +cat2 out of last position (ordering test reddened).

STILL passes:false: AC4 (golden-set cases for the newly-covered categories, tagged for per-category slicing) needs real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet — the same bootstrap problem US-1997 Phase 2 has. Until then the flag stays off, and the flag being off is why that is safe rather than merely convenient. The structural fix for AC3 is US-2432.

Also corrected in the same commit: vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md claimed each block appends a suffix "so accuracy-tracking can attribute an era per block". The suffix records a block PRESENCE, not its CONTENT — editing FABRIC_CRITERIA still reports +fabric — and the per-image stage is not attributed at all. The note now carries the versioned-vs-not split as a third axis alongside trusted/untrusted. | 2026-08-08 AC3 IS NO LONGER IMPOSSIBLE. The note above says the shadow/eval/canary lifecycle CANNOT reach GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA because it is interpolated into the per-image USER message, and names US-2432 as the structural fix. That fix shipped as US-2438: category_criteria is now one of two blocks in a versioned registry (ai_prompt_block_versions, migration 00563), and runEval takes a blockCandidate that pins exactly that block while the system prompt stays active. So the eval-gate leg of AC3 is available today. TWO CAVEATS, both real: the SHADOW leg is still missing — grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only and reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path to run a category-criteria candidate through, and that is US-2438 AC2 rather than a wiring task here. And AC4 is unchanged and still blocking on its own: a per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet. So GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false — what changed is that the gate is now buildable rather than architecturally unreachable.

userStories.title: Backups: mechanism verified, prod backup cron never installed — real RPO is total loss
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want prod data to be recoverable. The scripts are all real and executable (scripts/ops/backup-postgres.sh, backup-storage.sh, restore-postgres.sh, restore-drill.sh) and a restore drill genuinely passed 2026-06-12 (BACKUPS.md:129, 270 RLS policies matched) — but that drill ran against a LOCAL stack at migration 00151. The prod side is unchecked: LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:236-243 has all five boxes unticked, including 'Backup cron installed on the DB host' and 'first nightly dump confirmed in the offsite bucket'; the drill table at :231-234 is empty. PITR is explicitly aspirational (BACKUPS.md:90-92, 'MANUAL: wal-g setup happens on the prod host'). So the documented RPO<=24h / RTO<=2h is only true if a cron nobody confirmed is running. Prod is a SINGLE-NODE self-hosted Postgres (SCALING.md:47) holding grades, billing and the credit ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: Install the backup cron on the prod DB host (BACKUPS.md:42-43) and CONFIRM a dump plus its .sha256 lands in the offsite bucket — verified by listing the bucket, not by reading the runbook.

Run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:231. The 11-second figure at BACKUPS.md:129 came from a near-empty schema-only DB and will not predict prod RTO.
Either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest nightly-dump figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver.
Tick the five LAUNCH_CHECKLIST boxes only once each is independently verified.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/DR][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. This is the single highest-value hour of work in the repo: the ONLY finding in the entire audit whose failure mode is unrecoverable data loss. Everything else degrades; this one ends the company. Note the shape — NOT a missing-mechanism finding. The scripts exist, they work, someone drilled them. It is an ACTIVATION gap: a runbook step marked MANUAL that was never performed, and a checklist that honestly records it was never performed. The danger is that the presence of good tooling reads as protection. | 2026-08-02 AC3's DOCUMENTATION HALF DONE — the runbook no longer states an RPO the infrastructure may not deliver. AC3 says "either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver." The note was already honest about ONE gap (nightly-dump 24h vs PITR 5min, with a callout saying the 24h figure stands until wal-g is configured) and blind to the bigger one: EVERY number in that Targets section is a property of the backup MECHANISM, and the mechanism running is what was never verified. If the cron is not installed on the prod host, the real RPO is not 24 hours, it is TOTAL LOSS — and the table would have told an operator otherwise at exactly the moment being wrong costs the most. Added a danger callout under Targets stating that, marked LAUNCH BLOCKER, with the two checks that settle it (crontab -l on the DB host should list the backup line from the Setup section; the offsite bucket should hold a dump from the last 24h WITH its .sha256 beside it — a dump with no checksum is a backup nobody has proven readable) and an instruction to replace the callout with the date once both are true. I did NOT assert the cron is missing. I cannot see the prod host, and a runbook that states an unverified fact as fact is the same defect one level down. It says UNVERIFIED and how to verify. WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING WHILE THE REST IS BLOCKED: AC1, AC2 and AC4 all need someone on the prod host and are genuinely operator work. AC3 is the only half that is a claim rather than an action, and a runbook is read during an incident by someone who will not re-derive it — which is precisely when an overstated recovery point does its damage. The shape is worth remembering and is written into the callout: this is not a missing mechanism. The scripts exist, they work, the restore was drilled on 2026-06-12. It is a runbook step marked MANUAL that nobody performed. STILL OPEN, all operator: install the cron and confirm a dump plus checksum lands offsite (AC1), run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing (AC2), tick the five launch-checklist boxes only once each is independently verified (AC4).

userStories.title: Every alert channel is optional and silently no-ops — nothing proves anyone gets paged
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a SEV1 to reach a human. Today every channel degrades to silence when unconfigured. .github/workflows/uptime.yml:46 marks UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK 'Optional' and scripts/ops/uptime-check.mjs:188 logs 'not set — skipping webhook channel' then continues. Edge-side, ops-events.ts:104-108 falls back to MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, which ENV_REFERENCE.md:168 marks as not set. ops-events.ts:242-244 records an ops_event.alert_undelivered metric when neither channel exists — a metric that itself has no alert. INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:42-46 asserts all three sources 'must point at the same on-call channel before launch', which is an instruction, not a verified state; LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264-268 leaves it unchecked. The only channel that works with zero config is the GitHub uptime issue fallback, which pages only if repo-watch mobile notifications happen to be on.
acceptanceCriteria: Set UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK and MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, then RUN THE DRILL: break a target, confirm the message arrives on a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md. Configuration is not evidence.

Make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric — fail at boot (or emit at critical) when production has no alert channel configured. A monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence.
Confirm Sentry alert routing actually delivers (LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264) — see also the webhook dead-letter story, which routes ONLY to Sentry.
Measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target in INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:33 — a 10-minute GitHub cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Alerting][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Pairs with the backup story: that one is about surviving a disaster, this one is about LEARNING there is one. Every other alerting improvement is worthless until these two secrets are set and drilled, because they are the last mile for all of them. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (partially — see below); AC1/AC3/AC4 still need you. AC2 asked to make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric, because 'a monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence'. Added an 'alerting' feature group to env-validation: in PRODUCTION ONLY, a deploy with none of MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL set now reports DEGRADED on /health/ready and warns at boot, instead of the current state where every channel silently no-ops and nothing says so. Non-production is exempt via enabledWhen — a dev box has no business paging anyone, and warning there would train people to ignore the warning. ANY channel satisfies it, deliberately: the failure being caught is 'none of them', not 'not the one I expected'. I did NOT make it fatal at boot, which AC2 offered as an option. Refusing to start the edge because no webhook is configured would convert a monitoring gap into a total outage — strictly worse than the problem, and the opposite of the fail-open reasoning applied in US-2013. Degraded-and-loud is the right severity for 'we cannot tell you when things break'. STILL BLOCKED ON YOU and this is the launch-blocker part: AC1 (set the two secrets, break a target, confirm the message reaches a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers) and AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target). Configuration is not evidence and neither is a degraded-flag — this story stays open until a human has watched an alert arrive. Note US-2004's cron stall detector is now proven to detect, so it is queued up behind exactly this last mile. | 2026-08-02 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and fixed a reporting bug the measurement exposed. AC2's health surface WORKS: GET /health/ready reports features.alerting = "ok", so at least one channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL) IS configured in prod. That is worth recording plainly, because AC1's framing assumed none were set. What is still unproven is whether a message actually ARRIVES — AC1's drill is about delivery, not configuration, and a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" here forever. THE BUG THE SAME CURL FOUND: features.observability returned the literal string "missing: " — nothing after the colon. The cause is a group whose satisfiedWhen fails while every var it LISTS is present. observability requires SENTRY_DSN plus a real RELEASE_SHA; the DSN is set, so the `miss` array is empty, and the message named nothing. An operator reading that at 3am is told something is missing and refused the name of it, which is worse than no line at all because it costs them the time to go looking. FIXED in computeFeatureReadiness and warnMissingFeatureGroups: when nothing is literally absent, the message now says the vars are all present and the check still rejected one, instead of an empty list. Two tests pin both paths — the all-present case, and the regression that a genuinely absent var must still be NAMED, which is the whole value of the line for every other group. WORTH BEING PRECISE ABOUT WHAT observability's DEGRADED MEANS, since "missing" read alarmingly and I nearly reported it that way: Sentry IS configured and IS receiving events. The group is degraded solely because RELEASE_SHA is "dev" — US-2001's problem, reported here as a second symptom. So the dead-letter path in US-2011 does reach Sentry; its events are simply untagged and unattributable to a commit. One Coolify rebuild with the GIT_SHA build arg clears BOTH this line and US-2001. STILL OPEN AND ALL OPERATOR WORK: AC1's drill (break a target, confirm the page lands on a phone, date it in the launch checklist), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers — see US-2011, which routes ONLY to Sentry), AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target; a 10-minute cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified). None is a code change and none can be done from a checkout. VERIFIED: edge suite 5092 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean across 1291 files.

userStories.title: Brand KB has no tailoring/formalwear, western, golf, ski/snowboard, swim, scrubs/uniform or vintage-band-tee coverage
userStories.description: As a seller in a category we do not cover, I want my brand recognized, because an unrecognized brand loses the whole knowledge stack at once — no grounded baseline (garment_baselines falls back to ungrounded v2), no sizing chart, no style disambiguation, no tells. Verified against the 170-brand sizing seed and the ~177-brand brand_knowledge set: whole selling categories are absent. Tailoring and formalwear (suits, sport coats, tuxedos, neckwear, bridal) — nothing beyond Brooks Brothers/Peter Millar as general labels. Western (Ariat, Justin, Lucchese, Stetson) — none. Golf (Titleist, FootJoy, Callaway, Greyson) — none. Ski/snowboard (Burton, Spyder, Volcom, Obermeyer) — none, despite an outdoor-technical tier-2 pack existing. Swim (Speedo, TYR, Vilebrequin, Andie) — none. Scrubs and uniform (Figs, Cherokee, Wonderwink) — none, despite it being one of the highest-volume resale categories. Vintage and band tees — the single most price-sensitive tag-era category in resale, with no coverage at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Each category ships as its own brand pack migration following the existing conventions (brand_knowledge + brand_styles + brand_size_charts + colorways where they apply), with a header note recording what makes the group different — the convention every pack from 00447 onward follows.
Brand selection within each category is justified by resale volume, and that justification is in the migration header.
Tailoring's sizing is modelled honestly: chest+length letter suffixes (40R/40L/40S) and drop are the sizing system, not an alpha size — this cannot reuse the tops chart shape unchanged.

Vintage/band tees are seeded around tag_eras (single-stitch, made-in-USA, Screen Stars / Brockum / Giant tag generations) rather than around style names, because that IS the identity signal in the category — and it lands on the tag_eras consumer this epic builds.
