userStories.title: No affirmative consent to recurring billing is captured or retained at purchase
userStories.description: There is no checkbox, no separate consent step, and no consent artifact of any kind for the recurring charge — verified across payments.ts, billing.tsx and pricing.tsx (zero hits). Stripe's consent_collection parameter is not used on the Checkout Session (services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:395-422, 542-554), and no custom_text is set. A real consent system already exists but is scoped to signup only: legal_acceptances (00142_legal_acceptance.sql:39-49) captures tos_version, privacy_version, method, user_agent, ip_address, accepted_at — and its method enum (signup_clickwrap | oauth_clickwrap | reacceptance) has no purchase-time value. It is never written at subscribe time. Separately, the highest-volume path is the weakest evidence: the signup trigger insert (:121-126) omits ip_address and user_agent entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture express affirmative consent to the recurring charge at purchase, separate from and in addition to general ToS acceptance.
Record a durable consent artifact at subscribe time: user, timestamp, IP, user-agent, the plan/interval/amount consented to, and the version of the disclosure copy shown.

Extend the legal_acceptances method enum with a purchase-time value, or add a purpose-built table — reuse the existing versioning machinery (lib/legal-versions.ts) rather than inventing a second system.
Backfill ip_address and user_agent on the signup clickwrap path (00142:121-126).
Retain consent records per the period set by the counsel review gate (California: 3 years, or 1 year post-termination, whichever is longer) and ensure no data-retention job prunes them earlier.
Cover the iOS/App Store and future Google Play purchase paths too — consent there is collected by the platform, so record which platform captured it and when, rather than duplicating it.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Express informed consent plus retained proof is the core of both ROSCA and the California ARL. Today we could not demonstrate what any subscriber agreed to. Depends on the terms-snapshot story for the 'what was shown' half. | 2026-07-19 INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — and the scoping matters, so here is what the next pass needs. THIS STORY IS GENUINELY MORE COUNSEL-GATED THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS. US-2117, US-2119, US-2120 and US-2125 all turned out to be mechanism (I was wrong to call them gated, four times). This one is not the same: US-2114's AC1 explicitly puts 'the affirmative-consent WORDING AND MECHANISM' under review, so AC1 here is squarely gated, and AC5's retention period is gated by US-2114 AC5 by name. AC4 IS NOT GATED, and I traced it to a precise conclusion. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS: POST /api/legal/accept (routes/legal.ts:109) records ip_address via clientIp(c) and user_agent from the request header, SERVER-SIDE, and it already accepts method='signup_clickwrap' in its allowlist. So nothing needs building — the strong-evidence path is there and is used today by the legal GATE (oauth_clickwrap / reacceptance). The gap is only that the EMAIL-signup path never calls it: handle_new_user's trigger (00142:121-126) writes the signup_clickwrap row itself, inside Postgres, where it has no request context — hence no IP, no user-agent. That is exactly why the highest-volume path carries the weakest evidence. ⚠ THE TRAP, and the reason I did not just 'fix' it: the obvious shortcut is to pass ip/user_agent through signUp()'s options.data so the trigger can read them. DO NOT. Those would be CLIENT-SUPPLIED and trivially forged, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one — it looks authoritative in exactly the setting where the record's only value is that it can be trusted. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement and US-2119's refusal to send a dateless notice. THE ACTUAL SEAM, for whoever picks this up: email signup defers the session until confirmation (emailRedirectTo), so /api/legal/accept — which requires auth — cannot be called at signUp() time. The right hook is the FIRST AUTHENTICATED SESSION, in use-auth.ts's onAuthStateChange SIGNED_IN branch, which already runs exactly this shape of one-shot post-signup work (redeemStoredAffiliateRef, sendWelcomeEmailOnce gated on a user_metadata flag). Call /api/legal/accept with method='signup_clickwrap' there. ONE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST: legal_acceptances is an append-only audit table, so this produces TWO rows for one signup — the trigger's (guaranteed, weak) and the endpoint's (best-effort, strong). I think that is the RIGHT outcome rather than a defect: you always have a record, and usually a provable one. But it should be a decision, and the endpoint needs an idempotency guard so a repeated SIGNED_IN does not append a third. AC6 is also unblocked and unstarted: recording WHICH PLATFORM captured consent for IAP/Play purchases (where the platform collects it) rather than duplicating it — subscription_agreements.source (US-2117, migration 00486) already has the appstore/google_play values for exactly this. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC6 DONE. Both platform purchase paths now record WHICH PLATFORM captured the consent — appstore verify and the Play RTDN reverify each write a subscription_agreements row via recordPlatformAgreement. This became cheap only because two other pieces landed first: US-2117's table (with the appstore/google_play values already in its source CHECK) and US-2124's platform-event work that made me read these routes. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT IS THE DESIGN, and it is what AC6 actually asks for: Apple and Google COLLECT AND STORE the affirmative agreement natively, so duplicating it would be dishonest — we did not take that consent and cannot attest to its wording. The row therefore records THAT the platform took it, not a claim that we did. Concretely: amount_cents is 0 with an in-place comment saying it is NOT a real price, because the platform owns and localises the amount and inventing a figure would be the same error US-2117 refuses on the Stripe path — a partial record that reads as fact. A test asserts BOTH the zero and its explanation, because an unexplained 0 will eventually be read as 'this user agreed to pay nothing'. stripe_subscription_id is namespaced as <source>:<external_id> so an Apple transaction id cannot collide with a Stripe subscription id in the uniqueness index, and a 23505 is swallowed — a replayed IAP verify or a repeated RTDN must not report a failure, since the index firing IS the idempotency working. A test pins that both paths call it, so the gap cannot reopen on one platform while looking closed on the other. WHAT THIS CHANGES IN PRACTICE: before, 'what did this user agree to?' was answerable for a Stripe subscriber and unanswerable for an IAP or Play one — the two populations had different evidentiary standing for the same product. STILL OPEN and correctly gated: AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items; AC4 (server-side IP/UA on the signup clickwrap) is scoped above with its trap named — the mechanism already exists in /api/legal/accept, the seam is the first authenticated session, and passing a CLIENT-SUPPLIED ip through signUp() would be worse than the current absence. Verified: edge 4319 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: No record of what price or terms any user actually agreed to — pricing_plans is mutated in place
userStories.description: The users table stores flipdesk_plan and flipdesk_interval but NO amount column; price is resolved live on every read via getFlipdeskPriceIds() against pricing_plans. pricing_plans (00166:69-80) is mutated in place with only an updated_at trigger — no history table, no versioning. flipdesk_subscription_events records from_plan/to_plan and the raw payload but, per the note already in 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:20, not even the billing interval. Combined, there is no way to reconstruct what price any user was shown or agreed to on any past date. If a price changes, the historical record changes with it.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot the agreed terms onto the subscription record at purchase: amount, currency, interval, plan, trial terms, and the disclosure-copy version — immutable once written.
Version pricing_plans (history table or append-only revisions) so a past price is reconstructable.
Record the billing interval on flipdesk_subscription_events.
Make cancellation_reason append-only per-event rather than a single mutable text column overwritten on each cancel.
Follow the migrations skill: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the same commit, self-record footer.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Data] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the evidentiary half of the consent story — consent to WHAT is unanswerable without it. Also unblocks honest revenue reporting. | 2026-07-19 ALL FOUR SCHEMA ACs DONE (migration 00486) + the write path. ⚠ I FIRST ASSERTED THIS WHOLE COMPLIANCE BATCH WAS GATED ON US-2114 (counsel) AND THAT WAS WRONG — recording it because the error was mine and would have left a P0 sitting untouched. US-2114 gates what the disclosure copy SAYS; this story is about whether we can still PROVE what it said. Those are different questions, and only the first needs a lawyer. Testing the assertion instead of repeating it is what surfaced the work. AC1 subscription_agreements — immutable snapshot at purchase (plan, interval, amount, currency, trial terms, disclosure_version pointer). IMMUTABILITY IS TRIGGER-ENFORCED, not merely intended: UPDATE and DELETE both RAISE. A comment asking people not to edit a compliance record is not a control, and this table's entire value is that its contents cannot drift. disclosure_version is nullable because the copy versioning (US-2114/US-2115) has not landed — recording the POINTER now means no second migration later. AC2 pricing_plan_revisions — append-only history written BY TRIGGER on pricing_plans, deliberately not by the application: a history table that depends on the writer remembering is a history table with gaps. Stores a full jsonb row snapshot too, so a column added to pricing_plans later is captured historically without another migration here. Seeded with current rows as revision zero so the history has a floor rather than implying prices did not exist before today. AC3 flipdesk_subscription_events.billing_interval — the gap 00215's OWN comment recorded; from_plan/to_plan alone cannot distinguish a monthly→yearly switch from a no-op. AC4 subscription_cancellations — append-only; users.cancellation_reason was a single mutable column each cancel overwrote, so a repeat canceller left one reason and no trace it happened twice. Backfilled from that column (timestamped updated_at, the best available approximation — the true cancel time was never recorded, which IS the defect) and the old column is KEPT since readers still use it. WRITE PATH: lib/agreed-terms.ts, pure extraction + a thin IO half, wired into handleSubscriptionChange — chosen over checkout.session because the subscription object carries what Stripe ACTUALLY applied (amount, interval, trial) whereas checkout carries what was requested. THE DESIGN POINT WORTH REVIEWING: it DECLINES TO WRITE rather than writing a partial row when the subscription cannot support a truthful record (no price, no unit_amount, or an interval we do not sell — Stripe also emits day/week). A compliance record containing a plausible guess is worse than a visible gap, because it will be read as fact. The refusal is reported, so the gap is not silent. Best-effort throughout: a compliance record must never be why a paying customer fails to get entitlement. Idempotent via a unique index, so a webhook redelivery cannot mint a second agreement for one purchase. 9 tests. The one that matters most: a MISSING amount must yield NO record while a REAL zero is kept — 0 is a legitimate agreed price (comped/fully-discounted), so defaulting absence to 0 would be indistinguishable from a genuine free agreement on the record. Negative-verified by making absence default to 0; that test goes red. ⚠ THE RLS GUARD CAUGHT MY OWN TABLES, which is the system working: three new tables with owner columns, RLS enabled and no policies is exactly the case US-2008's widened guard exists to catch, and the full suite went red until I classified them. All three are now in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY with the reasoning — they are evidentiary, read only by admin/support tooling, and the failure mode of a permissive policy (a user reading, or influencing, the record of what they agreed to) is precisely what they exist to rule out. STILL OPEN: nothing schema-side. What remains is US-2114's counsel review before any disclosure COPY ships, and wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned. Migration 00486 is HELD (7th) — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md for the two backfills and the deploy-order note. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00215, 00486) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping.

userStories.title: Authenticity prompt activation must fail closed — the eval gate has never run
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-authenticity.ts (530 lines) is LIVE with three callers: the paid grading add-on (grading-pipeline.ts:1239), the buyer credit-metered check (routes/buyer-authenticity.ts:53), and an UNAUTHENTICATED public endpoint (routes/public-grading.ts:998). Results surface on public certificates. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts (268 lines) — the accuracy gate — has zero non-self callers. Its own header states: '⚠ THIS GATE DOES NOT RUN... Do not read this module's green tests as evidence the gate exists.' So an authenticity prompt version can ship today with no accuracy bar at all. The condition-grading engine has exactly this gate and enforces it; authenticity was built to the same design and never wired.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path, mirroring how the grading engine gates prompt versions (shadow -> eval gate -> canary).
Activation must FAIL CLOSED: an authenticity prompt version that has not passed the gate cannot be activated, and if no golden set exists yet, activation is blocked rather than defaulted open.
Add the admin route/surface needed to run the eval and view results.
Emit a startup or health warning while any live authenticity prompt version is ungated, so this cannot silently regress again.
Test that activation is refused when the gate has not passed, and that the refusal is visible rather than silent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Safety][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This is the single most urgent item in the epic: we are already making authenticity claims in production with no accuracy bar, including on an unauthenticated public endpoint. Same risk class as the FTC Section 5 substantiation work (US-2114..2128). Load the grading-engine skill first — it owns the prompt-version lifecycle this must mirror. Related: US-1996 tracks the backlog-integrity side of the same gap. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: shipped authenticityGateStatus + gateStatusFromRun (pure, fail-closed on BOTH no-run and query-error) + assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (the fail-closed guard a future activation path must call) + warnAuthenticityGate wired into main.ts as backgrounded non-throwing boot work (NOT a boot guard — US-778 crash-loop precedent). Model is part of the gate key, mirroring US-2036. Guard test extended: accepts either runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable, and now pins the boot check. 4348 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: (a) no authenticity prompt-ACTIVATION path exists to block — authenticity prompts are code constants, not ai_prompt_versions rows; building that lifecycle needs a migration and was deliberately NOT invented here (see the reasoning in authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, which argues against speculative lifecycles); (b) the gate will report ungated for every version until US-2131 seeds real labeled cases. Next: admin route to RUN the eval. ITER2 2026-07-19: added GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/gate (reports whether each live version has a passing run on the serving model; all_gated headline) and POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/eval (step-up gated — costs one vision call per case; surfaces the empty-golden-set case as a 400 setup state, not a 500). Reused the existing admin group so guards/audit are inherited. authenticity_eval_* already carry admin RLS policies, so no rls-guard registration needed. 4348 edge tests pass. | 2026-08-02 VERIFICATION — THE WORK SHIPPED AND THE RECORD NEVER SAID SO. This is a P0 safety story whose notes contained nothing but the founding audit, so anyone reading the backlog would conclude the authenticity gate is entirely unbuilt. It is not: commit 0e5afb89 "US-2130: make the authenticity eval gate runnable and its absence visible" landed it, and the note was written onto US-1996 instead. I walked all five ACs against the code. AC2 MET — assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (lib/authenticity-eval.ts:291) calls authenticityGateStatus and returns {ok:false} unless gated, so it REFUSES BY DEFAULT; with no golden set the status is not gated and activation is blocked rather than defaulted open, which is exactly what the AC asks. AC3 MET — an admin route runs the eval against a chosen prompt version, defaulting to AUTHENTICITY_PROMPT_VERSION_GROUNDED because that is what the live pass uses when brand tells are available, and it writes an audit log with the version, model and pass/fail. AC4 MET — warnAuthenticityGate() logs "[BOOT] authenticity: prompt X is serving UNGATED" for each live version, and it IS called, at main.ts:1685. It is deliberately best-effort and non-throwing, and the reason is recorded in its own header: a boot guard that can fail is how the schema-version check once crash-looped the whole edge service (US-778). AC5 MET — authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, and it asserts the boot call itself (/warnAuthenticityGate\(\)/ against main.ts), not just the function's existence. AC1 IS MET BY A DIFFERENT MECHANISM THAN IT NAMES, and the substitution is the interesting part. The AC says "wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path". THERE IS NO SUCH PATH: authenticity prompts are code constants, not rows in ai_prompt_versions. The previous pass declined to invent an activation lifecycle to satisfy the wording, and said why in the code — inventing a flow to satisfy a checkbox is how authenticity-eval.ts became dead code in the first place. Instead it shipped the property the AC exists FOR: a source-scan test that FAILS THE BUILD if an authenticity prompt-activation path ever appears without calling runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable. That is arguably stronger than the literal wiring, because it cannot be forgotten by omission — the wiring protects one call site that exists, the guard protects every call site that does not exist yet. RECOMMENDATION: close on all five, and let the fact that the gate has never actually RUN sit where it belongs — that is a golden-set problem (US-2131 built the curation surface for exactly this) and not a defect in the gate. I am not closing a P0 safety story myself on a substituted AC; the substitution is defensible and documented, but it is the owner's call whether "no activation path exists, and a guard fails the build if one appears" satisfies "wire it into the activation path". WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND WORTH NOT LOSING: the epic's framing stands — the scaffolding is built and the evidence base is not. The gate is runnable, visible and fail-closed; it has no golden set to run against, so nothing has been certified. That is the honest state, and it is a much better state than the notes implied.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22). | 2026-08-02 THE APPEAL PIPELINE IS BUILT AT BOTH ENDS AND HAS NO SELLER-FACING BUTTON. Verified by grep, not inferred. The SELLER endpoint exists and is complete: POST /authenticity-appeal at routes/grade.ts:1301 — it verifies the caller owns the submission, 422s when the grade has no authenticity assessment to contest, and rate-limits deliberately (the comment says why: hiding the verdict while an appeal is open means an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict indefinitely — that is a well-reasoned control, not boilerplate). The ADMIN side exists too: GET /authenticity/appeals is the open queue oldest-first and POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve closes them, and the queue's ordering carries its own reasoning (while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty). AND NOTHING IN src/ CALLS THE SELLER ENDPOINT. A grep for "authenticity-appeal" across every .ts and .tsx under src returns ZERO hits. So an operator opening the appeals queue sees a list that can only ever be empty, and a seller whose genuine item was flagged still has exactly what the story title says: no way to contest it. THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEPT FINDING, and it is the third instance today — the waitlist backend with no public capture form, the grade-card switch writing columns nothing read, and now this. Each time the expensive half was built and the cheap half was not, and each time the missing half is the one a USER touches. Worth naming explicitly on a story about a seller being unable to defend a genuine item: the backend being done makes this look further along than it is, and anyone reading the route file would conclude the feature ships. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC1 is therefore smaller than the AC implies but not trivial: the surfaces where a seller SEES the verdict (the certificate view and the submission detail) need a contest action that POSTs to the existing endpoint, plus the open-appeal state AC2 asks about — and AC2 is a real design question, not wiring, because the passport is append-only so a withdrawal is a superseding entry rather than an edit. AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published) is also still open and is arguably prior to AC1: they cannot contest what they were never told about. AC6 needs counsel. I did not build the UI — the certificate and passport display rules in AC2 have to be settled first, and shipping a contest button before deciding what the certificate shows while an appeal is open would put a seller in a state nobody has defined. | 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC2 DONE — the seller can now contest a verdict. MY EARLIER BLOCKER DISSOLVED ON INSPECTION, and that is worth recording because I nearly left this unbuilt on it: I said AC2 (what the certificate shows while an appeal is open) had to be settled first. It already was, server-side, and I had not read far enough. hideAssessmentForAppeal (lib/authenticity-appeal.ts:106) NULLS verdict, verdict_confidence, authenticity_confidence, counterfeit_risk and summary, sets under_appeal + appeal_opened_at, and stashes the original in appeal_hidden_original — guarded against stashing a stash on a second appeal, which would make the original unrecoverable. The endpoint then RESEALS (AC4) because integrity v4 covers the verdict, and its own comment explains why the reseal passes the HIDDEN assessment rather than the stored one. So AC2 and AC4 were shipped; only the button was missing. SHIPPED: NEW src/components/grade/authenticity-appeal-dialog.tsx and a "This is genuine — contest this result" action on submission-detail.tsx, the surface where the seller actually sees the verdict. THREE DETAILS THAT ARE NOT DECORATION. (1) The page now renders an UNDER-REVIEW card when under_appeal is set, instead of the normal card. Without it the seller sees a row of blanks where the verdict was — which reads as a bug, and is worse than not shipping the button at all, because it makes them think their appeal broke something. (2) The dialog is mounted at the PAGE root, not inside the authenticity card, so it is not unmounted the instant the card swaps to its under-review state on a successful file. (3) MIN_REASON = 20 mirrors the server's validateAppeal floor deliberately, and the client copy spends it telling the seller what a reviewer needs before they type: being rejected after writing is how someone abandons an appeal they were entitled to. The 429 path surfaces the SERVER's message rather than a generic retry, because that cap is a deliberate control (an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict) and a retry prompt would send the seller round the same loop. GUARD: NEW src/test/authenticity-appeal-wired.test.ts — something must POST to the endpoint, the dialog must be RENDERED somewhere rather than merely defined, the seller surface must handle under_appeal, and the client minimum must match the server's. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to every test that exercises the route directly, so only a scan catches it. STILL OPEN: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path), AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is PUBLISHED — arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told), AC6 (counsel, folded into US-2133). VERIFIED: full web suite 248 files / 3154 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, and a better outcome than expected. I wrote that AC5 was "still open" and "arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told". THAT IS WRONG. AC5 IS DONE. notifyAuthenticityFlagged (lib/authenticity-notify.ts:71) is called from grading-pipeline.ts:2785, fires only on a red_flags verdict, and is best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. It had reached the same design conclusion I was about to: it rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a notification type the user's preferences do not know about — an appeal IS a dispute. Its copy is careful in a way worth preserving: "our authenticity check flagged details it could not confirm ... an automated estimate from photos, not a determination", because saying the item IS counterfeit would assert something an ungated photo-only estimate cannot support. THE FLOW IS NOW END-TO-END, which is the actual news: the notice links to /dashboard/submissions/{id}, and that is exactly the page where the contest button I added this session lives. So the loop closes — red_flags verdict fires a notification, the seller clicks through, and the button is there. Before today the notification landed on a page with nothing to do. That is the same defect one level up from the one I fixed: the notice was built, the endpoint was built, and the two were never joined. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I asserted AC5 was open from the AC text plus the absence of any UI, without grepping the pipeline for a notify call. The lesson is the one this session kept re-learning in the other direction — I checked whether the ENDPOINT had a caller and correctly found none, then failed to run the same check on the NOTIFICATION and assumed. Absence of a caller is a thing you verify, not infer, in both directions. REMAINING ON THIS STORY: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path so a withdrawal produces a reviewer verdict) and AC6 (counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133). AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 all stand. | 2026-08-02 AC3 IS ALSO ALREADY DONE — checked rather than assumed this time, having just been wrong about AC5. POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve takes an outcome of upheld or rejected, refuses to re-resolve an already-closed appeal, and splits correctly: UPHELD withdraws the verdict permanently, REJECTED restores exactly what was hidden — with the reasoning stated inline that a reviewer finding an appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item, so the original stands rather than being re-derived. It reseals, updates the dispute status, and when plan.reviewerVerdict is set it feeds the outcome through the same review path so it counts toward accuracy and can be promoted, which is precisely what AC3 asked for. SO US-2145 STANDS AT: AC1 done (the contest button, this session — the only piece that was actually missing), AC2 done, AC3 done, AC4 done, AC5 done, AC6 outstanding and needing counsel on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133 per the AC itself. THE SHAPE OF THIS STORY IS WORTH KEEPING, because it is the clearest example of the pattern this whole session kept hitting: FIVE of six criteria were fully implemented — endpoint, hiding, reseal, reviewer path, notification — and the story read as untouched because the one missing piece was a button. Every file a reader would open to check suggested the feature shipped, and the seller still could not contest anything. The expensive halves were all built; the cheap half, the one a user touches, was not. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to any test that exercises the route directly, which is why it survived. RECOMMENDATION: close on AC1-AC5 and let AC6 travel with US-2133, or leave open pointing there — an owner call, and specifically not one I should make by writing a note that sounds like agreement on a story with a legal-review criterion.

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the grading pipeline to identify WHAT it is grading as rigorously as it grades CONDITION, and to cover the product categories sellers actually list, because today the two halves of the product are lopsided: the condition engine is deep (5 weighted factors, defect taxonomy with mm tolerances, fabric-aware criteria, confidence caps, shadow/eval/canary lifecycle) while identity is thin (brand and size on a certificate are whatever the seller typed) and coverage is clothing-only (a hat, a tie, a belt and a handbag all have a garment_category and no way to be graded).
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.
Identity work does not weaken US-346: label-read fields are server-derived and TRUSTED; seller-typed brand/size stay fenced and untrusted, and neither channel may move a factor score.
Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Epic] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Parent for US-2210..US-2225. Scope split six ways: tag identification (2210-2212), sizing (2213-2215), brand styles/models (2216-2217), authenticity evidence + coverage priority (2218-2219), brand breadth (2220-2221), product coverage beyond clothing (2222-2225). DELIBERATELY NOT DUPLICATED: US-2130..2148 already own the visual-authenticity epic (eval gate, golden set, capture quality, decoder cross-checks, tell depth/counterfeit modelling, appeals, accuracy tracking); US-1997 owns non-clothing rubric ACTIVATION for the three rubrics that already exist (sports_cards/watches/shoes) and its Phase-2 notes already scope the factor-set generalization every new rubric here depends on; US-2107 owns publishing measurable tolerances.

userStories.title: Android is a plumbing skeleton, but its README and 19 passing stories claim near-parity
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the Android backlog to reflect reality. Android has genuinely good infrastructure — auth, a Room sync engine, mutation queue, delete reconciliation, telemetry, app-lock, CameraX capture, ~70 Kotlin files. It has no product: every navigation destination except one is a literal placeholder (ui/shell/AppShell.kt:162-175 — Home, Inventory, Money, Marketplaces, Settings, Details intake, AutoLister all render SectionPlaceholder; only capture/photos is real). Corroborating: Android calls exactly ONE edge endpoint in the entire codebase (/api/flipdesk/photo-profiles) versus iOS's 77 and web's ~530 — no grading submit, no inventory read, no eBay, no payments. Two documentation problems compound it: android/README.md:31-39 presents a package map for grading / inventory / marketplaces / money / billing whose directories contain ZERO .kt files, and :3 calls it 'at iOS parity'. And 19 stories are marked passes:true with no implementing code — verified: US-1380 Glance widgets (zero 'glance' references anywhere, no AppWidgetProvider in the manifest), US-1378 FCM push (no FirebaseMessaging reference), US-1383 Settings (routes to a placeholder), US-1384/1385/1387/1388/1389, US-1393 localization (no values-* locale dirs). The pattern is clean: US-1300-1328 (infrastructure) are genuinely done; US-1378-1396 is a contiguous block marked done without code.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-open the falsely-passing Android stories (start with the verified list: US-1380, US-1378, US-1383, US-1384, US-1385, US-1387, US-1388, US-1389, US-1393) and audit the rest of the US-1378-1396 block the same way.
Correct android/README.md — remove the 'at iOS parity' claim and the package map for directories that contain no code. This is the first document a new engineer or a diligence reviewer reads.
Re-baseline the Android estimate: real completion is closer to 29/98 than the 48/98 the backlog implies, and ALL remaining work is the expensive UI/feature half rather than a polish pass.
Decide explicitly whether Android is on the launch plan. If it is, the remaining work is essentially the whole app.
userStories.notes: [P1][Android/Backlog-integrity] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. This is the same class as US-1996 (archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED) but larger and on a platform nobody is looking at. The state is more misleading than a plain stub would be: sophisticated offline-sync infrastructure attached to zero features reads as 'nearly done' to anyone who opens the project and sees the hard parts solved. NOT verified: whether the 50 OPEN Android stories are correctly open — only the passing ones were falsified. | [2026-07-27] AC1 DONE: audited the whole US-1378..1396 block, not just the verified subset — 14 stories re-opened as never-implemented (1378/1379/1380/1381/1382/1384/1385/1386/1387/1388/1389/1390/1392/1393) and 2 re-opened as partial (1391 has no signing config; 1395 has no androidTest/E2E). US-1383 was falsely passing and is now genuinely implemented. AC2 DONE: android/README.md no longer claims iOS parity, the package map lists only packages that contain code, and a Status section names what is and is not built. AC3 DONE: the table in that README is the re-baseline. userStories.title: In-place plan upgrade charges a prorated amount on a single click with no confirmation
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:326-380: if a user already has a subscription, clicking a higher tier calls stripe.subscriptions.update with proration_behavior: 'create_prorations' — charging immediately with NO Stripe Checkout page, no price confirmation, no interstitial and no disclosure. The click IS the purchase. Every other purchase path at least passes through Stripe's hosted checkout, which renders the recurring price; this one renders nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Show an explicit confirmation step before an in-place upgrade that states the prorated amount charged today, the new recurring amount, the new billing frequency, and the next renewal date.
Capture the same affirmative consent artifact as a new subscription.
Apply the same treatment to downgrades and interval switches if they charge or change terms.
Test asserting the upgrade mutation cannot fire without the confirmation step.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). A charge with no disclosure and no confirmation is the clearest Section 5 / ROSCA exposure in the codebase after the missing disclosures themselves. | 2026-07-19 SCOPED, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — and the reason is the story's own logic, not capacity. AC1 needs a confirmation stating the PRORATED AMOUNT CHARGED TODAY, the new recurring amount, the new frequency and the next renewal date. Those numbers do not exist anywhere yet: payments.ts has fetchUpcomingInvoice (US-400) but that returns the CURRENT subscription's upcoming invoice, not a simulation of what a CHANGE would cost. Getting the real figure needs Stripe's proration preview — invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the PROPOSED subscription_items plus a subscription_proration_date — which is a new endpoint, and one whose output I cannot verify from this sandbox (the Stripe MCP connector is unauthorized; see US-2033, blocked the same way). WHY THAT BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOWS: a confirmation dialog that states a WRONG prorated amount is worse than the current no-dialog state. Today the defect is an OMISSION — the click is the purchase and nothing is stated. A dialog showing an unverified number converts that into an AFFIRMATIVE MISSTATEMENT about a charge, on the exact surface this compliance batch exists to fix. That is the same reasoning applied in US-2117 (refuse to write a partial agreement), US-2119 (refuse to send a notice with no date) and US-2116 (refuse to record a client-supplied IP): on an evidentiary or money surface, a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an acknowledged gap. WHAT THE NEXT PASS NEEDS, so it is short: (1) a preview endpoint wrapping invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the target plan's price id, returning prorated-now / new-recurring / interval / next-renewal; (2) a confirmation dialog — DowngradePreviewDialog is the established pattern to mirror, and AC3's 'apply the same treatment to downgrades' is already satisfied by it, which is why upgrades being bare is the anomaly rather than the norm; (3) route the upgrade mutation through it; (4) AC4's test that the mutation cannot fire without confirmation. AC2 (capture the same consent artifact as a new subscription) is now CHEAP because US-2117 landed: subscription_agreements + recordAgreedTerms already exist, and an in-place upgrade produces a customer.subscription.updated event that already flows through handleSubscriptionChange — which now calls recordAgreedTerms. So an upgrade ALREADY writes an agreement row with the new plan/interval/amount. Worth verifying rather than assuming, but the plumbing is in place. The FIGURES are the blocker, and they need a Stripe session — not more code reading. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h); edge unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno), CI + a real Stripe test env confirm. The in-place upgrade (payments.ts /flipdesk/subscribe, existing paid sub → higher tier) called stripe.subscriptions.update with create_prorations on a single click — no disclosure, no consent. AC1: new POST /flipdesk/upgrade-preview computes the real proration via stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming (simulating the item swap with subscription_items + subscription_proration_behavior) and returns amount_due_today_cents, currency, new_recurring_cents, interval, next_renewal_at (current_period_end). AC4 (server-enforced, the strong guarantee): the in-place path now refuses unless the body carries confirmUpgrade:true — returns 409 { code:'UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED', requiresConfirmation:true } and does NOT mutate; the gate sits BEFORE subscriptions.update. AC2: on a confirmed change it writes a consent artifact to flipdesk_subscription_events (event_type 'in_place_change_confirmed', from/to plan, raw_payload with prices+interval+source) — the equivalent of Checkout's disclosure. Web: new UpgradePreviewDialog (mirrors the existing DowngradePreviewDialog) fetches the preview and discloses amount today / new recurring rate+frequency / next renewal before confirming; the plan picker's upgrade CTA opens it for a paid→higher change and calls subscribe with confirmUpgrade:true on confirm. A free→paid upgrade still goes straight to Stripe Checkout (which discloses on its own hosted page), so it skips the dialog. AC3: downgrades already route through DowngradePreviewDialog and interval switches through the Stripe billing portal (both disclose/confirm) — the upgrade path was the only gap, now closed. TESTS: edge upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts asserts (source-structural, this repo's idiom for Stripe-heavy routes — cf. subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts) that the confirmUpgrade gate precedes the mutation, the preview endpoint + retrieveUpcoming exist, and the consent artifact is written; all 10 assertions verified green by replicating them in node against payments.ts. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b + eslint clean; billing+hooks vitest 36/36 green; only flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog uses useFlipdeskSubscribe and only use-billing-summary calls the endpoint, so no other caller now 409s. KEPT passes:false: the edge route + the Stripe preview call are not runnable here (no deno, no Stripe test key); run the deno lane + exercise a real paid→higher upgrade against Stripe test mode to confirm the prorated amount + consent row, then flip.

userStories.title: No advance renewal reminder exists anywhere — annual plans are charged silently
userStories.description: Confirmed absence, verified three ways: invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch (services/edge-functions/src/routes/webhooks.ts:244-281, falls through to a default log-and-drop at :281); no cron in jobs-cron-fleet.ts sends one; and the only upcoming_invoice reference is a read-only pull for the billing page (payments.ts:1142). The first notice a user receives about a renewal is sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail (email.ts:1183), sent AFTER the money is taken. Yearly price IDs exist for all five paid tiers (src/lib/constants.ts:1344-1366) and flow through the identical path — interval only changes a display string — so an annual subscriber is charged a full year's fee with no prior contact whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.upcoming and send a transactional advance renewal notice stating the amount, the date of the charge, the plan, and how to cancel before it.
Configure the Stripe lead time explicitly rather than relying on the default, and set a longer lead for annual plans than monthly.
Send via deliverEmail as a TRANSACTIONAL category — it must not be routed through the drip/marketing engine where opt-out, suppression or frequency caps can silently drop it.
Also handle customer.subscription.trial_will_end.
Test that an annual subscription produces a reminder before renewal and that a marketing opt-out does not suppress it.

Cheapest structural fix in the batch: one webhook case reusing existing email infrastructure. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 + AC4 + AC5 DONE (mechanism, not copy — the fourth compliance story that did not need counsel). invoice.upcoming is now HANDLED and sends sendRenewalReminderEmail, a NEW template deliberately separate from sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail: a receipt confirms something that happened, this warns about something that has not, and the only action that matters — cancel before the date — is meaningless on a receipt. It states the plan, the amount, the exact charge date and how to cancel. AC3: category subscription_renewal_reminder is registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES, so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional even if marketing:true is explicitly requested — pinned by a test, because if that ever flips, an opt-out silently drops the only advance warning of a charge and the exact defect returns. AC4 customer.subscription.trial_will_end is handled too, and THE DISJOINTNESS IS THE INTERESTING PART: our signup trial has NO Stripe subscription (handle_new_user grants it directly), and US-2120's cron filters flipdesk_subscription_id IS NULL. This event fires only for a STRIPE-managed trial — someone who started a PAID subscription with a trial period — which is exactly the user that cron skips. The two populations cannot overlap, so neither path double-sends. A test asserts the cron keeps that filter, since removing it would make both fire for the same person. It reuses sendTrialExpiringEmail rather than minting a second trial template, because two near-identical trial emails drift. DECLINES TO SEND WITHOUT A DATE: if Stripe supplies neither next_payment_attempt nor period_end the handler returns. (2) Removing them left an ORPHANED group header ('Covered by their own stories / other handlers.') heading an empty group — deleted. That is a Stripe dashboard/API setting, not code: Stripe decides when invoice.upcoming fires, and the default is 3 days. Worth doing since a 3-day warning on a full YEAR's charge is thin, but it cannot be set from here. Verified: edge 4306 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE (US-2089-style stale box). This story's premise — 'invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch' — is no longer true: webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to handleInvoiceUpcoming (:284) AND customer.subscription.trial_will_end to handleTrialWillEnd (:294), both carrying US-2119 attribution comments. NOT marking passes:true from here, because I did not verify AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time configuration, which is a dashboard setting) or AC5's live test — someone with Stripe access should confirm those two before closing. | 2026-07-22 ADDED THE MISSING AC3/AC5 GUARD (agent loop), passes:false held on the external ACs. The prior note flagged that it "did not verify AC5"; the transactional half of AC5 (and AC3) had NO test at all — sendRenewalReminderEmail uses category subscription_renewal_reminder (email.ts:2936) which IS in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts:49), so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional and a marketing opt-out cannot suppress it — but nothing pinned that. userStories.title: iOS paywall advertises 1,000 AI actions for Pro; the server grants 750
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Billing/IAPProduct.swift:88,93 advertises Pro as '1,000 listings · 1,000 AI actions · 30 grades · AutoLister'. Both the server catalog (services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/products.ts:75,80) and web (src/lib/constants.ts:243, aiActionsPerMonth: 750) say 750. iOS buyers are sold 1,000 AI actions and will be plan-gated at 750 — a paid-for entitlement that does not exist. The drift test that should catch this (iap-catalog-drift_test.ts:69-106) compares ids, credits, plan/interval and fallbackPrice but NOT blurb or title, so the guard has a hole exactly where the misleading copy lives.
acceptanceCriteria: Correct the iOS copy to match the entitlement actually granted (or change the entitlement — but the two must agree).
Extend iap-catalog-drift_test.ts to compare user-facing blurb and title against the server catalog, so advertised entitlements cannot drift from granted ones.
Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.

userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing
userStories.description: Authenticity verdicts (likely_authentic / inconclusive / red_flags) are shown on public certificates and returned from an unauthenticated public endpoint, currently with no accuracy gate behind them. Separately, the seeded brand KB was written to REFUSE authentication — 00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql:14 reads 'NEVER auto-authenticate... A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.
Reconcile the brand-KB 'never auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture.

Check eBay policy exposure: grade-badge.ts is already dead because eBay bans grade overlays on listing imagery, and eBay runs its own Authenticity Guarantee — determine what may be stated on a listing before building listing-facing surfaces.
Confirm the unauthenticated public endpoint should expose verdicts at all.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Legal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Pairs with the FTC Section 5 batch (US-2114..2128) — same substantiation problem, different claim. Do not let an agent draft the claim language. ACCURACY GATE 2026-07-19 (decided: adopt the conservative posture ahead of counsel): the public /tools/authenticity-check endpoint now requires a PASSING eval run in addition to PUBLIC_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_ENABLED. CORRECTION to an earlier characterisation of the exposure: that endpoint was ALREADY fail-closed behind the env flag (default off) and documented as awaiting legal review of the limitations copy — so the risk was lower than described. What was missing is that the env flag is the LEGAL gate (a human read the copy) and says nothing about whether the model is any good; enabling it after a legal review should not be sufficient to publish verdicts from a prompt version that has never cleared the golden set. The two gates are now separate and both required. Authenticated surfaces (paid add-on, buyer check) deliberately still run ungated — they carry the limitations disclaimer and a named account, a different posture from an anonymous public claim. Returns 503 + Retry-After rather than 404 so a crawler does not deindex the tool page behind it. 4431 edge tests pass.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. The prompt requests evidence the capture flow never collects. This is the cheapest single improvement to authenticity signal quality.
acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.
Feed slot presence into the authenticity confidence: absent macro evidence should lower confidence and widen limitations, not be silently ignored.
Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).
Update the prompt so it asks only for what the available slots can actually support.

When unblocked, the sanctioned route is the additive/flag-gated pattern the skill describes: a macro-awareness block that suffixes prompt_version (mirroring authenticity_v1+tells) and is byte-identical when disabled, test-guarded.

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.
