userStories.title: Returns and Disputes: refunds are all-or-nothing and there is no closed/history view
userStories.description: As a reseller handling returns, I want to issue a partial refund and review resolved cases, so I can offer keep-it discounts and audit past outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: refundReturn in src/pages/flipdesk/post-sale.tsx accepts a refund amount and issues a partial refund through the existing eBay post-order refund edge route, not only a full refund
A partial refund amount is validated to be greater than 0 and no more than the order total
Each of the three cards (disputes, returns, cancellations) gains a closed/resolved view showing past outcomes, not only open items
A test asserts a partial-refund request sends the entered amount to the edge route
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC3 DONE for Returns, and it turned out to be a DEFECT rather than a missing view. The card fetched every return eBay returned, applied NO filter, rendered them all with Approve / Decline / Refund buttons, and said "No open returns." when the list was empty. So a case eBay had already closed was indistinguishable from one waiting on the seller — with a destructive action attached whose own confirm text reads "This issues a refund to the buyer on eBay immediately. This can't be undone." The edge degrades gracefully (isAlreadyResolved swallows eBay's rejection) so this was not losing money; it was showing a seller work that did not exist and hiding the work that did among it. SHIPPED: NEW src/pages/flipdesk/post-sale-state.ts with isClosedCase / splitByOpenState, the returns card split into open/closed with a toggle that only appears when there IS history, and the action row hidden on closed cases. THE CLASSIFIER IS A SUBSTRING MATCH, NOT AN ENUM, and that is deliberate: eBay's Post-Order state vocabulary is not published anywhere in this repo — the only values recorded are three examples in an ebay-postorder.ts comment — so an exhaustive enum would be guessing, and a guessed enum fails SILENTLY the first time eBay sends something unanticipated. THE DEFAULT IS OPEN, and the asymmetry is the whole design: mis-classifying an open case as closed HIDES work the seller must do before an eBay deadline with no way to discover it; mis-classifying a closed case as open shows one extra row whose buttons become a no-op. The first costs a case, the second costs a glance. THE ONE TRAP IN THE WORD LIST, pinned by its own test: REFUND is deliberately NOT a terminal marker on its own, because REFUND_OVERDUE is an OPEN case and the most urgent kind there is — a refund the seller owes and has not issued. Matching the bare word would bury exactly the row that most needs action. AC1/AC2/AC4 NOT DONE, and the reason is a finding rather than effort. AC1 says refundReturn should issue a partial refund "through the existing eBay post-order refund edge route". There are TWO routes and they are different eBay flows: /returns/:returnId/refund calls issueReturnRefund(ownerId, returnId, comments) and takes NO amount — eBay's return-refund closes the return in full — while /orders/:orderId/refund is the partial/proactive one (US-1978) and already accepts amount and line_items. So the capability exists, but on the ORDER, and US-1978's own header says it is for refunds "outside any return case", written for the seller who wanted to make it right without pushing the buyer into opening a return. Using it to settle an OPEN return is outside its designed use, and whether eBay permits an order-level partial refund while a return case is open is not knowable from this checkout. Getting that wrong moves money incorrectly, possibly twice. That needs an answer about eBay's semantics before it is a UI change, and I did not guess it. AC3 for cancellations and payment disputes is left too — the helper reads `status` as well as `state` precisely so one rule covers all three cards, so wiring them is small, but each needs its own look at which actions must disappear on a closed case. VERIFIED: 8 new classifier tests, 108 flipdesk tests pass, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 AC3 NOW COMPLETE — all three cards. Disputes and cancellations had the IDENTICAL defect to Returns, which is the part worth recording: this was not one card someone forgot to filter, it was the same mistake made three times independently, because each card was written to answer "what needs my attention" and each one shipped the raw list instead. On Payment disputes it was the worst of the three: Accept & refund and Contest rendered against a respond-by deadline that had already passed, on a dispute eBay had already decided — Accept refunds the buyer, and Contest is meaningless once a decision exists. On Cancellations, Approve & cancel and Reject on a request already settled. Both now split open/closed with the same toggle, both hide their action rows on closed cases, and both empty states say which view is empty. The classifier needed no change to cover them, which is why it reads `status` as well as `state` — disputes carry the former, returns and cancellations the latter, and one rule across all three is the only way they stay consistent as eBay's vocabulary shifts. THE TOGGLE ONLY APPEARS WHEN THERE IS HISTORY, on all three: a "Show closed (0)" button teaches nothing and adds a control to a card whose whole job is to be scannable. STILL OPEN ON THIS STORY: AC1, AC2 and AC4, all three about partial refunds, and blocked on the eBay-semantics question recorded in the previous note rather than on effort — the return-refund route takes no amount, and the order-refund route that does is documented as being for refunds outside any return case. VERIFIED: full web suite 247 files / 3150 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors.

userStories.title: MeasureCard is a brochure with no path into the actual measure flow
userStories.description: As a reseller reading the MeasureCard page, I want a button into the measure tool and a sample of the finished result, so the page leads to the capability it describes instead of dead-ending.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/flipdesk/measure-card.tsx adds a primary CTA linking into the item measure surface
The page shows a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo
The mailed-card status surfaces an ETA and, once shipped, a tracking number (today only a date, lines 199-206)
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC1 DONE; AC2 and AC3 recorded as blocked with the reason, not attempted. AC1: measure-card.tsx gains a "Measure an item" card with a primary CTA into /dashboard/flipdesk/inventory?status=cataloged. THE DIAGNOSIS BEHIND THE FIX, because the story's title undersells it: every control on that page produced an ARTEFACT — a PDF to print, a card to be mailed — and not one of them led to the thing the artefact is FOR. A seller who read the whole page still had to already know that measuring happens on an item, and where to find one. That is the specific shape of "brochure": not missing content, missing a next step. TWO CHOICES IN THE LINK WORTH STATING. It points at ?status=cataloged rather than the inventory root, so the seller lands on pre-listed items — the set that actually needs measuring — instead of their entire catalog; statusParamToTab folds cataloged / measured / photographed into the To-list tab, so one status param reaches the right view. And it uses ?status= rather than ?tab= deliberately: status is the documented EXTERNAL entry point that the Overview pipeline grid and the Kanban "+N more" links already use, tab is the table's internal view key, and the mapping function exists precisely so external links survive a tab rename. AC2 NOT DONE — it asks for a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo. That is an image asset. Producing it needs the measure pipeline run against a real garment with a real card in frame, and a judgement about whose item is safe to show publicly. Same class as US-1949 AC1: a human with the product open, not a code change. AC3 NOT DONE, and it splits. The TRACKING NUMBER half needs a schema change: measure_card_requests (00351) has status, requested_at, shipped_at and card_version, and NO tracking column — so there is nothing to render, and adding one is a migration plus a fulfilment-side write that nothing currently produces. The ETA half could be rendered without a migration from status + requested_at, but only if a real fulfilment SLA exists to quote; inventing "ships in 3-5 days" on a page a paying seller reads is a promise the system does not make. Both need an answer about the fulfilment process before they are code. VERIFIED: build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 100 flipdesk tests pass. | 2026-08-08 AC3's TRACKING HALF DONE. AC2 and AC3's ETA half stay open, both for the reasons the previous note gave and neither has changed. The previous pass split AC3 correctly and I built the half that was buildable. NEW migration 00561_measure_card_tracking.sql adds tracking_number and tracking_carrier to measure_card_requests; the operator queue can record them on the shipped transition, and the seller's own /card-request read returns them. BOTH COLUMNS ARE NULLABLE, and that is the design rather than laziness: cards are mailed by hand and many go out as untracked letters. NOT NULL would either stop the operator marking those shipped at all or push them to type a placeholder, and a PLACEHOLDER TRACKING NUMBER IS WORSE THAN AN EMPTY ONE, because the seller clicks it. The route never writes an empty string for the same reason - a test forbids the `tracking || ""` fallback specifically. THE REFUSAL THAT MATTERS, and the reason this needed more than a column. The bulk status route takes up to 500 ids; tracking is per-PARCEL. Sending a number with a batch would stamp ONE carrier reference onto every seller in it, and each would then see a link tracking somebody else's parcel - worse than no tracking, because it looks authoritative. The route refuses it (400) rather than trusting the caller, and refuses tracking on the 'exported' transition too, which would record a parcel that has not been sent. PLAINTEXT, DECIDED NOT DEFAULTED. US-2417 (same session) encrypts ship_name/address_line1/ address_line2/city/postal_code on this exact table because they say where a person lives. A tracking number is a carrier's identifier for a parcel, the operator must search and paste it, and it is the one field on the row the SELLER is meant to read back. Same reasoning that keeps state and country readable there. A GUARD AGAINST AN INTERACTION I WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE MISSED: the seller summary has deliberately never echoed the address (US-1579), and since US-2417 those columns are ciphertext - so adding a field to that summary is now a place where a careless change would BOTH undo a privacy decision and return unreadable data. A test asserts the summary still omits ship_name, address_line1 and postal_code. 4 cases in NEW src/tests/measure-card-tracking_test.ts, comments stripped before every assertion. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the batch guard removed, the shipped-only guard removed, and the empty-string fallback introduced. Each reddened with its own message; route restored and re-run green. VERIFIED: migration applied from clean AND re-applied (idempotent), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00561 with the manifest regenerated in the same pass, deno check + deno lint clean across 1426 files, full edge suite 6003 passed / 0 failed. 00561 is HELD and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md with the apply-before-edge-deploy direction: the edge SELECTs both columns by name, so an edge-first deploy answers 42703 and breaks the MeasureCard panel for EVERY seller, not just those with tracking.

userStories.title: Listing Performance: decorative refresh icon, no KPI tiles, no pagination or search
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want a real Sync now button, top-line KPIs, and a searchable paged table on Listing Performance, so I am not stuck waiting six hours behind a fake refresh icon or scrolling a thousand rows.
acceptanceCriteria: The RefreshCw element in src/pages/flipdesk/listing-performance.tsx (lines 263-267) becomes a working Sync now button that triggers the eBay traffic sync and reflects progress
The page shows aggregate KPI tiles (total views, average CTR, percent stale)
The table paginates and supports title search server-side rather than limit(1000) plus a client filter (line 145)
No unbounded read is introduced, honoring the US-2168 and US-2169 read contract
userStories.notes: Partial 2026-07-28. LANDED AC1: new user-scoped edge route POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/sync/performance/me (services/edge-functions/src/routes/flipdesk-ebay.ts) reusing syncListingPerformanceForUser(ownerId) — tenant-scoped (owner from JWT, no body id, US-268), with a tenant-isolation_test.ts no-auth case; the decorative RefreshCw in src/pages/flipdesk/listing-performance.tsx is now a real 'Sync now' button (spinner + toast + query invalidation). LANDED AC2: three KPI tiles (total views, avg CTR, % stale) computed across all active listings. LANDED partial AC3: title search box + 50-per-page client pagination + a US-2169 'showing first 1000' truncation notice. NOT DONE AC3/AC4 (server-side): the read is still .select(...).limit(1000) + client filter (line ~145) — search/sort/pagination remain client-side because the KPI tiles need the full set; genuinely server-side paging requires a server aggregate RPC for the KPIs + server-side listing_title search (mind the inventory_items.title fallback). Verified: frontend tsc+eslint clean; deno check + deno lint clean; tenant-isolation suite 17 passed / 0 failed with the new case. | 2026-08-08 A USER-VISIBLE BUG FOUND AND FIXED, plus the AC3/AC4 database half written and verified but DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED YET. Read the bug first, because it is the part that was actively lying to sellers. THE STORY'S OWN PREMISE IS STALE, AND THE STALENESS SHIPPED. AC3 says the read is '.limit(1000) plus a client filter (line 145)'. It is not - US-2169 replaced that with fetchAllPages, which advances by the rows actually returned and fetches the WHOLE set. What survived that change was `const truncated = listings.length >= 1000` and the notice it drives: 'Showing the first 1,000 active listings. Use search or the no-views filters to narrow down the rest.' So EVERY seller with 1,000 or more active listings was told their report was cut short, and pointed at a workaround for a problem that no longer existed. A UI claiming missing data is worse than one silent about complete data: it sends the person hunting for rows already on screen. Both the flag and the notice are gone, with a comment naming fetchCapped as the shape to use if a cap ever returns - it asks for one row past the cap, so `truncated` is a FACT rather than a guess from a length that no longer means what it did. AC4 IS ALREADY SATISFIED and the story does not know it: fetchAllPages IS the US-2169 read contract, so there is no unbounded read to introduce. What remains under AC3 is not boundedness, it is that the browser holds every active listing in memory to compute three tiles. NEW MIGRATION 00560_listing_performance_rpcs.sql, HELD AND UNAPPLIED. Two SECURITY INVOKER functions - the default, chosen and stated: they run as the CALLING role, so the existing RLS on listings and inventory_items scopes them and there is no tenant filter inside to get wrong, and nothing for US-2282's grant guard to carry. flipdesk_listing_performance_summary() returns the KPI figures plus last_synced_at; flipdesk_listing_performance_page(...) returns one searched, sorted, paged page with total_count riding on each row, so the caller gets the page AND the page count in one round trip (a separate count query is a second read that can disagree with the page it labels). TWO CORRECTNESS WINS THAT ARE NOT ABOUT SPEED. (1) The title fallback - blank listing_title resolves to the inventory item's title - moves into the query, so SEARCH NOW COVERS IT. The client-side search matched listing_title only and silently missed every listing whose DISPLAYED title came from the item, which is a wrong answer rather than a slow one. (2) The ILIKE pattern is escaped, so a seller searching a title containing % or _ matches literally instead of wildcarding. Proven both ways: a search for '50%' returned exactly the one title containing a literal percent sign. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL POSTGRES, not by reading. Applied from clean and then RE-APPLIED (idempotent). Two bugs the database found that a review would not have: view_trend_7d is jsonb, not numeric, and CREATE OR REPLACE cannot change a return type once the summary gained last_synced_at - so the file now carries a signature-scoped DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS, which is what re-runnable has to mean against a database holding either shape. A THIRD bug I caught before applying: with p_sort = 'title' the numeric CASE still fell through to `ELSE views_total`, so a title sort would have ordered by views and used the title only as a tiebreak. Guarded and then proven - Zebra Coat with 999 views sorts BELOW Alpha Shirt with 1 view under title ASC. BEHAVIOURAL PROOF with two seeded sellers: A's results never included B's listing (RLS scoping through SECURITY INVOKER, measured rather than assumed), the title fallback resolved, the no-view window filtered, total_count was correct under limit 1 offset 1, an unknown sort key fell back instead of erroring, prosecdef = false on both, anon has no EXECUTE and authenticated/service_role do. WHY IT IS HELD RATHER THAN APPLIED: its CALLER does not exist yet. Applying it now would put two functions in prod that nothing invokes - the exact shape US-1995 recorded, a half that ships without its other half and then reads as done. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md says so, with the required NOTIFY pgrst reload (without it PostgREST 404s the new RPC and it looks like a bug in the page). REMAINING, and it is the frontend half only: replace the fetchAllPages query and the separate chunked titles query with rpc('flipdesk_listing_performance_page'), drive the KPI tiles and the 'last synced' header from rpc('flipdesk_listing_performance_summary'), delete the client-side filter/sort/slice, take pageCount from total_count, and reset page to 0 when search, sort or the no-view chip changes. The RPC already supports every sort key the page offers, including title and days_listed (as listed_at). VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, schema-version guard green (EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00560, manifest regenerated in the same pass, 18 passed / 0 failed). | 2026-08-08 (same day, second pass) AC3 AND AC4 NOW DONE. The frontend half that the previous note listed as remaining is wired, so 00560 is no longer a migration without a caller. WHAT CHANGED IN listing-performance.tsx: the fetchAllPages read over every active eBay listing is gone, the separate chunked titles query is gone, and the client-side decorate/filter/sort/slice is gone. One rpc('flipdesk_listing_performance_page') returns the fifty rows on screen; one rpc('flipdesk_listing_performance_summary') feeds the three KPI tiles and the 'last synced' header. The chunked titles query alone cost a 900-listing catalog NINE extra round trips on every load, because a single .in() with hundreds of UUIDs overflowed the request URL. The LEFT JOIN in SQL removes all of them. FOUR THINGS THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG IN A SERVER-PAGING SWITCH, all pinned by tests: (1) THE QUERY KEY carries search, noViewDays, sortKey, sortDir and page. Omit one and TanStack serves the first page's cache for the second — which presents as 'paging is broken' rather than 'the key is wrong', and is much harder to find from the symptom. (2) A PAGE RESET on every input change. Without it a seller on page 9 who narrows the search lands on an empty page and reads it as 'search found nothing'. (3) days_listed INVERTS the direction it sends. It is derived — more days listed means an OLDER listed_at — so passing sortDir through unchanged silently runs the one sort a seller uses to find stale stock backwards, while still looking like a sorted table. (4) COUNTS COME FROM total_count, never from pageRows.length, which caps at PAGE_SIZE and would read '50' forever on any catalog above one page. The pager's upper bound clamps to total, since the last page is usually short. TWO OF MY OWN MISTAKES, both worth recording because they are environmental rather than logical. The file is MIXED CRLF/LF — original lines CRLF, lines added this session LF — so a patch script matching plain \n silently applied only to its own lines and reported success. Every pattern is \r?\n now. And a bash `node -e` with backticks in the string got eaten by the shell, which is the rule this session already wrote down for prd.json notes and I broke for source: any script containing backticks goes in a temp .mjs file, never in a bash-quoted -e. userStories.title: iOS: the item's own columns don't own their eBay specifics, so changing Size edits nothing the listing will publish
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want changing Size or Color on the item to update the eBay item specific too, so that I don't have to open Category & Specifics and type the same value a second time.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a structured column (brand/size/color/material/style) on the iOS item editor updates that column's eBay aspect even when the aspect's provenance is ai_extracted or manual. Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects builds a 'preserve' map of every manual/aiExtracted aspect and passes it as 'known', so the AI-filled Size survives and the seller's new Size is discarded - the opposite of the documented contract that the columns OWN those five aspects (see the web helper projectColumnAspects in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts and its tests).

The save writes BOTH aspect stores, not just one: inventory_items.ebay_aspects (+ebay_aspect_sources) AND listings.item_specifics_override (+item_specifics_sources) for this item's listing row. Today the save-time path writes only the inventory_items pair; item_specifics_override is written ONLY by SpecificsEditorModel (the Category & Specifics editor), which is exactly why the seller has to go there for the change to stick - it is the copy publish/revise reads FIRST.

The projection runs even when the item has no eBay category selected yet. Today reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id, so column values set before a category is picked never reach the aspect stores.

The projection is a PURE local function (a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects: non-empty column overwrites its aspect and stamps provenance inventory_derived; a blanked column clears it), not a server round trip. Today every save calls EbayAspectsService.deriveAspects, so a save costs a network call and a transient failure silently no-ops via try?.

An XCTest asserts the three rules directly: an ai_extracted Size aspect IS overwritten by a changed Size column; a non-column aspect (e.g. Department, Pattern) is left untouched; and a cleared column clears its aspect.

A deno or vitest drift guard asserts the iOS column-to-aspect name mapping matches the web/edge registry (services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-registry.ts, vendored to src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json), so the two platforms cannot disagree on which aspect a column owns.

Publish still re-normalizes against the real category spec server-side (forceColumnAspects / COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK in flipdesk-ebay.ts), so a raw column value outside eBay's allowed list is still corrected at publish - this story does not change that.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-03 WARNING, READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: AC4 and AC5 as written would re-open a bug fixed on 2026-08-02 (commit ea9e27a2). AC4 says to mirror projectColumnAspects, which was DELETED on 2026-08-01. Its replacement, projectColumnAspectsForSpec in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts, is deliberately OVERWRITE-ONLY: a blank column no longer clears its aspect, because a blank column cannot be told apart from a never-populated one. Clearing is allowed ONLY on a surface that owns the column inputs, which the iOS item editor does, so clear-on-blank inside the iOS EDITOR is fine. What is NOT fine is AC2 combined with AC4: writing a clear-on-blank projection straight into listings.item_specifics_override, the store the publish check reads FIRST. A blank Brand column carrying an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ordinary state of an iOS-created item, and deleting it there is exactly the reported failure: Brand plainly visible in the specifics editor while publish refuses with "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand". Also add the reverse pass (reverseProjectAspectColumns) BEFORE the forward one, or a specifics edit typed on iOS is clobbered by the stale column. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract.

userStories.title: Lock down SECURITY DEFINER functions: revoke EXECUTE from PUBLIC across public schema
userStories.description: Postgres grants EXECUTE on every new function to PUBLIC by default. No migration in supabase/migrations/ ever revokes it, and no `REVOKE ... ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC` exists anywhere. Because these functions are SECURITY DEFINER they run as the owner and bypass RLS, so any holder of the anon key can call them directly through PostgREST. grant_grade_credits and debit_grade_credits carry no GRANT/REVOKE statements at all; the revenue-dashboard functions (00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:273-274) grant to authenticated and service_role but never revoke the implicit PUBLIC grant. Impact: mint yourself unlimited grade credits, drain another user's credit balance, and read the full revenue and customer roster anonymously.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration revokes EXECUTE on all existing public-schema functions from PUBLIC, then re-grants explicitly to the roles each function actually needs.
`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC` so future functions are closed by default.
Every SECURITY DEFINER function is inventoried with its intended caller role; credit-mutating functions (grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, refund/reserve variants) are service_role only.
A test or CI check fails if a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships without an explicit grant block.
Migration triple honoured: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
Run `SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef;` against prod before and after and record both in the story.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. Pairs with the guard_users_protected_columns gap — either one alone gives free grading. Fix both together. | 2026-08-04 BLOCKED on US-2403, with the migration WRITTEN AND VERIFIED. Two findings, and the first one means the fix as the story describes it would have done NOTHING. (1) THE STORY'S DIAGNOSIS IS HALF WRONG. It says Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default and no migration revokes it. Reading pg_proc.proacl on a live stack says otherwise: grant_grade_credits carries {postgres=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres} — DIRECT grants to anon and authenticated, granted by postgres, from Supabase's own ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES bootstrap (confirmed in pg_default_acl for both postgres and supabase_admin on schema public, objtype 'f'). PUBLIC does not appear in the ACL at all. So 'REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC' is a NO-OP on exactly the functions the story names. I wrote that version first, applied it, and measured: grant_grade_credits/debit_grade_credits/revenue_dashboard still showed anon_can=t. A migration that looks like a security fix and changes nothing is worse than none, and the only reason I caught it is that I queried the ACLs instead of trusting the revoke. (2) THE CORRECTED MIGRATION IS WRITTEN AND PASSES EVERY CHECK, and is parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED (the suffix is deliberate — apply-prod-migrations.sh globs *.sql, so the rename is what stops an accidental apply). It revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon AND authenticated on every non-extension function in public, closes the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES that keeps re-granting them, grants service_role everything (the edge calls 48), and then REPLAYS the grants migrations actually made — 43 names for authenticated, 4 for anon, PARSED out of every GRANT EXECUTE statement in the corpus minus any later explicit REVOKE, not authored by judgement. Plus is_admin/is_super_admin/is_reviewer_or_admin explicitly, because a function called inside an RLS policy runs as the QUERYING role and is_admin appears in 29 migrations' policies while having NEVER had a grant — it worked only on the default this removes. Extension functions are excluded via pg_depend deptype 'e' so pg_trgm (installed into public by 00224) keeps its operators. MEASURED AFTER APPLYING, on a fresh stack: all 527 apply from zero; ZERO of the 28 client-callable RPCs (parsed from src/ + ios/ call sites) lost authenticated EXECUTE; grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, grant_api_credits, admin_adjust_credits, revoke_grade_credits and reserve_ai_action are now f/f/t (anon no, authenticated no, service_role yes); revenue_dashboard and system_health keep authenticated because their own migrations explicitly granted it, and lose anon; similarity/show_trgm still callable by PUBLIC. (3) WHY IT IS NOT SHIPPING: verifying the behaviour crashed the database. On this image any function-permission denial for a role in supautils.hint_roles (anon, authenticated, service_role) segfaults the backend. Filed as US-2403 with the isolation. 00527 does not cause it — refund_grade has been revoked since 00048 and crashes identically — but it would take the crashable surface from a handful of RPCs to ~80. REMAINING ACs when unblocked: AC4 (a CI check that a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships with an explicit grant block) is NOT written; AC6 (proname/proacl before and after against PROD) is an operator read. | 2026-08-08 AC4 DONE. AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 stay parked in 00527_...sql.BLOCKED behind US-2403; AC6 is an operator read against prod. AC4 was the half that never needed either, and it is now written: NEW src/test/security-definer-grants.test.ts. WHAT IT ENFORCES: every CALLABLE SECURITY DEFINER function in the migration corpus must be named by an explicit GRANT EXECUTE or REVOKE somewhere. Silence is not 'closed' on this stack - it is 'open to anon and authenticated', per the pg_proc.proacl reading in the note above - so a function that states nothing has been granted to the browser by a default nobody wrote down, on the one construct in the schema that deliberately bypasses RLS. TRIGGER FUNCTIONS ARE EXEMPT, and that is a real distinction, not a convenience: a RETURNS trigger function is invoked by the trigger machinery as part of the firing statement and EXECUTE is never consulted. 15 of the 83 are that shape. MY OWN FIRST PARSER PRODUCED EXACTLY THE MISCLASSIFICATION THE TEST EXISTS TO PREVENT, and the guard-the-guard is what caught it. Draft one read a fixed 2500-character window after each CREATE FUNCTION. From grant_grade_credits (00037:180) that window runs straight into handle_new_user (00037:233), whose RETURNS TRIGGER made a CREDIT-GRANTING RPC read as an exempt trigger function - so the single function US-2282 had measured carrying EXECUTE for anon on a live database would have been waved through by its own guard. Fixed by bounding each definition at the NEXT CREATE FUNCTION rather than by a character count. Two landmark assertions (a known callable, two known triggers) are what failed; without them the file would have shipped green and wrong. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE COUNTS THAT ONLY THE FIXED PARSER COULD SHOW: 83 distinct SECURITY DEFINER functions, not 86, and 15 trigger functions, not 19 - the extra 4 were non-SECURITY-DEFINER helpers (set_updated_at among them) swept up by the bleeding window. THE DEBT IS ENUMERATED, NOT TOLERATED: 18 callable SECURITY DEFINER functions say nothing about who may execute them. Seven move money or credits (grant_grade_credits, grant_api_credits, debit_api_credits, grant_appstore_credits, grant_buyer_reward_credit, issue_buyer_reward_credit, redeem_buyer_reward_credit) and three are the RLS predicates themselves (is_admin, is_reviewer_or_admin, is_super_admin) - which is the sharper problem, because a function called inside an RLS policy runs as the QUERYING role, so is_admin has always worked ONLY because of the default this debt describes, and hand-revoking it would break 29 migrations' policies at once. That is what 00527 handles as one atomic replay; the list says so, so nobody picks these off one at a time. The list is SHRINK-ONLY in both directions: a name that gains a grant or revoke FAILS the test until its entry is deleted in the same commit, and a name that stops being a SECURITY DEFINER function fails too. So the ground gained cannot be quietly given back, and the list cannot rot into a place where things go to be forgotten. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS with a throwaway migration: a new ungranted callable SECURITY DEFINER function reddened naming it; the SAME function with a REVOKE + GRANT block passed; and granting an existing debt entry reddened the shrink-only case telling the reader to delete the entry. Probe migration removed, tree confirmed clean. VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean, eslint clean, the three cases pass, full vitest 3671 passed / 0 failed.

userStories.title: extension.pem private key is committed to the repository
userStories.description: git ls-files confirms extension.pem and extension.crx are tracked. extension.pem begins with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. .gitignore has no .pem or .crx rule. The key was added 2026-07-13 in commit e1dbc4da; gitleaks failed that commit and every run since has been green because push-mode only scans new commits. This is the Chrome Web Store signing identity for the extension. Anyone with repo read access can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives. Also tracked and probably unwanted: ios-screenshots/Payment/ios.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-appstore.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-raw.zip.
acceptanceCriteria: Rotate the Chrome Web Store extension key first. Removing the file does not un-leak it.
git rm --cached extension.pem extension.crx; add *.pem, *.crx and ios-screenshots/*.zip to .gitignore.
Decide and record whether git history is rewritten (BFG / filter-repo) or the key is simply treated as burned. Rewriting rewrites every open PR.

userStories.notes: [P0][Security/Secrets] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. via git ls-files + file header + .gitignore read. Rotation is a human action, not a code change. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the code half is done; AC1 (rotate) and AC3 (the rewrite-or-burn decision) are HUMAN actions and are now written down where the person doing them will find them. AC2 DONE: extension.pem, extension.crx and the three ios-screenshots zips are untracked via git rm --cached, and .gitignore refuses *.pem, *.crx, *.p12, *.keystore, *.jks and ios-screenshots/**/*.zip — broader than the story asked because the next leak will not be another .pem. Verified with git check-ignore. AC4 DONE: NEW .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml runs gitleaks over the FULL history weekly (Mondays 06:00 UTC, plus workflow_dispatch), with fetch-depth:0 and the gitleaks BINARY rather than gitleaks-action — the action derives its scan scope from the triggering event and on a schedule there is no diff, so `detect` over the checked-out repo is the unambiguous form. The report uploads on failure, because a bare red X names nothing. WHY THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT and worth stating plainly: there WAS a secret scanner, it WAS working, and it could not have caught this. secret-scan.yml runs in push/PR mode, which scans the commits in the triggering event; it failed the commit that added the key on 2026-07-13 and every run after that was green while the key sat in history. Per-push asks 'is this change clean?'; only a history sweep asks 'is the repository clean?'. AC5 DONE (structurally): vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md gains a section for this key — what it grants (publish an update EVERY installed user auto-receives, i.e. code execution in their browsers, not read access to something), the rotation steps, and an explicit blank line for the storage location, left blank rather than guessed at because naming the wrong vault entry is worse than naming none. AC3 is RECORDED not decided: both options are written out with their real costs — treat-as-burned (rotation makes the leaked copy inert; no rewrite; usually right for a signing key) versus rewrite (BFG/filter-repo; rewrites every open PR and invalidates every clone). .gitleaks.toml carries a COMMENTED-OUT allowlist stanza to uncomment AFTER rotation, with an explicit 'DO NOT uncomment before rotation — silencing a live key is worse than the leak, because it also removes the reminder.' EXPECT THE SCHEDULED SCAN TO BE RED until one of those two happens: the key IS still in history, so a finding is the job working, not a broken job. ALSO ADDED: src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts refuses any tracked .pem/.crx/.p12/.pfx/.keystore/.jks/.key/.ppk at the point a developer notices — their own test run, before the push. It reads git ls-files rather than the filesystem, because an ignored file on disk is fine and a TRACKED one is the bug, and it skips (not fails) without a git binary, since a false red on a P0 guard trains people to ignore it. Negative-verified by force-adding a .pem to the index (reddened naming the file, reverted). REMAINING FOR THE OWNER: (1) rotate the Chrome Web Store signing key and revoke the old one; (2) fill in the storage-location line in key-rotation.md; (3) choose burn-vs-rewrite and, if burning, uncomment the gitleaks stanza. VERIFIED: 3079 tests pass (239 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green, vault-lint 108 notes clean. | SEVERITY RE-ASSESSED 2026-08-03, in BOTH directions, because the original framing is wrong in a way that changes what the owner should do. WORSE THAN RECORDED: the repository is PUBLIC (gh repo view reports visibility PUBLIC) and commit e1dbc4da is on origin, and reading that path out of history still returns a PRIVATE KEY header today. So this is not 'anyone with repo read access' — it is anyone at all, with no access, right now. Untracking the file (AC2) did nothing about that and was never going to; only rotation does. BETTER THAN RECORDED, and this is the part that should stop anyone panicking: the claim that 'anyone can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives' is NOT true today. Checked: no manifest in extension/, extension-condition/ or extension-unified/ declares an update_url or a key field, so there is no self-hosted auto-update channel; and US-1757 (publish to the Chrome Web Store and AMO) is still OPEN and operator-gated, so the extension has never been published and has no installed users. Uploading to the Web Store needs the developer ACCOUNT, which this key is not. WHAT THE KEY ACTUALLY GRANTS: the ability to package a CRX carrying the SAME extension ID as the real one — which matters for sideloading, for enterprise-policy deployment, and for any future self-hosted update channel, and which would let a lookalike be presented as genuine. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR SEQUENCING, which is the practical finding and was recorded nowhere: rotation is CHEAP right now and gets expensive the moment the extension is published, because after publication that ID is the installed identity. So AC1 must be done BEFORE US-1757, and US-1757 should not proceed until it is. RE-VERIFIED the code half rather than trusting the note: git ls-files finds no .pem, .gitignore lines 155-156 refuse *.pem and *.crx (git check-ignore confirms both files), .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml exists, and src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts passes 3/3.

userStories.title: users_billing_source_chk rejects 'googleplay' — Play subscriptions may be failing outright
userStories.description: 00104_appstore_billing.sql:25 defines users_billing_source_chk allowing only 'stripe' and 'appstore'. The Google Play verification path writes 'googleplay'. If the constraint is live in prod as written, every Play subscription write fails: the customer is charged by Google and receives no entitlement.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm against prod whether the constraint still excludes 'googleplay' and whether any Play purchase has ever succeeded.

userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Verify against prod before assuming customers were affected — the constraint may have been altered outside migrations. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED, and it is worse than 'may be failing' — it fails, deterministically. users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE, in 00104_appstore_billing.sql line 25: CHECK (billing_source IS NULL OR billing_source IN ('stripe','appstore')). grep across every file in supabase/migrations returns exactly two hits for the constraint name, both in 00104 (the IF NOT EXISTS probe and the ADD CONSTRAINT). NO migration ever drops or re-adds it. 00321_google_play_billing.sql touches public.users but only to add columns — its own header comment says "billing_source already carries 'stripe'/'appstore'; Play sets 'googleplay'", which reads as if the constraint had been widened, and it never was. Meanwhile the Play grant path genuinely stamps it: services/edge-functions/src/lib/google-play/products.ts declares billing_source: 'googleplay' as a literal type on the users update, and the expiry sweep queries .eq('billing_source','googleplay'). So every Play subscription grant UPDATE violates the check and returns 23514, and the sweep can never match a row because no row can hold that value. WHAT MAKES THIS EASY TO MISS: three OTHER constraints were correctly widened for Play — 00354 added 'googleplay' to the dead-letter provider check, 00414 allows it on buyer_billing_source, 00486 allows 'google_play' on the agreed-terms source. Only the seller-side users constraint was left behind, so a targeted grep for 'googleplay' in migrations returns four confident-looking hits and none of them is the one that matters. THE FIX is a one-line ALTER (drop + re-add with the third value), needing the US-1108 triple. Worth checking prod for stuck Play purchasers before shipping it: they paid Google and were never entitled here. | AC2 + AC3 DONE 2026-08-07, migration 00558 (HELD). RE-VERIFIED FIRST as the note asks, and the 2026-08-04 verification holds exactly: users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE (00104:24-25) allowing only stripe/appstore, grep returns exactly two hits for the name and both are in 00104, and no migration ever drops or re-adds it. The writers are three literals and only three — stripe (routes/webhooks.ts:666), appstore (lib/appstore/reconcile.ts:59), googleplay (lib/google-play/products.ts:104) — confirmed by scanning every object-literal assignment across the edge service, src/ and functions/, not by reading the two files the story names. AC2: 00558 drops and re-adds the constraint with the third value. It uses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD rather than 00104s IF NOT EXISTS probe DELIBERATELY: the probe is the reason the stale definition survived every subsequent apply, so repeating it would make this migration a no-op the next time someone widens the set. AC3: NEW src/test/billing-source-constraint.test.ts, 3 cases. It does NOT hardcode the allowed set — a constant here would be a THIRD copy needing maintenance, which is the same class of bug the test is for. It parses the live CHECK body out of the highest-numbered migration that defines the constraint (apply order is filename order, so a later re-add supersedes) and compares it against the literals scanned from source. Both directions: a value the code writes that the constraint rejects, and a value the constraint permits that nobody writes. The third case pins googleplay/appstore/stripe by name, because the first two both pass if the Play writer is DELETED and the constraint narrows to match — a silent removal of Android billing rather than a fix. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: reverting 00558 to the 00104 set reddens 2 of 3 cases and the failure message names lib/google-play/products.ts as the writing file. VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, schema-version_test 18/18 (which is what proves the US-1108 triple — EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00558, manifest regenerated to 303 entries, self-record footer present). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md updated: held count 16 -> 17, and it records that this one is unusual in that it has NO forward dependency — the edge already writes googleplay today and that write is already failing, so applying it makes existing code start working rather than creating a window where old code breaks against new schema. REMAINING, BOTH OPERATOR-ONLY (no Supabase access from this host): AC1 confirm against prod whether the constraint still excludes googleplay and whether any Play purchase ever succeeded; AC4 reconcile and grant retroactively for anyone charged by Google without entitlement. The affected set IS recoverable rather than lost — the Play purchase token is recorded even when the users-row grant failed, so start from the Play purchase records, not from users.billing_source (which by definition can hold no googleplay row).

userStories.title: Unlimited free trials: handle_new_user grants 14 days of Pro with no abuse check
userStories.description: 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql:102-104 grants every new signup a 14-day Pro trial with no card, no device fingerprint, no email-domain check and no prior-trial lookup. Deleting the account and signing up again resets it. Each trial can consume real Claude Vision spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the abuse control: card-on-file for trial, per-device/per-email prior-trial record, or a hard cap on trial grading volume. Record the decision.
A prior-trial record survives account deletion (keyed on something that persists, not on the users row).
Trial grading volume is capped independently of the plan's normal allowance.

userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Abuse] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Measure before building — the fix depends on whether this is being exploited today. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED against the LIVE definition, not the one the story cites. handle_new_user has been redefined six times; the current body is 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql, and it grants flipdesk_plan='pro', subscription_status='trialing', trial_ends_at=now()+interval '14 days' to every signup EXCEPT a buyer-only one (v_buyer_only, from a client-supplied account_type of 'buyer'). No prior-trial lookup, no email-domain check, no device or IP signal, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING — so one auth user is one trial and a second address is a second trial. The claim holds exactly as filed. ONE CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S FRAMING: 00303 is not the live definition, 00401 is, and the difference matters if a fix is written — 00401 already carves out buyer-only signups, so any abuse check has to compose with v_buyer_only rather than wrap the whole grant. A SECOND THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FIXING: the whole function body is wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS RETURN NEW, deliberately, so a profile-row failure can never abort auth signup. Any abuse check added here inherits that — if it raises, the user still gets an auth account and gets NO profile row at all, which is a worse outcome than an extra trial. The check probably belongs downstream of signup, not inside this trigger. | 2026-08-08 AC4 IS NOW RUNNABLE — the measurement this story insists on doing FIRST is written as §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, so it rides along with the other operator reads instead of being a separate ask. AC1 stays open ON PURPOSE: the correct abuse control is a different control if the answer is 'two people did this' than if it is 'two hundred', and the story is right that building before measuring picks one blind. FOUR QUERIES, ALL READ-ONLY. (a) trials started per month vs converted vs still trialing. (b) THE ABUSE SIGNAL: addresses that normalise to the SAME mailbox once a Gmail-style plus-tag and dots are stripped. That is the cheapest possible way to take a second trial, so any stem with n > 1 is one person holding several. It returns COUNTS and nothing else - no addresses, not even the normalised stems - because this output gets pasted around and the rest of the file is deliberately secret-free. (c) what the trials COST: grading submissions made inside the trial window, per account and worst-case, which is the number that decides whether AC3's trial-specific volume cap is worth building at all. (d) whether any of it came from an account since DELETED, which is what makes the delete-and-resignup loop measurable rather than hypothetical. A READING GUIDE SITS UNDER IT, because the numbers alone do not imply the fix: (b) and (d) both zero means the hole is real but unexploited and a plain prior-trial record suffices; (b) above zero means it is already in use and the record has to SURVIVE deletion, which is exactly why AC2 asks for it to be keyed on something outliving the users row. TWO BUGS IN MY OWN SQL, both found by EXECUTING it rather than reading it, and both would have hurt the operator rather than me. (1) I wrote subscription_status NOT IN (..., 'incomplete'). There is no 'incomplete' - the enum is none/trialing/active/past_due/paused/canceled/comp - so on prod that is 22P02 and, under ON_ERROR_STOP, it ABORTS THE WHOLE SESSION partway through, taking the other eighteen sections with it. That is precisely the failure mode this file's own header says it exists to prevent. Rewritten to name the PAID statuses positively (active, comp), which is also the safer shape: an exclusion list silently counts any status added later as a conversion. (2) account_deletion_log records requested_at, not deleted_at. THE REPO'S OWN GUARD CAUGHT A THIRD THING I HAD NOT THOUGHT ABOUT: src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts failed because prod-diagnostics-console.sql - the meta-command-free copy for the Supabase SQL editor - was out of sync. Regenerated with scripts/gen-console-diagnostics.mjs and executed separately; both files now run to completion. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by review: the FULL file and the FULL console copy each ran against a throwaway local stack with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, both exit 0, zero ERROR lines, and §19 returned real rows against the seeded data (3 trial-window submissions across 2 accounts) - so the queries execute and shape correctly, not merely parse. prod-diagnostics-safety 9 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN: AC1 (the control, once the numbers are in), AC2 (a prior-trial record surviving deletion), AC3 (a trial-specific volume cap). NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC2, because there is a real tension nobody has written down yet: US-2005 PURGES email-keyed rows on account deletion, so a prior-trial record holding an address would be erased by the very deletion it exists to remember. The shape that resolves it already exists in this codebase - email_suppressions is deliberately EXEMPT from that purge on legitimate-interest grounds, for the same reason (forgetting a suppressed address harms the person the erasure protects). A salted hash rather than an address would be stronger still. Do not solve this by quietly adding a table to the purge-exempt list without saying why.

userStories.title: Batch grading re-charges on every retry, up to 5 times for one garment
userStories.description: lib/grading-batch-worker.ts:59-124 and :155-176: gradeBatchItem unconditionally INSERTs a new submission (:66-79) and calls runPaymentPrecedence (:97) on every invocation. runJob reclaims a stale job (:167) and calls it again with no reference to the submission a prior attempt already created and paid for. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS is 240s but a single image's worst case is already 3 attempts x 120s = 360s, so a job can be marked stale while the original pipeline is still running and may still write a valid grade. After GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS (15 min) the reclaim cron starts a second paid attempt. MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS is 5. Result: up to 5 credits debited for one payload, plus duplicate certificates.
acceptanceCriteria: The created submission_id is persisted on the job row BEFORE the charge, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission rather than creating a new one.

Payment is charged at most once per job row, enforced by an idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions (the column and partial unique index already exist at 00216_credit_ledger_admin.sql:35-42 and the grading path never sets it).
Item lease duration exceeds the true worst-case runtime (3 AI attempts x timeout + composite), or the work is made cancellable.
Regression test: a job forced through 3 reclaims debits exactly one credit and produces exactly one certificate.
Audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id, and refund affected customers.
userStories.notes: [P0][Grading/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-confidence money bug from the grading audit — the code path is described concretely and matches the reclaim-cron design. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the double-charge is FIXED at the root (AC1, AC3, AC4); AC2 is defence-in-depth that now needs a migration, and AC5 is an operator action. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the note asked: gradeBatchItem created a submission and called runPaymentPrecedence unconditionally on every invocation, and runJob called it again on every reclaim with no reference to the submission a prior attempt had created and paid for. Confirmed the two windows that made it reachable rather than theoretical: GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS was 240s while one garment's worst case is (AI_MAX_RETRIES + 1) x AI_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 x 120s = 360s (ai-config.ts DEFAULTS), so the worker abandoned a pipeline that was still running; and GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS was 360s — EQUAL to that worst case — so the reclaim cron could pick up a job nobody had abandoned. With MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS at 5 that is up to 5 credits and 5 certificates for one garment. AC1 DONE: the submission id is written to the job row IMMEDIATELY after creation and BEFORE any money moves, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission instead of creating another. The ordering is the point — writing it after the charge would leave exactly the window this story is about; writing it before means a container death mid-flight leaves an UNPAID submission, which the resume path declines and starts clean, costing nothing. The fix is deliberately NOT a smarter charge: payment is per-submission, so resuming skips the charge BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard someone has to remember. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/paid-submission.ts holds isPaidSubmissionStatus as its own pure module — it is the hinge the whole fix turns on and keeping it out of the worker means it can be tested without booting the grading pipeline. It fails CLOSED on unknown/NULL/unpaid, and the asymmetry is the reason: a false negative re-creates a submission nobody paid for (free), a false positive skips a real charge or resumes a row we do not own. The paid values are the three grade-billing.ts actually writes — included, credits, paid_stripe — read off the source, not guessed. The resume path also re-stamps status=processing (tenant-scoped, mirroring the charging chokepoint's own .eq(user_id)) and records the API usage the abandoned attempt never got to record, exactly once. AC3 DONE: both windows are now DERIVED from the AI budget instead of written down beside it, because two hardcoded numbers that must track a third are two numbers that drift — which is precisely how the lease ended up shorter than the work it was leasing. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS = (getAiMaxRetries()+1) * getAiTimeoutMs() + 90s composite headroom (450s at current defaults, up from 240s); GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS = 1.5x the lease (675s, up from 360s) so a merely-slow worker is never mistaken for a dead one; GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS is floored above the job window so the batch sweeper cannot fire before its jobs are even reclaimable. The pre-existing assertion (timeout < stale) in grading-batch_test.ts still holds. AC4 DONE: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/grading-batch-recharge_test.ts, 6 Deno cases pinning the lease-exceeds-worst-case relationship, the stale margin, the sweeper ordering, the derivation arithmetic (asserted rather than the literal, so raising AI_TIMEOUT_MS keeps it green), and both directions of the paid-status rule. VERIFIED: 20 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled paid-submission module plus the timing arithmetic reproduced independently (old lease 240000 confirmed BELOW the 360000 worst case); all four changed edge files parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: (AC2) the idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions. The column and partial unique index exist (00216:35-42) but the credit debit goes through the debit_grade_credits RPC, so threading a key needs a FUNCTION SIGNATURE CHANGE — a migration, which cannot be pushed from this host under the held-migration rule. It is defence-in-depth behind the root fix, not the fix itself. (AC5) audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers — an operator action; the query is: grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch. | AC2 DONE 2026-08-03, migration 00516 (HELD). The note above said this needed a function signature change and so a migration, and that is exactly what it took. debit_grade_credits gains a TRAILING p_idempotency_key defaulting to NULL, so every existing 4-arg caller is untouched; the old 4-arg overload is DROPPED in the same file, because leaving it would let those callers silently keep resolving to the pre-idempotency body. When a key is supplied and a ledger row already carries it the function debits nothing and returns the current balance — returning rather than raising on purpose, since the caller intent (this submission is paid for) is already satisfied and an error would make a harmless retry look like a billing failure and push the caller into a checkout it does not need. The edge passes grade-batch-job:{jobId}, keyed on the JOB rather than the submission because the job is what a reclaim re-runs. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by inspection: applied to the local stack and exercised in a rolled-back transaction — the same key three times debits ONCE (10 -> 7 -> 7 -> 7, exactly one ledger row), a different key debits normally, and a call with no key debits every time, which is the assertion that protects the existing callers. Storage needed no migration: 00216 already had the column and its partial unique index, unused. REMAINING: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. That is an operator action; the query is grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. Edge suite 5155/0.

userStories.title: The golden-set eval gate never runs in CI and the live prompt versions have no DB row
userStories.description: Two compounding problems. (1) The grading eval appears in none of the 16 files in .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json. The only eval task there is the agent eval, and CI does not call that either. No build, deploy or PR is blocked by golden-set accuracy. runScheduledEval raises alerts and blocks nothing. (2) The code defaults are per_image_v5 and composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63) but the only grading seed migration (00050_grading_self_improvement.sql:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 and composite_v2, and no migration sets is_active. So the live prompts have no row and were never evaluated. (3) The repo contains no golden-set data at all: zero INSERTs into grading_eval_cases, no seed, no fixture. A fresh database has an empty golden set; runEval throws on empty but grading-monitor.ts:287-294 treats zero cases as a clean skip, so an empty set is silent. Net effect: editing prompt text in ai-grading.ts ships straight to customers without ever touching an eval.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, against prod, whether grading_eval_cases has any rows and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active. Record the answer in the story before building.
The golden-set eval runs in CI and fails the build on regression, or the reason it cannot is written down.
