EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 (grading-eval.ts:26-29) is reconsidered: on a 1.0-10.0 scale a prompt can be a full grade point off on average and pass.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Lifecycle] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The prompt-lifecycle doc reads as if a pipeline gate exists. It does not. Either add one or correct the doc. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — ALL FOUR factual claims independently RE-VERIFIED and TRUE; AC4 and AC5 shipped, the doc corrected; AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 need prod access or a migration and are recorded with why. VERIFICATION (mechanical, not by reading the cited lines): (1) NO CI GATE — the golden-set eval appears in no file under .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json; the only match anywhere in those trees is a mention in scripts/ralph/progress.txt. Nothing blocks a build, PR or deploy on grading accuracy. (2) THE LIVE PROMPTS HAVE NO ROW — code defaults are per_image_v5 / composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63); the sole seed migration (00050:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 / composite_v2 with is_active false. Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding". DOC CORRECTED (the story's own closing note asked for exactly this): .claude/skills/grading-engine/references/prompt-lifecycle.md read as if a pipeline gate existed. It now opens with what the gate does NOT cover — no CI gate, code defaults with no DB row — while stating clearly that the part which IS real (activation and canary refusing an un-evaled version, via checkPromptServingEligibility, US-2300) applies only to versions that go through a DB row. VERIFIED: 4 alert assertions plus the seeding scan run against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — the scan reports exactly composite_v4 and per_image_v5 as unseeded, matching the declaration; grading-monitor.ts and the test parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm against prod what grading_eval_cases holds and which ai_prompt_versions are active) — operator only, and it should be done BEFORE the rest, as the AC says. AC3 (seed rows for the code defaults) — a migration, push-blocked here. AC2 (eval in CI) — depends on AC1/AC3: a CI eval against an empty golden set would be theatre, and the golden set must grow from REAL human-corrected grades, never fabricated ones, so it cannot be seeded from this host either. AC6 (EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 lets a prompt be a full grade point off on a 1-10 scale and still pass) — a product judgement about acceptable error, with a real cost either way, and it belongs to the owner rather than to a sandbox.

userStories.title: The 0.75 review threshold lives in ~18 places and only the edge copy is tunable
userStories.description: Four named constants, none shared: ai-config.ts:267 (tunable via env + DB setting), src/lib/constants.ts:1310, ios GradeFactors.swift:117, android GradeFactor.kt:47. Plus roughly fourteen hardcoded literals making the same decision: main.ts:1678, admin-grading.ts:1320 (hardcoded in the same file that reads the tunable at :2103), admin-dashboard.ts:107, listing-suggestions.tsx:123, extension-condition/content/marketplace.js:267, extension-unified/research/marketplace.js:370, GradeReportView.swift:247 and :254, five display-bucket sites, and four SQL view copies (00082:56-58, 00118:45-47, 00138:69-71, 00194:64-66). Lowering the threshold in the admin UI moves the real gate but leaves the admin agreement metric, the dashboard count, both browser extensions and all three clients still deciding at 0.75.
acceptanceCriteria: One authoritative value, served to every surface that makes the decision (clients read it from config, not from a literal).
SQL views derive their buckets from a single function or table rather than four copies of the literal.
A lockstep guard test fails if a new 0.75 literal appears in a decision site.
Comparison operators stay consistent (< threshold routes to review); the audit found no off-by-one today.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Config] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Also: grading-pipeline.ts:2561 calls reconcileNeedsReview without the calibrated threshold, so it re-flags at the flat value and makes calibration a no-op in the direction it was built for. Fix together. | 2026-08-03 AC3 and AC4 DONE, AC1 done for the web+edge decision sites, AC2 NOT done and explicitly left. The mobile copies are out of scope on this host. A CORRECTION TO THIS STORY'S OWN NOTE, and it is the most useful thing here. The note says grading-pipeline.ts 'calls reconcileNeedsReview without the calibrated threshold, so it re-flags at the flat value and makes calibration a no-op in the direction it was built for'. THAT IS WRONG. The parameter's DEFAULT is reviewConfidenceThreshold(), and a JavaScript default is evaluated PER CALL — so omitting the argument reads the current DB-backed setting rather than freezing anything. Calibration works today. Passing a literal there is what would break it, so a test now asserts the call site contains NO numeric argument, which pins the working behaviour instead of 'fixing' a bug that was not there. THE DISTINCTION THAT SHAPED EVERYTHING ELSE, and which an indiscriminate sweep would have destroyed: not every 0.75 is a copy of the gate. confidenceLabelFor in admin-grading.ts must match the public_certificate SQL VIEW byte for byte, because the admin queue and the public certificate label the SAME grade. If that bucket followed the tunable gate, the two surfaces would disagree about a certificate a buyer is looking at — a worse failure than a stale boundary. Same for the passport bands. So the sites are ENUMERATED by KIND, because no rule can tell them apart: the difference is intent. TWO DECISION SITES FIXED. (1) admin-grading.ts's agreement metric counted reviewed grades with a hardcoded 0.75 — the story's own headline example. It counts what the gate caught, so scoring against a different number meant the CALIBRATION SCREEN reported on a threshold nobody was using, which is worse than not reporting. (2) listing-suggestions.tsx told a seller their grade was low-confidence at a literal 0.75; it now reads the shared constant, because that advice has to mean the same thing as the gate. AC4 VERIFIED AND PINNED: reconcileNeedsReview is the one implementation and it compares `effectiveConfidence < threshold`. A test asserts that exact line — `<=` would send a grade sitting exactly on the threshold to a human and `>` would invert the gate, and neither would be visible in a diff of a number. AC3: NEW src/test/confidence-threshold-sites.test.ts, 8 cases. Decision sites must read the shared symbol AND contain no confidence-vs-literal comparison; pinned buckets must still bucket (a stale exemption is how the next regression gets waved through); the threshold must still come from the settings registry; and the SQL-view copies are asserted to STILL EXIST, so AC2 being open is a fact the suite states rather than something a reader has to notice. MY OWN GUARD FAILED TWICE, both found by mutation, and the first is the exact failure it was written to prevent. The confidence-vs-literal pattern used `\s*` between the field and the operator, so `Number(r.confidence_score) < 0.75` — with a `)` in the gap — MATCHED NOTHING. Putting the literal back left the suite green. There is now a CANARY case asserting the pattern matches the two real forms and not the fixed one, because a never-matching regex is indistinguishable from a clean tree. Second: the pinned bucket was excluded line by line on the shape of its return statement; it is removed by FUNCTION NAME now, so the exemption is a declared function rather than any line that resembles one. AND A CRLF TRAP: an assertion used a multi-line string with \n against an edge source file. Those are CRLF, so it matched nothing and failed for a reason unrelated to the threshold. It is a regex now. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the agreement metric hardcoded again, the seller suggestion hardcoded again, the threshold no longer reading the registry, the gate comparison flipped to <=, and the re-derivation handed a frozen 0.75. Each reddened on its own case — two of them only after the guard itself was fixed. AC2 NOT DONE, STATED PLAINLY: four migrations (00082, 00118, 00138, 00194) each carry their own confidence_score >= 0.75 bucket boundaries. Deriving them from one function or table is a migration this pass did not write, and it is the half where a mistake is hardest to reverse — the views feed the public certificate. AC1 is likewise only done for web+edge: the iOS and Android constants are unreachable from this host, and 'clients read it from config' for the PUBLIC methodology page needs a served config value, which is a design decision rather than a substitution. VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, deno check + lint clean across 1334 files, full edge suite 5300 passed / 0 failed, web 793 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03 AC2 RE-SCOPED, not done — and the correction changes what the work is. THE STORY SAYS 'four SQL view copies (00082, 00118, 00138, 00194)'. They are not four copies. They are four successive CREATE OR REPLACE revisions of ONE view, public.public_grade_reports — and there are THIRTEEN such revisions in the corpus, not four. Only the LATEST (00356) is live; the other twelve are immutable history and must not be touched, which is the opposite of what 'consolidate four copies' implies. SO AC2 IS A ONE-VIEW CHANGE: add an IMMUTABLE public.grade_confidence_label() and CREATE OR REPLACE the live view to call it, so the NEXT revision cannot re-fork the boundaries. That is smaller than the AC implies and also more delicate than it sounds. WHY IT IS NOT DONE IN THIS PASS, stated rather than deferred silently. The view is 86 lines and feeds the PUBLIC CERTIFICATE, and CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW demands the entire definition again with identical column names, types and order. Two options and both have a real cost: hand-transcribe 86 lines (a single column slip breaks every certificate page), or generate the body from pg_get_viewdef, which is safe against transcription but emits Postgres's normalised form — a style break in a corpus of hand-written, commented migrations, and the next author would CREATE OR REPLACE from the previous hand-written version and silently undo it. IT ALSO NEEDS A SECOND LITERAL SET CONSIDERED: the same view buckets authenticity_confidence at 0.85/0.6, a different scale from the review threshold, so a single grade_confidence_label() would be wrong for it. Two functions or one with an explicit scale argument — a decision, not a substitution. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the display buckets must stay PINNED to the view either way. The admin queue's confidenceLabelFor mirrors these boundaries so the two surfaces agree about a certificate a buyer is looking at; extracting them into a function is about preventing DRIFT BETWEEN REVISIONS, not about making them follow the tunable review gate. The guard added earlier today already asserts the view copies still exist, so this AC being open is a fact the suite states rather than something a reader has to notice.

userStories.title: FlipDesk grading drops the label photo the pipeline still blocks on
userStories.description: flipdesk-grading.ts:83 sets REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES to front and back only, with a comment claiming the tag shot is covered by the sub-0.75 review path. That premise is false: lib/image-quality.ts:68 still lists label as required with severity 'block' and there is no carve-out at its only call site (grading-pipeline.ts:1859). A FlipDesk item with no tag photo is charged (flipdesk-grading.ts:591), runs one Claude Vision call per image, then abstains to needs_photos and refunds. Money returns, AI spend burns every time, seller round-trips. iOS and Android both use this path with no local check.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide: either FlipDesk requires the label photo, or image-quality gets an explicit FlipDesk carve-out. Record which and why.
The two requirement lists cannot disagree — one source, or a test that asserts they match.
The client validates before upload so the seller is told up front, not after a round trip.
Measure how often this fires today (submissions ending needs_photos with a refund) to size the wasted AI spend.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Grading] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1, AC2, AC3 DONE. AC4 is a prod query and stays open as the operator half. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked, and every claim held. AC1 DECISION (owner, via AskUserQuestion): FLIPDESK REQUIRES THE TAG PHOTO. THE OLD COMMENT'S PREMISE WAS FALSE, which is what made this worth asking about rather than assuming: flipdesk-grading said front+back were enough because 'the <0.75 → human-review path already covers the weaker-signal case'. image-quality.ts lists `label` in REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES at severity `block`, and grading-pipeline.ts applies it at Step 4b — BEFORE any confidence scoring. The review path it named never executed. So a FlipDesk item with no tag was charged (flipdesk-grading.ts runPaymentPrecedence), ran ONE CLAUDE VISION CALL PER IMAGE, abstained to needs_photos, and was refunded. The money came back and the AI spend did not, every time, and the seller round-tripped to be told something we could have said up front. Requiring it is therefore strictly better for the SAME seller the old comment was written to protect. THE OTHER OPTIONS AND WHY NOT: loosening image-quality would have changed grading for every WEB submission too (more human review, a global product change for a FlipDesk bug); a FlipDesk-only carve-out would have frozen two deliberately-different paths forever. Both were offered to the owner with their costs. ⚠ LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: the old comment's concern is real — some garments (Lululemon cut size labels, tagless resale) genuinely have no readable tag. That is a product question about what those sellers photograph, and it is recorded at the call site rather than settled by loosening a grading gate. AC2 DONE BY DERIVATION, not by matching two literals: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is now REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES.map(gradingImageTypeToPhotoType), so the lists cannot drift apart again. Two tests pin the derivation and the round trip — a wrong entry in the inverse map would make them agree on paper while asking the seller for a photo type the UI cannot produce. A REAL BUG THE TEST CAUGHT, and it would have been a prod outage rather than a wrong answer: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is built at MODULE LOAD, and I first placed the GRADING_TO_PHOTO_TYPE map below it. A function declaration hoists; the `const` it reads does not, so the module threw ReferenceError at import and the edge would not have booted. The map is now above its use with that reason written next to it. AC3 DONE: the client already had a readiness mirror (src/lib/grading-readiness.ts) driving the Submit card live, so the seller is told before paying. THE TRAP IN THE CLIENT HALF: REQUIRED_PHOTO_TYPES was doing DOUBLE DUTY — it gates 'may this item advance to photographed and be listed?' AND fed the grading readiness preview. Adding `tag` to it would have blocked the LISTING pipeline for every tagless garment, which nobody asked for and is a different product decision. Added a SEPARATE REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES (front, back, tag); the listing list is unchanged, and a test asserts the two stay different. THE SHARED FIXTURE (src/test/fixtures/grading-readiness-cases.json, asserted by BOTH suites) was regenerated from the rules rather than hand-edited — 13 cases each needing a blocker string and a missingPhotos list is where a typo becomes a cross-project contract both sides then agree on. But a straight recompute BROKE WHAT THE CASES WERE FOR: 'fully ready' had no tag, so it stopped being ready and every case collapsed onto the same missing-tag blocker, testing nothing. Inputs were patched to preserve each case's intent, the case named 'tag photo does not satisfy anything' was renamed (it is no longer true), and a 'missing tag only' case was added for the new rule — 14 total. Also fixed a latent wrong-name in the edge parity test: it passed the GRADING type `label` where the FlipDesk readiness function takes `tag`. It passed either way while neither was required. AC4 REMAINS (operator): count submissions ending needs_photos with a refund, to size the wasted AI spend. It belongs with the other prod diagnostics. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5358 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1339 files, tsc -b clean, web readiness + hooks suites 112 passed.

userStories.title: quick-grade bypasses every pipeline-level confidence control
userStories.description: quick-grade.ts:137 returns composite.needs_human_review straight from compositeGrade, so the Snap-to-Value and browser-extension path never sees the partial-image cap, peer-norm, forensic or reconcile passes. Separately, auto-approve requires confidence >= 0.9 (grade-auto-approve.ts:22) while the clients call >= 0.75 'certified', a mismatch already recorded as a UI bug in ios/IOS_APP_REVIEW_AUDIT_2026-06-30.md:46.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide whether quick-grade should carry the pipeline controls or is deliberately a lighter product. Record the decision.
If deliberate, the difference is documented and the quick-grade output is labelled differently to customers.
The auto-approve threshold and the client 'certified' threshold are reconciled or the labels are changed.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/QuickGrade] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. DECISION-then-build. | 2026-08-02 BOTH CITED CLAIMS INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, as this story's own note asked before anyone fixes anything. Both are true, and the second is worse than the story states. CLAIM 1 CONFIRMED: quick-grade.ts:137 is `needsHumanReview: composite.needs_human_review` — straight from compositeGrade. I then grepped quick-grade.ts for every pipeline-level control by name (applyGradingConfidencePolicy, peer-norm, composeConfidenceCap, confidenceCeiling, forensic, reconcile) and got ZERO hits. So the Snap-to-Value and browser-extension path genuinely sees none of them: not the partial-image cap, not the peer-norm outlier cap, not the visual-verification discrepancy trigger, and not the confidenceCeiling that US-2299 added to stop a capped grade being boosted back over its cap. CLAIM 2 CONFIRMED AND SHARPER THAN RECORDED. grade-auto-approve.ts:22 DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 0.9, env-overridable. constants.ts:1310 GRADING_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.75. The story frames the 0.75 side as clients calling it "certified", i.e. a UI label. It is more than a label: src/pages/marketing/grading-methodology.tsx:99 renders that constant into a PUBLIC METHODOLOGY PAGE that tells buyers "when confidence falls below 0.75, the submission is routed to a human reviewer before the grade is finalized — low-confidence cases never ship unchecked." So the 0.75 number is a published claim about the product, not an internal threshold, and it is the number a buyer would cite in a dispute. THE TWO FINDINGS COMPOSE, which is the part worth deciding on rather than either alone: a quick-grade result inherits none of the caps that would LOWER its confidence, and the public page promises that anything under 0.75 gets a human. A quick-grade that reports 0.8 because no cap ever ran is, by the page's own wording, a grade that shipped unchecked while appearing to satisfy the promise. That is the same confident-wrong-number shape as US-2386 and US-2390, on the surface where it is most externally visible. AC1 IS A PRODUCT DECISION AND I AM NOT MAKING IT — the honest options are (a) quick-grade is a lighter product and must be labelled as such everywhere it surfaces, including not being called certified, or (b) it carries the pipeline controls and stops being quick. What I have removed is the need for whoever decides to re-derive any of it. NOTE FOR THAT READER: AC3 says "reconciled or the labels are changed", and the methodology page means changing the label is a change to a PUBLISHED claim — treat it as copy that needs the same care as the refund policy in US-2127, not as a UI string.

userStories.title: Nothing in version control creates or verifies the 73 production cron schedules
userStories.description: There is no scheduling mechanism in the repo. docker-compose.coolify.yml has no cron, sidecar or command (only the healthcheck at lines 70-79); same for the other compose files. .github/workflows has zero /api/jobs references and its only three schedule blocks are lighthouse, staging-smoke and an uptime probe. pg_cron is unused (zero cron.schedule across all 506 migrations). Cloudflare is unused (no crons in wrangler.toml, no scheduled handler in functions/). The sole mechanism is 73 hand-typed Coolify UI scheduled tasks documented in COOLIFY.md:222-255 and CRON_SETUP.md. Nothing creates, applies or verifies them. The only runtime check is cron-fleet-health, which is itself one of the 73 hand-entered tasks — if the operator never created it, nothing alerts about anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the mechanism: schedules-as-code (compose sidecar, pg_cron, or a scheduler service) or a verified manifest. Record the decision.
At minimum: an artifact in the repo listing every expected schedule, and a job that compares it to what actually ran and alerts on absence.
Confirm cron-fleet-health itself is scheduled in prod and that its alerts reach a human.

Confirm ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are set in prod system_settings — both default to empty string (ops-events.ts:78-79), in which case the entire alert path terminates in an admin screen nobody is watching.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Cron] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Root cause behind the three dead schedules. Start with the prod verification, not the build. | 2026-08-02 VERIFIED, with two counts corrected. The central claim is TRUE and I checked each half rather than the summary. NO pg_cron: grep for cron.schedule / pg_cron across every file in supabase/migrations returns nothing. NO scheduler in compose: services/edge-functions/docker-compose.coolify.yml contains only a healthcheck block and traefik labels — no cron, no sidecar, no command, no entrypoint; same for docker-compose.yml, .dev.yml and .staging.yml. NO Cloudflare crons: wrangler.toml has no triggers section and no cron key, and nothing under functions/ exports a scheduled handler. NO CI scheduling: zero references to api/jobs anywhere in .github/workflows. So the sole mechanism really is hand-typed Coolify UI tasks, and the repo has no way to create, apply or verify them. CORRECTION 1: the story says the workflows have three schedule blocks (lighthouse, staging-smoke, uptime). There are FOUR — secret-scan-history.yml also runs on a schedule. Immaterial to the conclusion, but the story should not be quoted as an inventory. CORRECTION 2: the count 73 is stale. CRON_REGISTRY now holds 74 entries — 67 recorded:true and 7 recorded:false — of which 2 are marked oneOff. The number moves whenever a job is added, which is itself an argument for AC2's manifest-and-compare over any figure written into prose. CONFIRMED AND WORTH THE EMPHASIS THE STORY GIVES IT: cron-fleet-health is itself entry number N of the same hand-entered list, so if the operator never created that one Coolify task, nothing in the system alerts about anything — the watcher and the watched share a single point of failure. AC4 CONFIRMED AT THE CODE LEVEL: ops-events.ts reads ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email via getSetting with an empty-string default for both, so an unconfigured prod terminates the entire alert path in an admin screen. WHAT I CANNOT DO FROM HERE, and it is the half the story says to start with: AC3 and AC4 both require PROD state — whether the cron-fleet-health task exists in the Coolify UI, and whether those two system_settings rows are non-empty in production. This host has no prod access. Those two are operator checks, not agent work, and should be split out so the buildable half (AC1/AC2, schedules-as-code or a verified manifest) is not blocked behind them. RELATED, same day: US-2312 made every recorded cron run report body-level failures and populate rows_processed, and US-2318's notes measured that the admin dashboard's 2000-row window covers only ~14.2 hours at the current fleet cadence — so the ledger this story would compare a manifest against is more trustworthy than it was, but the screen reading it still hides daily jobs. | 2026-08-03 AC1 DECIDED and AC2 CLOSED. AC3 and AC4 are prod checks this host cannot make and stay open as the operator half — which is what the 2026-08-02 pass asked for. AC2 WAS MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT, and saying so is the honest half of this. The story asks for 'an artifact in the repo listing every expected schedule, and a job that compares it to what actually ran and alerts on absence'. CRON_REGISTRY is that artifact (74 entries, each with a schedule and an endpoint), lib/cron-fleet-governance.ts is that comparison — its own header calls itself 'the diff between the SCHEDULE (CRON_REGISTRY) and REALITY (cron_runs)' — and US-2004's routes/jobs-cron-fleet.ts is the alert. All three predate this story. SO THE REAL HOLE IS THE ONE THE STORY EMPHASISED and nothing had addressed: cron-fleet-health is itself entry N of the same hand-typed Coolify list. If the operator never created that one task, or deleted it, or typo'd its secret, then nothing in the system alerts about anything — and the silence is indistinguishable from health. The watcher and the watched share one point of failure, which means the alerting is not merely unverified, it is unverifiABLE from inside. AC1 DECIDED, and scoped rather than sweeping: THE SCHEDULES STAY IN COOLIFY, EXCEPT ONE. Moving 74 tasks into a compose sidecar or pg_cron is a migration with its own failure modes, and the diff-against-reality job already covers a missing task ONCE SOMEONE IS WATCHING. What moves to schedules-as-code is exactly the job whose absence is silent by construction. NEW .github/workflows/cron-fleet-watchdog.yml invokes /api/jobs/cron-fleet-health every 6 hours from GitHub-hosted runners — infrastructure that cannot fail the way Coolify does. If the Coolify task exists these ticks are near-no-ops (the job takes a lock); if it does not, the alarm stays connected. TWO DELIBERATE DESIGN CHOICES. It SKIPS, exit 0, when EDGE_JOB_SECRET is unset — a watchdog that cries wolf every six hours because nobody configured it gets muted, and a muted watchdog is worse than none. And it checks the BODY as well as the status, because this endpoint can answer 200 with an error payload and this is the one job where a green-looking check that proves nothing is exactly the failure being fixed. NEW src/tests/cron-fleet-watchdog_test.ts, 6 cases, pinning the two halves agreeing: the workflow is SCHEDULED (a workflow_dispatch-only file would look like coverage and provide none), it calls the endpoint the REGISTRY declares, it sends the header requireJobSecret reads, the unset-secret branch exits 0, the body is inspected, and every registry entry still carries a schedule and an endpoint. TWO WEAKNESSES IN MY OWN GUARD, both found by MUTATION rather than by reading, and both the same family. (1) The endpoint assertion searched the whole file — but the workflow names that endpoint in its header comment and its step name too, so it would have been satisfied by PROSE while the actual request drifted. It matches the curl line now. That is the eighth time a guard here has been confused by a comment. (2) Worse, the fixed version used `includes`, and '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-healthz' CONTAINS '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-health' — so a renamed route still passed. It matches with the closing quote now, so the path has to end where the registry says it ends. A substring check on a path is a prefix check, and prefix checks wave through exactly the rename they exist to catch. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: the schedule removed, the endpoint drifted, the auth header changed, the unset-secret branch made to fail, the body check deleted, and a registry entry stripped of its endpoint. Each reddened on its own case — two of them only after the guard itself was fixed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STORY carried forward from 2026-08-02 and still true: there are FOUR scheduled workflows, not three, and the fleet is 74 entries, not 73 — which is itself the argument for a manifest over a number in prose. REMAINING (operator, both need prod): AC3 — confirm the cron-fleet-health task actually exists in the Coolify UI and that its alerts reach a human. The new watchdog reduces the cost of getting this wrong but does not answer it. AC4 — confirm ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are non-empty in prod system_settings; both default to empty string, in which case the entire alert path terminates in an admin screen nobody is watching, and every alert this story is about would be raised into a void. VERIFIED: deno lint clean across 1334 files, full edge suite 5300 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §11 reports whether ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are configured — PRESENCE and length only, never the value, since a webhook URL is a capability rather than a setting. A MISSING ROW is reported separately from an empty one, because ops-events.ts falls back to "" for both and the two look identical from the code's side. If they are unset, every alert this story is about is raised into a void, including the cron-fleet-stalled one. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §11's second query returned webhook_row_present 1 and email_row_present 1, so both ops_alert settings rows EXIST. STILL MISSING: the first query of §11, which reports whether each row's value is actually non-empty. A present row with an empty value behaves identically to a missing one — ops-events.ts falls back to '' either way — so row presence alone does not answer AC4. That is the one number left on this story.

userStories.title: Weekly north-star email marks users celebrated before it sends, and loses the tail on any throw
userStories.description: routes/jobs-north-star.ts:150-260. The loop has no try/catch and the handler is try/finally with no catch (:65, :273). The north_star_weekly_log insert is at :173-180, the send at :210, and the next run's dedupe reads exactly that table (:90-100) — so a send throw permanently marks the user celebrated and they never get the email. Worse, selection is keyed to weekStartKey (:69) and the cron is weekly, so a throw at user 50 of 1000 means users 51-1000 get no log row and no email, and that week is never recomputed. Their digest and milestone emails are gone, not deferred. Same pattern for milestones at :230-250.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-user try/catch so one failure cannot abort the run.
The log row is written after a successful send, or written as 'attempted' and only marked sent on success.
A failed user is retried on a later run rather than being permanently skipped by the week key.
Test: a throw at user N still delivers users N+1..end.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Email] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-02 EVERY CLAIM VERIFIED against routes/jobs-north-star.ts, and the permanence argument holds. The handler opens try at the top and closes with finally { await lock.release() } and NO catch, so anything thrown inside escapes to Hono. The per-user loop has no try/catch either — its only error branch is the 23505 unique-violation continue on the log insert. The ordering is exactly as described: the north_star_weekly_log insert happens BEFORE coordinateMarketingSend, and the next run's skip set is built by selecting user_id from that same table filtered on week_start = weekStartKey. So a send that throws leaves the user marked celebrated with no email, and a throw at user N leaves users N+1..end with neither a log row NOR an email. The permanence is the part worth being precise about: weekStartKey is derived from now() each run (last Monday), so the following week computes a DIFFERENT key and the failed week is never revisited. Those users' digest and milestone mail is lost, not deferred — the story's wording is accurate. TWO THINGS THE STORY DOES NOT SAY. (1) This job DOES take a job lock (north-star-digest, 600s lease). That matters because US-2311 landed today: release now verifies the holder, so a slow run can no longer delete its successor's lock. Any fix here inherits a lock that actually holds, which was not true this morning. (2) Detection now exists where it did not. Because the handler has no catch, a throw becomes a 500, and US-2312 (also today) records a non-2xx run as an error in cron_runs and raises a job.failed warning. So the failure is no longer silent — but nothing about the DATA LOSS self-heals, and the alert will simply repeat weekly. Do not let the new visibility be mistaken for mitigation. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE for AC2/AC3: the log row currently doubles as both the dedupe key and the celebration record, which is why writing it late is not a free change — a send that succeeds but whose log write fails would then re-send next week. The clean shape is the one AC2 names second: insert as attempted, mark sent on success, and have the skip set select only rows in the sent state, so a crash between the two re-tries rather than either duplicating or losing. AC3's retry then falls out for free, because an attempted row for an old week is still findable once the skip set stops matching on week_start alone. RELATED CLASS: this is the same advance-then-act defect recorded on US-2319 (buyer-digest claims the period before resolving the recipient) and US-2316 (newsletter-ab sends before upserting the ledger). Three jobs, one shape — worth one shared claim/release helper rather than three separate fixes. | 2026-08-02 AC1, AC2 and AC4 DONE. AC3 NOT done and is a PRODUCT DECISION, not remaining engineering — reasoning below so the next person does not just build it. AC1: the per-user body is wrapped. The handler is try/finally with no catch, so before this a throw at user 50 of 1000 escaped to Hono and users 51-1000 got neither a log row nor an email. A thrown user is now counted, reported through captureException with route jobs.north-star.user, and the loop continues. AC2: the north_star_weekly_log insert MOVED to after coordinateMarketingSend. That row is also the next run's skip set, which is what made writing it first so damaging — a send that threw marked the user celebrated with no email. Chose AC2's first option (write after a successful send) over its second (write as attempted, mark sent) because the second needs a status column on north_star_weekly_log, i.e. a migration, and 00512 is already held; the ordering fix removes the data loss without one. THE TRADE, stated rather than buried: writing after the send means a crash BETWEEN send and insert could re-send on a manual same-week re-run. Writing before meant a crash lost the email permanently. A rare duplicate is recoverable and a silently missing email is not, and AC2 sanctions this ordering explicitly. The 23505 branch is preserved so a concurrent run losing the race stays a no-op rather than an error. Also added a `failed` count to the response, which is one of cron-run-outcome.ts's FAILURE_KEYS (US-2312, same day), so a run that loses part of the cohort records as an ERROR instead of reporting a plausible-looking send count. AC4: 5 cases in NEW src/tests/north-star-digest_test.ts — the insert-after-send ORDERING (index comparison, by regex rather than a literal so deno fmt reindentation cannot make it pass by matching nothing on both sides), the per-user wrap, the failed count reaching the response, the 23505 no-op surviving the reorder, and a behavioural model showing a throwing user leaves no celebrated record while the cohort behind them still runs. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: inserting a log write before the send reddens the ordering test. Probe reverted, tree confirmed clean. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5059 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean across 1289 files. WHY AC3 IS A PRODUCT CALL. AC3 asks that a failed user be retried on a later run rather than skipped by the week key. Nothing in the code prevents that; the question is whether it is DESIRABLE. weekStartKey is last Monday, and the email's whole content is that week's activity — items listed, streak, milestone. Retrying next week means mailing someone a celebration of a week that is now two weeks gone, with a streak figure that has since moved. The two honest options are (a) widen the selection to the previous TWO weeks and skip anyone with a log row, accepting stale content, or (b) accept the loss for that week and rely on the now-visible failed count plus job.failed alert to tell an operator it happened. (b) is nearly free and is what today's change already delivers; (a) is a marketing-content decision about whether a late digest is better than none. I did not pick one on the owner's behalf. Note the loss is now BOUNDED where it was not: previously one throw silently lost every user after it, and now it loses only the users who individually threw, and says how many. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-03: any "HELD"/"apply-BEFORE-push" wording earlier in this note describes the state AT THE TIME OF WRITING and is STALE. Prod was measured at applied=00514 on 2026-08-03 via /health/ready (the database's own answer, not a recollection), and every migration up to 00514 is on origin/main. The only migration currently held is 00515 (US-2168), which is unrelated to this story. Do not read this note as evidence that the branch is frozen.

userStories.title: Concurrent token refresh disconnects sellers on providers that rotate refresh tokens
userStories.description: No advisory lock, mutex or single-flight guard exists in any token path (no pg_advisory, no FOR UPDATE, no in-flight promise map). The read-modify-write is check expiry, refresh, persist. Four connectors do this and all four persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, which proves rotation is expected: etsy-client.ts:392-396, whatnot-client.ts:347-350, depop-client.ts, flipdesk-google.ts:353-355. Scenario (Etsy, 1-hour tokens): a user opens the Marketplaces page while the sync cron fires; both see expiresAt - now < 60s (etsy-client.ts:368) and POST the same refresh token; Etsy rotates and invalidates the old one on first use; the second call gets 400 invalid_grant; isPermanentEtsyAuthFailure classifies 400 as PERMANENT (:243) so the handler sets is_active:false and stores a reconnect message (:410-416). The user is force-disconnected by a race, not a revocation. eBay is not exposed (its refresh token is not rotated).
acceptanceCriteria: A per-connection advisory lock (keyed on connection id) around refresh, so concurrent callers wait rather than racing.
invalid_grant immediately after a successful sibling refresh is treated as transient (re-read the row and retry once) rather than permanent.

refreshExpiringEtsyConnections (etsy-client.ts:467) scans on a 24-hour horizon but delegates to getEtsyAccessToken which only refreshes inside a 60-second window, so the cron decrypts every active connection every run and proactively refreshes nothing. Fix or delete it.
Confirm whether Etsy/Depop/Google actually invalidate the old token on rotation — that sets the real severity.
Audit prod for connections deactivated with an invalid_grant refresh_error and offer affected sellers a reconnect.
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Auth] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE for all three affected connectors. AC4 needs a partner answer and AC5 needs prod; both are named below with what to ask. THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT ON THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ON ONE CONNECTOR. Etsy, Whatnot and Depop all do read-expiry → refresh → persist with no coordination, all three persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, and all three classify the loser's failure as PERMANENT — is_active false plus a reconnect message. eBay is genuinely not exposed (no rotation). But there is no flipdesk-google.ts in the repo and nothing under src/lib/google* stores refresh_token_encrypted, so the fourth connector the story names does not exist. Three, not four. AC2 IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIX AND IT WENT IN FIRST, because it makes the race SURVIVABLE rather than rarer. NEW lib/token-refresh-race.ts exports the pure siblingRefreshWon(before, after, now): before deactivating, each connector re-reads its own row, and if a sibling has stored a DIFFERENT and still-valid token then we lost a race rather than the grant — use their token, leave the connection active. It compares ciphertext, which is the right test even though a fresh IV means identical plaintext encrypts differently: the question is 'did this row change', and an unchanged row is byte-identical because nobody rewrote it. AC1 DONE as in-replica single-flight, and the cross-replica advisory lock the AC names was CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. try_acquire_job_lock (00094) would give one with no migration, but job_locks is the cron fleet's table — cron-fleet-governance reads it — and keying it per CONNECTION would put a row per seller per marketplace into a table that exists to describe scheduled jobs. A lock also only makes the race rarer, while AC2 makes it harmless. If duplicate refresh calls later show up as a quota problem, that is what the lock fixes, and it belongs on its own table. Recorded in the module header so the next reader sees a decision rather than an omission. The single-flight entry is deleted in a finally, so a REJECTED refresh is not cached — on these paths a shared rejection would turn one transient provider 503 into a deactivation for everyone waiting behind it. AC3 DONE, FIXED NOT DELETED, and it was worse than 'refreshes nothing': all THREE sweeps (not just Etsy's) select connections expiring within 24 HOURS and then called a getter that only refreshes inside 60 SECONDS. So every run decrypted every active connection and renewed none of them — a cron wearing the costume of a safety net. The getters now take refreshWithinMs (default 60s) and the sweeps pass their own horizon. The single-flight key deliberately IGNORES the threshold: a page load arriving mid-sweep inherits the freshly renewed token, and a sweep landing on a page load's still-valid token simply renews on the next tick. A NEGATIVE TEST THAT PROVED NOTHING, caught and fixed. The 'an unchanged row is not a sibling refresh' case used a 30-second expiry on both sides and stayed GREEN with the unchanged-row guard deleted — the freshness floor rejected it for an unrelated reason. The times are the test: the token now has HOURS left, which is the sweep's world, where refreshWithinMs is the 24-hour horizon and a proactive refresh can fail on a row nowhere near expiry. There the unchanged ciphertext is the ONLY thing between a dead grant and being called a race. NEW src/tests/token-refresh-race_test.ts, 10 cases: six behavioural on the pure helper and the single-flight (including different connections not collapsing, and a rejection not being cached), and four on the wiring — all three connectors wired with eBay's absence ENUMERATED as a decision, the race check running BEFORE the deactivating update by index, and the sweep passing its horizon AND the getter honouring it. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS, each reddening on its own case: the unchanged-row guard removed, the freshness floor removed, the in-flight entry left behind, a connector losing single-flight, a sweep reverting to the 60s window, and the race check physically moved below the deactivating update. REMAINING. AC4: confirm Etsy/Depop/Whatnot actually invalidate the old refresh token on rotation. That sets severity, not correctness — the fix is right either way — so it is a documentation question, not a blocker. AC5: audit prod for connections with is_active=false and a refresh_error matching the reconnect message, and offer those sellers a reconnect. That needs the prod session and is a candidate for scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql on the next pass. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1328 files, full edge suite 5267 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §13 lists connections already deactivated with a refresh_error, split by marketplace and by the distinct error text — the split matters because a genuine revocation must not be mistaken for a lost race and offered a pointless reconnect. No token material is selected; refresh_error is our own message, not the provider's payload. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §13 returned NO ROWS: not one marketplace connection is deactivated with a refresh_error. AC5 ANSWERED — the refresh race never disconnected a seller in production, so there is nobody to offer a reconnect to. The fix shipped before it cost anyone their connection, which is the good version of this outcome. AC4 (do Etsy/Depop/Whatnot actually invalidate the old token on rotation?) still needs a partner answer and is a severity question rather than a correctness one.

userStories.title: Marketplace webhooks have no freshness window and one debug flag disables all four
userStories.description: Verification itself is correct everywhere — all four receivers read the raw body, verify before any DB write, fail closed when the secret is missing, and use constant-time comparison (or asymmetric verify for eBay). Three residual gaps. (A) isDebugAllowed('WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG') is checked at flipdesk-webhooks.ts:123, :201, :493, :1229 and skips the whole verify block when true; lib/env.ts:82-85 returns false in production and edgeEnv() defaults to 'production' when unset, so a bare container fails closed — but any staging or preview with EDGE_ENV non-production and the flag on accepts unsigned requests on the account-deletion path (mass seller disconnect) and logs headers plus 2KB of body verbatim. (B) No replay or freshness check anywhere. All four rely on event-id dedupe which is skipped when the provider's id header is absent (:756, :389, :512) and FAILS OPEN on a DB error (:770, :400, :595, :1290). eBay's notification.publishDate is declared in the type at :744-745 and never read; Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At is never read. (C) fetchPublicKeyMaterial (ebay-notification-verify.ts:135-154) does getAppAccessToken plus a call to eBay's public_key/{kid} for any attacker-supplied kid, with no timeout and no negative cache (keyCache at :92 stores only successes), bounded only by the 600/60s limiter at main.ts:1025 — so an attacker can drive 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica and burn the app's API quota.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod. If it does, this is live.
A timestamp freshness window (+/- 5 min) on the eBay and Shopify receivers using the headers already sent.
Dedupe fails CLOSED on a DB error rather than open.
Negative cache plus a timeout on the eBay public-key fetch.

Depop's header names (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256 at :495-496, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id at :512) are unconfirmed guesses. The signature failure mode is safe (401) but the dedupe failure mode is SILENT — if Depop uses neither header, every delivery is reprocessed with no error. Confirm and narrow, including the hex-or-base64 hedge at depop-api.ts:488-491.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Webhooks] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Secrets at rest are CLEAN: crypto-aes.ts uses a fresh 96-bit IV per encryption, key from env never logged, and v2 binds user_id as GCM additionalData so a ciphertext copied to another tenant fails to decrypt. No plaintext tokens in any log path. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC2 and AC4 DONE. AC3 is PUSHED BACK ON with a reason (see below). AC1 and AC5 need an operator and a partner respectively. AC4 DONE, and it was the real one. fetchPublicKeyMaterial did getAppAccessToken plus a bare `fetch` — no deadline — to eBay's public_key/{kid} endpoint, with `kid` taken from the REQUEST'S OWN signature header, so an unauthenticated caller chose it. Only SUCCESSES were cached, so every request bearing a non-resolving kid produced a fresh token + a fresh outbound call, bounded only by the 600/60s limiter: 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica, burning the app's own quota, on requests that were going to be rejected anyway. Added a NEGATIVE cache (5-min TTL — short, because a kid can legitimately start resolving when eBay publishes a key, and a long negative cache would then reject genuine notifications until the process restarted) and a 5s timeout via fetchWithTimeout. The no-bare-fetch guard's declaration for that file went 1 -> 0, which is how I knew the change actually landed. AC2 DONE: NEW lib/webhook-freshness.ts, applied to the eBay and Shopify receivers using the timestamps both providers ALREADY SEND and neither receiver read — eBay's notification.publishDate (declared in the payload type and never touched) and Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At. A signature proves the provider signed a payload; it does not prove the payload is recent, and a captured delivery stays validly signed forever. TWO ASYMMETRIES, deliberate and both tested. ABSENT timestamp -> ACCEPT: a provider renaming a header or shipping a topic without the field must not become an outage on a path we do not control, and freshness is a SECOND line after the signature. PRESENT but unparseable -> REJECT: that is not an omission, it is a value that does not mean what it claims, which is the shape a forged replay has. The window is symmetric because provider clock skew runs both ways and a one-sided window rejects every delivery from a clock running fast — indistinguishable from an outage. The eBay check sits in the ROUTE, not in processEbayWebhookEvent: that function runs detached from the response, so a rejection there could not produce a status and would be indistinguishable from success to the caller. Both checks run AFTER signature verification so an unsigned request is still reported as unsigned rather than as stale. A TEST OF MINE WAS WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS: I asserted '0000' is unparseable. Date.parse accepts it as year zero, so it is a valid-but-ancient timestamp and is caught by the staleness branch instead. Rejected either way, but via the honest reason — the test now asserts that explicitly rather than being loosened. AC3 — I AM NOT IMPLEMENTING THIS AS WRITTEN, and the reason should be decided rather than inherited. The AC says dedupe should fail CLOSED on a DB error. The current fail-open is not an oversight: US-509 chose it, documented it inline, and made it observable (a webhook.fail_open metric plus a captured exception), on the grounds that the downstream payout/sale ingest is idempotent. Failing closed would DROP a real webhook on a transient database blip — losing a genuine sale — to prevent a double-process that the idempotent ingest already prevents. That trade looks worse, not better. If the owner still wants fail-closed, it needs a durable retry/parking path first, otherwise it converts a benign duplicate into permanent data loss. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod — if it does, the unsigned-request path is live) is an operator check. AC5 (Depop's header names are unconfirmed guesses, and the dedupe failure mode is SILENT) needs Depop's actual documentation. VERIFIED: edge suite 5155/0, deno lint clean across 1308 files.

userStories.title: Add Shopify fulfillment: tracking numbers never reach Shopify
userStories.description: The platform coverage matrix shows Shopify as REAL for connect, list, sync, delist and price revise, but SHELL for ship. There is no fulfillmentCreate call anywhere in the repo. A seller who ships a Shopify order through FlipDesk leaves the Shopify order unfulfilled and the buyer never gets tracking.
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping an order marked as sourced from Shopify calls fulfillmentCreate with the tracking number and carrier.
Failure to fulfil is surfaced to the seller, not swallowed.
Test against the Shopify sandbox.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Shopify] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1 and AC2 DONE. AC3 (sandbox) is operator work and stays open. No migration. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked: there is no fulfillmentCreate anywhere in the repo, and eBay + Depop both have ship routes while Shopify has none. The claim held exactly. A PRECONDITION THE STORY DOES NOT MENTION, and it had to be fixed first or AC1 was impossible: sales.platform_order_id was NEVER POPULATED FOR SHOPIFY. ingestShopifyOrder recorded the money and dropped the only handle back to Shopify, so the ship route would have had nothing to fulfil against. The column has existed since 00032 and eBay has always used it. Now stored. ⚠ Sales ingested BEFORE this change have it null and cannot be fulfilled — the route 409s with `missing_platform_order_id` and tells the seller to re-sync, rather than writing tracking locally and returning ok. Recording it silently would tell the seller their buyer was notified when no Shopify call was ever made, which is the exact failure this story exists to remove, reintroduced for older rows. WHY THIS IS TWO API CALLS: Shopify does not fulfil an ORDER. Since the 2022 fulfillment-orders migration the unit is the FULFILLMENT ORDER — an order split by location and by who is responsible — and fulfillmentCreate takes fulfillment-order ids, never an order id. NEW lib/shopify-fulfillment.ts reads the order's fulfillment orders, then submits EVERY fulfillable one. Submitting only the first would mark a multi-location order part-shipped and silently leave the rest, which reads as complete success on both sides. TWO REFUSALS THAT ARE NOT ERRORS, and one that is: a fulfillment order already CLOSED returns alreadyFulfilled rather than throwing (re-shipping is the common case — a retry, or a seller correcting tracking — and throwing turns a no-op into a red banner). A fulfillment order assigned to a THIRD-PARTY fulfilment service is skipped even though its status is OPEN: submitting for it claims someone else's work is done. But a NULL order throws, because that means the id is wrong or belongs to another shop, and reading it as 'already fulfilled' would swallow a real misconfiguration. AC2 IS THE SUBTLE ONE: fulfillmentCreate answers HTTP 200 with a populated `userErrors` array when it refuses. A handler checking only the transport status tells the seller their buyer has tracking when Shopify said no. assertNoUserErrors throws and carries Shopify's own words plus the field, because the seller is the only one who can fix a bad tracking number. The route returns 502 with that detail. A refusal on the SECOND fulfillment order still fails the whole call — reporting success because something worked would leave half the order unshipped with the seller told otherwise. notifyCustomer defaults TRUE: Shopify emailing the buyer is the entire point. TESTS: 10 cases in NEW shopify-fulfillment_test.ts driving the real function through an injected graphql fake (the codebase's existing deps pattern) — selection, third-party skip, userErrors, every-order submission with the tracking payload asserted, the no-op, a partial refusal, a missing order, an unparseable response, plus two source guards on the order-id storage and the 409. A tenant-isolation case was added for the new route (US-268 rule): it is scoped through inventory_items.user_id like the eBay one, and it gets its own case because a leak here would not merely read A's row — it would FULFIL A's Shopify order under B's request. A REAL WEAKNESS IN MY OWN TEST, found by negative verification: the ordering assertion used indexOf on both markers, and indexOf returns -1 when a marker is GONE — so -1 < anything is true and deleting the refusal code entirely left the case GREEN. Both indices are now checked for presence first, with that reason written next to them. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SEVEN WAYS: only the first fulfillment order submitted, userErrors swallowed, a third-party-held order claimed, a missing order read as fulfilled, the sale losing its order id, the 409 refusal removed, and notifyCustomer defaulting off. Each reddened on its own case. AC3 REMAINS (operator): exercise it against the Shopify sandbox with a real order. Everything decided before and after the network call is pinned here; what cannot be pinned without a shop is that Shopify accepts this exact mutation shape. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5368 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation 17/0, deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1341 files. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-08: the word held above is not a hold. This story has NO migration of its own — the note names 00032 only to say the platform_order_id column has existed since then, and 00032 is long since on origin/main. Nothing here is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on this account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint keys its silence on an explicit correction so a fixed story stops being reported.

userStories.title: The entire authenticated web surface ships with no security headers
userStories.description: functions/_shared/spa-shell.ts:58-67 builds a fresh Response copying only content-type, cache-control and x-robots-tag, and Cloudflare's _headers file does not apply to Pages Functions. Verified live: /login and /dashboard return no CSP, no HSTS, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy. functions/_shared/security-headers.ts already exists with a correct ssrSecurityHeaders() and is only used by blog-render.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: spa-shell.ts applies ssrSecurityHeaders() like blog-render.ts does.
CSP is developed in report-only first, then enforced — the SPA loads Sentry, PostHog and Stripe, so a blind enforce will break it.
A test or synthetic check asserts the headers are present on /login and /dashboard.
Verify after deploy with an actual request, not by reading the code.
userStories.notes: [P1][Web/Security] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Verified live against the deployed site by the auditor. The helper already exists — this is a wiring fix plus CSP tuning. | 2026-08-02 CLAIM VERIFIED — AND AC1 AS WRITTEN WOULD CAUSE AN OUTAGE. Do not implement it literally. THE DEFECT IS REAL: functions/_shared/spa-shell.ts returns a fresh Response whose headers object contains only content-type, cache-control and x-robots-tag. Nothing else. And Cloudflare _headers genuinely does not apply to Pages Function responses — functions/_shared/security-headers.ts says so in its own opening comment, which is why it was written. ssrSecurityHeaders() exists and grep confirms exactly one consumer, blog-render.ts. So the authenticated surface ships bare, as reported. WHY AC1 IS WRONG: ssrSecurityHeaders() was purpose-built for standalone SSR content pages and its header comment states the intent outright — "These pages are standalone (they do NOT mount the SPA), so their CSP is much tighter than the app shell's — only self + GA + fonts/images, no Stripe / PostHog / Sentry / Turnstile." Applying it to the SPA shell breaks the app in three separate ways, and each one is a regression this repo has ALREADY had and documented in public/_headers: (1) its script-src/connect-src omit Stripe, PostHog, Sentry, Turnstile, Cloudflare Insights and the Google Ads origins the SPA loads — checkout, error reporting and analytics all break; (2) it sets Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, while public/_headers deliberately uses same-origin-allow-popups, with a written explanation that bare same-origin severs the window handle so popup.close() silently no-ops and the Google Photos picker and the Stripe/eBay/Google OAuth popups are left open for the user to close by hand; (3) its script-src is nonce-based, but the SPA shell serves a PREBUILT index.html whose one inline head script is allowed by a sha256 hash that scripts/prerender.mjs recomputes at build time — there is no nonce to stamp on a static file, so that script would be blocked and the Consent Mode / font / GA bootstrap would not run. A fourth, smaller one: ssrSecurityHeaders sets no Permissions-Policy, and public/_headers carries camera=(self) precisely because shipping camera=() once made getUserMedia reject in production and silently broke both the grading photo capture and the barcode scanner. THE RIGHT SHAPE: the SPA shell should emit the SAME header set public/_headers already defines for static responses — that set is already tuned, already survived the COOP, camera and inline-hash incidents, and its CSP already lists every origin the SPA needs. So the work is to lift those directives into a shared constant both the static file and spa-shell.ts are generated from (the sha256 is already auto-synced by scripts/prerender.mjs, so the CSP string is machine-written today and can be machine-shared), NOT to reuse the content-page helper. Two header sets exist because two surfaces have genuinely different needs; collapsing them onto the tighter one is the bug. AC2 stays right and is the reason to go report-only first, but note the CSP being rolled out is then the EXISTING enforcing one, so the risk is narrower than the AC implies — it is about the Function-served routes matching what static routes have had all along. AC3/AC4 stay right and AC4 is the important one: this was found live, and it must be confirmed live, because reading spa-shell.ts is exactly what would have said it was fixed. | 2026-08-03 connect-src, for whoever rewrites this policy: https://analytics.google.com (the APEX host) was added to BOTH public/_headers and functions/_shared/security-headers.ts on 2026-08-03. The wildcard https://*.analytics.google.com does NOT match the bare domain, and GA4 posts /g/collect to the bare domain, so every analytics hit on the site was being blocked. Do not drop it. Second, reinforcing the outage warning already on AC1: the connect-src inside ssrSecurityHeaders() is far shorter than the one in _headers, missing api.gradethread.com, functions.gradethread.com, Stripe, Sentry and PostHog, so applying it to the SPA shell unchanged would break the signed-in app. | 2026-08-03 AC1 (correctly, not literally), AC2 FIRST HALF and AC3 DONE. AC2's second half and AC4 need a deploy and are one line plus a browse. AC1 IMPLEMENTED THE WAY THE 2026-08-02 NOTE SAID, NOT THE WAY IT IS WRITTEN. ssrSecurityHeaders() is for standalone content pages that do not mount the SPA and says so in its own header; applying it here breaks the app four ways, each a regression this repo already had. NEW functions/_shared/app-shell-headers.ts emits the SAME set public/_headers defines for static responses — the set that already survived the COOP, camera and inline-hash incidents. THE HASH PROBLEM, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUILD STEP. The shell's inline bootstrap is allowed by a sha256 that scripts/prerender.mjs recomputes into dist/_headers at build time. A constant in the Function would be a SECOND copy that nothing updates — stale the first time the bootstrap changed, and the symptom would be a blocked Consent Mode / GA bootstrap on signed-in routes only. So the Function hashes the HTML IT JUST FETCHED, with extraction mirroring csp-hash.mjs exactly. Self-correcting, no build wiring. PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL BUILD, which is as close to AC4 as is reachable offline: after npm run build, the hash the Function would compute from dist/index.html is byte-identical to the one prerender wrote into dist/_headers. If those two ever disagreed the bootstrap would run on static routes and be blocked on authenticated ones. AC2 FIRST HALF: the CSP ships REPORT-ONLY and every other header is enforced immediately. The reasoning matters — the static surface has enforced this policy for a long time, but only for STATIC responses, so the Function-served authenticated routes have never had it enforced against them at runtime. An origin only the signed-in app uses would break at the worst moment. The other headers cannot break a page that works today and are exactly what the authenticated surface was most exposed by, so they go on now. AC3: NEW src/test/app-shell-headers-parity.test.ts, 8 cases. The central one asserts the shell's CSP is TOKEN-IDENTICAL to public/_headers, both directions, with the sha256 normalised away — because this fix necessarily creates a SECOND copy of one allowlist, and the drift presents in the worst way: a feature works on the marketing pages and breaks once you sign in. The rest pin the four choices already paid for (COOP allow-popups, camera=(self), the missing headers present, report-only) plus the one that would repeat the original bug — that serveSpaShell actually CALLS the helper. A correct helper with one consumer that was not this one is precisely how the surface ended up bare. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: an origin added to _headers only, a directive dropped from the shell copy, COOP reverted to bare same-origin, camera closed to self, the shell no longer applying the headers, and the CSP flipped to enforced without the live check. Each reddened on its own case. CHECKED AND NOT A PROBLEM: /embed/grade/[id] falls back to the shell, and the shell now sends X-Frame-Options: DENY. That is fine and intended — the embed is a SCRIPT WIDGET precisely because the zone already ships DENY plus frame-ancestors 'none'; the shell fallback there is for loading the embed page top-level, which is not framed. A FLAKY GUARD FIXED ON THE WAY PAST. src/test/no-dead-column-writes.test.ts failed on a 5s TIMEOUT in the full run while passing in isolation — each case re-reads the whole scanned corpus, ~2s alone and ~7s under parallel load. That is the worst way for a guard to fail: it looks like a real finding, it does not reproduce, and the next person learns to re-run rather than to read it. Timeout raised to 30s with the reason recorded. TO CLOSE: deploy, then exercise sign-in, Stripe Checkout, the eBay/Google OAuth popups, a grading photo capture and the barcode scanner. AC4 also wants a real request against /login and /dashboard confirming the headers are there, since reading spa-shell.ts is exactly what would have said this was already fixed.
