userStories.title: There is no per-image shadow path at all, so a per-image prompt change can never be compared on live traffic
userStories.description: US-2438 gave the grading user message a per-block versioned seam and wired the golden-set eval to it, so a block candidate can now be SCORED. It still cannot be SHADOWED, and the reason is structural rather than a missing wire: grading-shadow.ts runs at the COMPOSITE stage only, and it reuses the champion's per-image results verbatim rather than re-running them. So there is no code path anywhere that runs two per-image prompts over the same photos and compares them. That matters more than it sounds: a golden set is a few dozen curated garments, while shadow comparison is the only mechanism that sees what a change does to the actual mix of items sellers send. Every per-image change to date — GRADING_TAG_OCR, GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2, and now any block override on garment_type_criteria or category_criteria — has shipped with a golden set and a flag and nothing else. US-2438 AC2 asks for shadow, eval and canary on a block override; eval and canary exist, shadow does not, and building it is its own piece of work.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-image shadow path exists: for a sampled slice of live submissions, the challenger per-image prompt (or block override) runs over the SAME photos as the champion and both results are persisted for comparison. Decide and record whether it re-runs every image or a chosen subset, because the cost is per image per submission and this is the decision that sets the bill.

The shadow run cannot affect the grade the seller receives, and that is test-guarded rather than asserted — the champion's result is what the pipeline consumes, on every path including the one where the shadow call throws or times out.

The comparison records what a reviewer actually needs: per-factor deltas and the tier/score disagreement rate, not just whether the two strings differed. A shadow that reports 'they were not identical' repeats what the surface hash already said.
Cost is bounded and visible before it is enabled: a sampling rate, a per-day ceiling, and the projected spend written down. Grading is a paid call and this doubles it for the sampled slice.

grading-shadow.ts's composite-only limitation is either removed or the note at the top of it says plainly that per-image is covered elsewhere, so the next reader does not conclude shadow means both stages.
US-2438 AC2 is updated to point here rather than staying open on a dependency it cannot satisfy itself.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Lifecycle] Filed 2026-08-08 out of US-2438, whose AC2 asks that a block override go through shadow -> eval -> canary before it serves. Eval and canary landed in US-2438; shadow is the missing leg and it is missing for both blocks AND for the per-image system prompt, which is the larger point. VERIFIED, not assumed: grading-shadow.ts is invoked at the composite stage and takes the already-computed per-image results as input, so it compares two COMPOSITE prompts over identical per-image evidence. Nothing re-runs analyzeImage under a challenger. THE HONEST FRAMING for whoever picks this up: this is not a gap someone forgot to wire, it is a cost decision nobody has taken. Per-image is the expensive stage — one vision call per photo, several photos per submission — so a naive shadow doubles the most expensive part of the product for whatever slice it samples. That is why AC1 asks for the sampling decision to be made and recorded rather than defaulted. Until it exists, a per-image change's evidence is a golden set plus a flag, and the flag is a switch rather than a gate (see vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md, 'What a flag carries, and what it does not'). | 2026-08-08 SCOPED, NOT STARTED — four things established by reading the code, each of which the AC text does not tell you and each of which changes the design. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive them. (1) THE IMAGES ARE GONE BY THE TIME SHADOW RUNS. grading-pipeline.ts holds the base64 data URIs inside withImageBufferSlot (steps 3+4, line ~1465), a process-wide memory gate whose whole purpose is bounding how many submissions buffer multi-MB image data at once; the closure scopes imageData so it is GC-eligible the moment it returns. runShadowGrades is called at step 7, well after. So a per-image shadow has three options and they are not equivalent: pass imageData through to step 7 (defeats the memory gate for every submission, sampled or not), re-download inside the shadow path (costs a storage fetch on the sampled slice only), or decide sampling BEFORE step 4 and run the challenger inside the buffer slot (cheapest, but couples the shadow to the hot path, which AC2 exists to prevent). RE-DOWNLOAD IS THE ONE THAT FITS THE ACs: the cost is negligible beside a vision call per photo, and it keeps the shadow entirely after the seller's grade is delivered. (2) AC1'S SAMPLING QUESTION HAS A FORCED ANSWER, and it is not the cheap one. AC1 offers 'every image or a chosen subset'. A subset cannot work: re-running two of six photos leaves a composite built from a MIX of champion and challenger analyses, which is neither leg, and AC3 needs per-factor deltas — which only exist downstream of a composite. So the challenger leg is ALL images plus one composite call, and the only cost lever left is the SUBMISSION sampling rate. grading-shadow.ts's own header already reached this conclusion and wrote the guidance down: sample at a single-digit percentage of the composite rate. (3) THE TABLE CANNOT TELL THE TWO STAGES APART. grading_shadow_results (00115) has no stage column, so per-image rows would be indistinguishable from composite ones in every existing query and in the admin comparison view. It DOES accommodate a block candidate without change: shadow_prompt_version_id is nullable (checked the DDL, not assumed) and shadow_prompt_version_name is text, so the block:<key>[<scope>]=<version> convention US-2438 established for grading_eval_runs.prompt_version_name transfers directly. A migration is needed for stage plus the per-image sampling columns. (4) NOTHING IS HELD ANY MORE. The previous note's 'HELD MIGRATION: 00563 do NOT push' is stale — PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md records 00563 as APPLIED and MEASURED (health/ready reports expected 00563 / applied 00563 / match), so a new migration here starts from a clean base. NOT STARTED because a partial version of this is the specific failure this story's own area keeps producing: US-2222's AC3 note records bumping PER_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION as something that 'would have looked like compliance and changed nothing', and US-2438's fourth pass explicitly refused to half-ship runEval for the same reason. A shadow path that runs but cannot produce per-factor deltas, or that quietly reuses champion analyses for the images it did not re-run, would report agreement it never measured. | Done 2026-08-09. SHIPPED the per-image shadow path. Migration 00566_per_image_shadow.sql (HELD, see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md): grading_shadow_results gained stage (CHECK per_image|composite, DEFAULT composite so every existing row backfills truthfully), shadow_block_version_id, images_analyzed, vision_calls, per_factor_deltas, tier_agreement; ai_prompt_block_versions gained is_shadow / shadow_sample_rate / shadow_daily_cap, all defaulting to 0 or false. AC1: services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-shadow-per-image.ts runPerImageShadowGrades re-downloads the photos and re-runs EVERY image plus one composite -- the decision is recorded in the file header with the reason a subset cannot work (a partial re-run yields a composite built from a MIX of champion and challenger analyses, which is neither leg), so the only cost lever is the submission sampling rate. AC2: fire-and-forget from grading-pipeline.ts step 7 and the function never throws; guarded by src/tests/grading-shadow-isolation_test.ts (a source guard that the call is 'void ... .catch(' and never awaited, negative-verified by rewriting it to await and watching 2 of 3 cases redden) plus 21 cases in src/tests/grading-shadow-per-image_test.ts driving every failure branch through injected deps. AC3: perFactorDeltas + tiersAgree persist per-factor signed deltas and tier disagreement; summarizeComparisons in grading-shadow.ts now returns tier_disagreement_rate, tier_scored, mean_factor_deltas and vision_calls, and admin-grading.ts /shadow/comparison + /shadow/results select the new columns and accept an optional stage filter. AC4: three independent switches, all off -- PER_IMAGE_SHADOW_DAILY_VISION_CAP (unset = OFF, enforced as a SUM over vision_calls that fails CLOSED when unreadable), shadow_sample_rate and shadow_daily_cap per candidate; projectedVisionCalls() is the exported arithmetic and the projected spend is written down in vault/10-ops/env-reference.md, services/edge-functions/.env.example and the module header (about 84 extra vision calls a day at 400 submissions, 6 photos, one candidate at 3%). AC5: grading-shadow.ts's header now says it is the composite stage only and names grading-shadow-per-image.ts. AC6: US-2438 carries an appended note; vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md's mechanism table and the flag-vs-version table are corrected. Also de-duplicated uint8ToBase64 / mediaTypeForVision / the image download into services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-image-encoding.ts (it was three copies, one held together only by a comment) and rewired grading-pipeline.ts and grading-eval.ts onto it. Two real bugs found and fixed by the new tests: perFactorDeltas used Number()+isFinite, so a factor the challenger omitted arrived as null, coerced to 0 and wrote a -9 delta reading as a total collapse (now a typeof check); and a code comment claiming submission-images rejects HEIC was false (00323 widened it), so the comment now states the real reason the sniff falls through. VERIFIED: deno lint + deno check src/main.ts clean, full edge suite 6163 passed / 0 failed, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, npm run ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3724 passed / 0 failed, npm run vault:lint --strict clean after re-reading and correcting six drifted notes.

userStories.title: Migration 00122 is gitignored and was never committed — the migration sequence has a hole and no fresh environment can reach prod's schema
userStories.description: supabase/migrations/00122_verified_storefront_listings.sql is named explicitly in .gitignore (line 95) and does not exist in the working tree or anywhere in git history (`git log --all -- 'supabase/migrations/00122*'` returns nothing). 00121 and 00123 are both present, so the sequence has a hole at exactly one number. The ignore line was added by 645cd1f3, the same commit that shipped the storefront-listings feature — so whatever DDL that feature needs was applied to prod by hand and then deliberately kept out of the repo. Consequences: the verify:db lane resets a throwaway stack from supabase/migrations/ and therefore proves migrations apply on a fresh schema that is NOT prod's schema; any new environment built from the repo is missing the objects; and EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION (00563) counts a file nobody can read. This is the inverse of the usual drift — normally the repo is ahead of prod.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish what 00122 actually did. The storefront feature is live, so the objects exist in prod: read them out of the running database (information_schema / pg_dump of the relevant tables, policies and functions) rather than reconstructing from the feature commit's application code, which only shows what it EXPECTED.

Decide whether the ignore was protecting something. A migration excluded on purpose usually means it carried a secret, an environment-specific value, or a destructive one-off. If that is the case the answer is a sanitised replacement, not un-ignoring the original — and the reason goes in the file.

Restore a committed migration covering those objects, idempotent per the US-1108 triple (idempotent SQL / EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the SAME commit / self-record footer). It must be safe to apply to a prod that ALREADY has the objects — that is the whole reason it has to be idempotent rather than a plain CREATE.
Remove the .gitignore line, and confirm no other migration is ignored: `git check-ignore supabase/migrations/*.sql` must match nothing.

Add a guard so a migration can never be gitignored again — the sequence-gap and the ignore are each independently checkable, and neither was checked. Fold it into the migrations lint rather than a new one-off script.
userStories.notes: [P1][DB/Drift] Found 2026-08-08 while working US-2437 AC4 (the tracked-and-gitignored guard) — reading .gitignore top to bottom for that check is what surfaced it; nothing was looking for it. EVIDENCE, all measured: .gitignore:95 names the file; `ls supabase/migrations/ | grep 00122` is empty; `git ls-files` is empty; `git log --all --oneline -- 'supabase/migrations/00122*'` is empty (never committed, not deleted later); 00120, 00121, 00123, 00124 all present; `git log -S 00122_verified_storefront_listings -- .gitignore` points at 645cd1f3 'feat(storefront): implement storefront listings feature for verified profiles'. P1 because it silently invalidates a safety net rather than breaking a feature: verify:db and the db-migrations CI lane both exist to prove migrations apply to a FRESH schema, and they have been proving it against a schema that is missing an object prod has. Nobody would notice until a restore, a new environment, or a migration that assumes 00122's objects exist. NOT urgent in the user-facing sense — storefront listings work in prod, which is precisely why this survived. | 2026-08-08 AC4 and AC5 DONE; AC1-AC3 stay open because they need a read of the running database, which no checkout can do. AC4: the .gitignore line naming 00122 is gone, replaced by a comment recording why the hole was invisible; `git check-ignore supabase/migrations/*.sql` now matches nothing. Removing the line does NOT restore the file and the comment says so - it restores the ability to notice. AC5 SHIPPED as scripts/migrations-lint.mjs, wired into BOTH scripts/verify.mjs (web lane) and .github/workflows/ci.yml. Four rules, each of which was independently checkable and none of which was checked: (1) no ignore rule may reach supabase/migrations/ - two halves, because they catch different mistakes: git check-ignore over every entry plus two probe paths, AND a literal read of .gitignore / .git/info/exclude / a nested supabase/migrations/.gitignore. The second half is the one that finds a 00122: a rule written against a filename that does not exist yet matches nothing on disk, so no scan of the directory can ever see it. (2) filename shape NNNNN_snake_case.sql, 5 or 6 digits. (3) no two migrations share a schema_migrations version. (4) sequence gaps against an annotated KNOWN_GAPS map that may only shrink. NOT IN db-migrations.yml, deliberately: that workflow is path-filtered to supabase/migrations/**, and the change that lost 00122 was a .gitignore edit, which would not have triggered it. Same reason it is in the web lane rather than the Docker-gated db lane - the bug is invisible to a check that applies the files present. THE SEQUENCE HAS FIVE GAPS, NOT ONE, and measuring them is what made the baseline usable: 00011, 00014 and 00479 were never authored (no file in any commit), 00527 is 00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED where the suffix IS the safety mechanism (US-2403), and 00122 is this story. A bare list of numbers would have been unshrinkable, so every entry carries its reason and a test asserts each reason is non-trivial. TWO THINGS I EXPECTED TO BE BUGS AND WERE NOT, checked rather than assumed. The three 6-digit filenames (000355_photo_types_v2, 000375_push_device_tokens, 000385_feedback_messages) look like a numbering error and are the opposite: commit e4a44545 split three duplicate-prefix pairs, and 000355 sorts lexically between 00035 and 00036, so apply order is preserved exactly. They are pinned in SIX_DIGIT_BY_DESIGN and a NEW 6-digit name now fails, because it would mean the collision recurred - that collision broke `supabase db start` outright with a duplicate-key error naming a Postgres constraint rather than a file, which is why rule 3 exists at all. ONE REAL SUBTLETY: git check-ignore reports NOTHING for a tracked path by default, so an ignore rule added over the existing migrations read as clean until --no-index went in. Found by negative verification, not by review. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SEVEN WAYS end to end: an ignore rule over an existing migration, an ignore rule matching only future files, a malformed filename, a duplicate version, a new gap, a stale KNOWN_GAPS entry, and a missing pinned 6-digit file - each reddened its own case and was restored. 17 cases in NEW scripts/migrations-lint.test.mjs, all against SYNTHETIC directories rather than the real one: a test asserting 'the repo passes today' goes green forever the moment the repo is clean and never proves the rules would fire. Six source mutations confirm that (SHAPE widened, nested-ignore handling dropped, the unexplained filter stubbed, the filled filter stubbed, duplicate detection stubbed, the pinned-but-absent push removed) - each reddened, module restored. STILL OPEN AND ALL OWNER WORK: AC1 (read 00122's objects out of prod via information_schema/pg_dump, not reconstructed from 645cd1f3's application code, which shows what it EXPECTED), AC2 (decide whether the ignore was protecting a secret or an environment-specific value, in which case the answer is a sanitised replacement), AC3 (commit an idempotent migration safe to apply to a prod that already has the objects, per the US-1108 triple). VERIFIED: migrations-lint green (561 migrations, 5 annotated gaps), test:scripts 355 passed / 0 failed across 16 files, check-tracked-ignored green, eslint 0 errors, prd-lint OK.
